examples: curl_in(list(0, r, 0), cylindrical, list(r, t, z))

operators.name: cycle_type
operators.doc:
`cycle_type(perm)`: sorted list of disjoint cycle lengths of permutation `perm`.

The cycle type: the sorted cycle lengths, fixed points included.

# Panics
Panics if an image is outside the permutation's degree.

operators.name: cyclic_group
operators.doc: Constructs the cyclic group `Z_n` of order `n` on elements `0..n-1` under addition modulo `n`.

operators.name: dare
signatures: (Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>) -> Tensor<2, Real>
operators.doc:
`dare(a, b, q, r)`: the stabilising solution `P` of the discrete algebraic Riccati equation.

Solves the discrete algebraic Riccati equation
`P = A^T P A - A^T P B (R + B^T P B)^{-1} B^T P A + Q`.

Uses monotone value iteration from `P = Q` with a `1e-12` stopping
tolerance and an iteration cap of 10 000.

# Errors
Returns an error for inconsistent dimensions or a singular `R + B^T P B`.

operators.name: dawson_complex
operators.doc:
`dawson_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of Dawson integral `D+(z)`.

Complex Dawson integral `D+(z) = exp(-z^2) * int_0^z exp(t^2) dt`.

operators.name: debye_frequency
operators.doc: `debye_frequency(v, n)`: Debye cutoff frequency `v (6 pi^2 n)^(1/3)` for sound speed `v` and atomic density `n`.

operators.name: debye_heat_capacity
operators.doc: `debye_heat_capacity(N, TD, T)`: Debye model heat capacity at temperature `T` with Debye temperature `TD`.

operators.name: dedekind_eta_complex
operators.doc:
`dedekind_eta_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `eta(tau)`.

Dedekind eta function `eta(tau)` on the upper half-plane `Im(tau) > 0`
using modular reduction to the fundamental domain and Euler's pentagonal theorem.

operators.name: definite_sum
operators.doc:
`definite_sum(F, k, n)` seeks a closed form in `n` for the sum of `F(n, k)` over all integer `k`.

The names `k` and `n` are symbols. Creative telescoping obtains a recurrence and the solver checks its proposed closed form against direct values where the support is known.

For example, `definite_sum(binomial(n, k), k, n)` returns `2^n`. The request remains unevaluated when the solver cannot establish a closed form.

operators.name: defint
operators.doc: `defint(f, x, a, b)`: definite integral of `f` with respect to bound variable `x` from `a` to `b`.

operators.name: degree
operators.doc:
`degree(poly, var)`: returns the polynomial degree of `poly` in `var`.

Degree, or `None` for the zero polynomial.

operators.name: deinterleave
operators.doc:
Reverses block interleaving of depth `depth` on byte list `data`.

De-interleaves data (reverses the interleave operation).

# Arguments
* `data` - The interleaved data.
* `depth` - The interleaving depth used during interleaving.

# Returns
The de-interleaved data.

operators.name: delaunay_2d
operators.doc:
`delaunay_2d(points)`: the counter-clockwise Delaunay triangulation of a list of `list(x, y)` points, as `list(i, j, k)` index triples.

Delaunay triangulation of `points` by Bowyer–Watson insertion.

Returns counter-clockwise triangles as triples of indices into `points`.

# Errors

Returns `Err` when fewer than three points are supplied, when a coordinate
is not finite, or when two points coincide.

operators.name: delaunay_3d
operators.doc:
`delaunay_3d(points)`: the Delaunay tetrahedralisation of a list of `list(x, y, z)` points, as `list(i, j, k, l)` index quadruples.

Delaunay tetrahedralisation of `points`.

Returns positively oriented tetrahedra as quadruples of indices into
`points`.

# Errors

Returns `Err` when fewer than four points are supplied, when a coordinate is
not finite, or when two points coincide.

operators.name: denest_sqrt
operators.doc: `denest_sqrt(expr)`: denests nested square roots in `expr` (e.g. `sqrt(a + b*sqrt(c))`) into simpler radical sums when possible.

operators.name: density_of_states_3d
operators.doc: `density_of_states_3d(E, m, V)`: 3D free-electron density of states at energy `E`, mass `m`, and volume `V`.

operators.name: derangements
operators.doc: `derangements(n)`: subfactorial `!n`, counting permutations of `n` elements with no fixed points.

operators.name: det
operators.doc: `det(A)`: determinant of square matrix `A`.

operators.name: diag
operators.doc: `diag(v_or_A)`: build a diagonal matrix from vector `v`, or extract the main diagonal of matrix `A`.

operators.name: diff
operators.doc:
`diff(f, x)`: symbolic derivative of `f` with respect to `x`.

The derivative of `f` with respect to the symbol `x`, as an unevaluated
request.

operators.name: difference
operators.doc:
`difference(x, d)`: the `d`-fold first difference of `x`.

`d`-fold first difference.

Each pass replaces `x` by `x[t+1] - x[t]`, so the result is `d` entries
shorter than the input (and empty once the series is exhausted).

operators.name: diffn
operators.doc: `diffn(f, x, n)`: `n`-th order symbolic derivative of `f` with respect to `x` for non-negative integer `n`.

operators.name: digamma
operators.doc: `digamma(z)`: logarithmic derivative `psi(z) = Gamma'(z) / Gamma(z)`.

operators.name: digamma_complex
operators.doc:
`digamma_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of the complex digamma function `psi(z) = Gamma'(z) / Gamma(z)`.

The digamma function `ψ(z) = Γ'(z) / Γ(z)`; poles give NaN.

operators.name: digraph
operators.doc: Directed graph constructor `digraph(n, edges[, hyperedges])` with vertices `0..n-1`, edge list `list(list(u, v[, w]), ...)`, and optional hyperedges.

operators.name: dihedral_group
operators.doc: Constructs the dihedral group `D_n` of order `2*n` with rotations `r0..r(n-1)` and reflections `s0..s(n-1)`.

operators.name: dim_irrep
operators.doc: `dim_irrep(T, hw)`: dimension of the irreducible representation of type `T` with highest weight `hw` (Dynkin labels).

operators.name: dimension
operators.doc: `dimension(qty)`: returns the physical dimension of quantity `qty`.

operators.name: dims
operators.doc: `dims(A)`: dimensions `list(rows, cols)` of matrix `A`.

operators.name: diophantine
operators.doc: `diophantine(eq, vars)`: integer solutions to Diophantine equation `eq` in variables `vars`.

operators.name: dirac
operators.doc: `dirac(x)`: Dirac delta distribution centered at `x = 0`.

operators.name: dirac_adjoint
operators.doc: `dirac_adjoint(psi)`: Dirac adjoint `psi^dagger gamma^0` of a four-component spinor `psi`.

operators.name: dirac_equation
signatures: (Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Symbol>) -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: `dirac_equation(psi, m, x)`: residual `(i gamma^mu partial_mu - m) psi` of the free Dirac equation in natural units.

operators.name: dirac_gamma
operators.doc: `dirac_gamma(mu)`: 4x4 Dirac gamma matrix in the Dirac representation (`mu = 0..3`, or `5` for `gamma^5`).

operators.name: directional
operators.doc: `directional(f, vars, v)`: directional derivative `(grad f) . v` along vector `v`.

operators.name: dirichlet_eta_complex
operators.doc:
`dirichlet_eta_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `eta(s)`.

Complex Dirichlet eta function `eta(s) = sum_{n>=1} (-1)^(n-1) / n^s`
using Borwein's accelerated alternating sum for small `|Im(s)|` and
`(1 - 2^(1-s)) * zeta(s)` elsewhere.

operators.name: discrete_convolution
operators.doc: `discrete_convolution(f, g, n)`: discrete convolution sum `sum_k f(k) * g(n - k)`.

operators.name: discriminant
operators.doc:
`discriminant(poly, var)` computes the discriminant of a positive-degree polynomial in `var`.

Coefficients may be exact rationals or expressions independent of `var`.

The discriminant is one for a linear polynomial and zero when the polynomial has a repeated root.

operators.name: distance
operators.doc: `distance(a, b)`: Euclidean distance `abs(a - b)` between complex points `a` and `b`.

operators.name: div
operators.doc: `div(F, vars)`: divergence `sum_i dF_i/dx_i` of vector field `F`.

operators.name: div_in
operators.doc: `div_in(F, sys, vars)`: divergence of physical-component vector `F` in orthogonal coordinate system `sys(vars)`.

operators.name: divide
operators.doc:
`divide(a, b)`: the quotient `a / b`.

Rewritten to `mul(a, pow(b, -1))` and printed as `a/b`. The name is `divide` because `div` is the divergence of a vector field.

operators.name: divisor_count
operators.doc:
`divisor_count(n)`: number of positive divisors `tau(n)` of positive integer `n`.

Returns the number of positive divisors `\tau(n) = \sigma_0(n)` (`divisor_count(0) = 0`).

operators.name: divisor_sum
operators.doc: `divisor_sum(n)`: sum of positive divisors `sigma_1(n)` of positive integer `n`.

operators.name: divisors
operators.doc:
`divisors(n)`: sorted list of all positive divisors of `n`.

Returns all positive divisors of `n` in ascending order (`divisors(0)` is empty).

operators.name: dlog
operators.doc: `dlog(g, h, n)`: discrete logarithm `k` satisfying `g^k = h (mod n)`.

operators.name: dlqr
signatures: (Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>) -> { gain: Tensor<2, Real>, riccati: Tensor<2, Real> }
operators.doc:
`dlqr(a, b, q, r)`: `list(K, P)`, the discrete linear-quadratic gain and the Riccati solution.

Discrete linear-quadratic regulator: returns `(K, P)` with
`K = (R + B^T P B)^{-1} B^T P A`.

# Errors
As [`dare`].

operators.name: dnf
operators.doc: `dnf(formula)`: converts propositional `formula` to disjunctive normal form.

operators.name: doppler_effect
operators.doc: `doppler_effect(f, v)`: longitudinal relativistic Doppler-shifted frequency for receding velocity `v`.

operators.name: dot
operators.doc:
`dot(u, v)`: Euclidean dot product `sum_i u_i v_i` of vectors `u` and `v`.

Dimension-generic dot product: dispatches on the vector type.

operators.name: double_factorial
operators.doc:
`double_factorial(n)`: double factorial `n!! = n * (n - 2) * ...`.

Computes the double factorial n!!
n!! = n * (n-2) * (n-4) * ... * (1 or 2)

operators.name: drude_conductivity
operators.doc: `drude_conductivity(n, e, tau, m)`: Drude electrical conductivity `n e^2 tau / m`.

operators.name: dsolve
signatures: () -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>> with 0... x Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: `dsolve(eq_or_system, func_or_vars, [ics...])`: symbolically solves an ordinary differential equation or system of ODEs for `func_or_vars`, optionally subject to initial/boundary conditions.
examples: dsolve(list(diff(x(t), t) = y(t), diff(y(t), t) = -x(t)), list(x(t), y(t)))

operators.name: dwt2
operators.doc:
`dwt2(matrix, wavelet)`: single-level 2D separable discrete wavelet transform returning `list(LL, LH, HL, HH)`. The first letter gives the row-wise filter and the second gives the column-wise filter.

One level of the separable two-dimensional transform, `x` row-major with `rows x cols` entries.

The rows are transformed first, then the columns, and the four sub-bands are packed into a
`(2*ra) x (2*ca)` row-major array with `ra = w.coeff_len(rows, b)` and
`ca = w.coeff_len(cols, b)`: `LL` at rows `0..ra`, columns `0..ca`; `LH` at rows `0..ra`,
columns `ca..2ca`; `HL` at rows `ra..2ra`, columns `0..ca`; `HH` at rows `ra..2ra`, columns
`ca..2ca`. In each label, the first letter gives the filter within each row (horizontal)
and the second the filter within each column (vertical).

# Errors
[`WaveletError::Shape`] when `rows * cols` does not match `x.len()`, or when a row or column
transform fails.

operators.name: dwt_approx
operators.doc: `dwt_approx(x, wavelet)`: single-level discrete wavelet approximation coefficients of `x`.

operators.name: dwt_detail
operators.doc: `dwt_detail(x, wavelet)`: single-level discrete wavelet detail coefficients of `x`.

operators.name: dynkin_index
operators.doc: `dynkin_index(T, hw)`: Dynkin index `dim(V) * C(V) / dim(g)` of irrep `V(hw)` of type `T`.

operators.name: ec_add
operators.doc: Computes the elliptic curve point sum `P + Q` on curve `C`.

operators.name: ec_compress
operators.doc: Compresses an affine point `list(x, y)` to `list(x, odd)` where `odd` is `0` or `1` indicating the parity of `y`.

operators.name: ec_curve
operators.doc: Constructs an elliptic curve `list(a, b, p)` for `y^2 = x^3 + a*x + b (mod p)` with `a` and `b` reduced modulo odd prime `p`.

operators.name: ec_decompress
operators.doc: Decompresses `(C, x, odd)` to the affine point `list(x, y)` on curve `C` using Tonelli-Shanks modular square root.

operators.name: ec_double
operators.doc: Computes `2*P` on elliptic curve `C`.

operators.name: ec_is_infinity
operators.doc: Returns `true` if elliptic curve point `P` is the point at infinity `list()`.

operators.name: ec_mul
operators.doc: Computes scalar multiplication `k*P` on elliptic curve `C` for integer `k` (which may be negative).

operators.name: ec_neg
operators.doc: Returns the additive inverse `-P` of point `P` on elliptic curve `C`.

operators.name: ec_on_curve
operators.doc: Returns `true` if point `P` lies on elliptic curve `C` (including the point at infinity `list()`).

operators.name: ec_order
operators.doc: Computes the order of point `P` on elliptic curve `C` by repeated addition (up to 10^6 steps).

operators.name: ec_x
operators.doc: Returns the x-coordinate of an affine elliptic curve point `list(x, y)`.

operators.name: ec_y
operators.doc: Returns the y-coordinate of an affine elliptic curve point `list(x, y)`.

operators.name: ecdf
operators.doc:
`ecdf(sample, x)`: empirical cumulative distribution function of `sample` evaluated at `x`.

Empirical CDF of `data` at `x`.

operators.name: ecdh_public
operators.doc: Computes an ECDH public key `d*G` on curve `C` from generator `G` and private scalar `d`.

operators.name: ecdh_shared
operators.doc: Computes the ECDH shared secret point `d*Q` on curve `C` from private scalar `d` and peer public point `Q`.

operators.name: ecdsa_sign
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc: Computes an ECDSA signature `list(r, s)` for `(C, G, n, d, h, k)` with generator `G` of order `n`, private key `d`, message hash `h`, and explicit nonce `k`.

operators.name: ecdsa_verify
signatures: (Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int, Tensor<1, Int>, Int, Tensor<1, Int>) -> Bool
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc: Verifies an ECDSA signature `list(r, s)` for `(C, G, n, Q, h, sig)` against public key `Q` and message hash `h`, returning a boolean.

operators.name: effective_sample_size
operators.doc:
`effective_sample_size(chain)`: the effective number of independent draws in `chain`, from the initial positive sequence of its autocorrelations.

Effective sample size by the initial positive sequence estimator.

The autocorrelations are summed in adjacent pairs and the sum is truncated
at the first non-positive pair, which keeps the estimate from being dragged
down by the noise of the tail. Lags are computed only until that truncation,
so a well-mixing chain costs two passes over the data. Returns the number of
independent draws with the same information content as the chain.

# Errors
Returns an error for fewer than four draws or a constant chain.

operators.name: egcd
operators.doc: `egcd(x, y)`: extended Euclidean algorithm returning `list(g, s, t)` with `g = s*x + t*y = gcd(x, y)`.

operators.name: ei
operators.doc: `ei(x)`: exponential integral `Ei(x) = -PV int_{-x}^infty exp(-t)/t dt`.

operators.name: eigenvals
operators.doc: `eigenvals(A)`: eigenvalues of square matrix `A`.

operators.name: eigenvects
signatures: (Tensor<2, Int>) -> Tensor<1, { _0: Dyn<term>, _1: Int, _2: Tensor<2, Dyn<term>> }>
operators.doc: `eigenvects(A)`: eigenvalues and eigenvectors of square matrix `A`.

operators.name: einstein
operators.doc: `einstein(g, vars)`: Einstein tensor `G = Ric - (R / 2) * g` for metric `g` in `vars`.

operators.name: einstein_field_equations
operators.doc: `einstein_field_equations(Ric, R, g, T)`: residual `G - (8 pi G_N / c_0^4) T` of the Einstein field equations.

operators.name: einstein_heat_capacity
operators.doc: `einstein_heat_capacity(N, TE, T)`: Einstein model heat capacity at temperature `T` with Einstein temperature `TE`.

operators.name: einstein_tensor_from
signatures: (Tensor<2, Int>, Int, Tensor<2, Int>) -> Tensor<2, Real>
(Tensor<2, Dyn<term>>, Dyn<term>, Tensor<2, Dyn<term>>) -> Tensor<2, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: `einstein_tensor_from(Ric, R, g)`: Einstein tensor `G = Ric - (1/2) R g` from Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, and metric.
examples: einstein_tensor_from(ricci(list(list(a^2, 0), list(0, a^2*sin(theta)^2)), list(theta, phi)), ricci_scalar(list(list(a^2, 0), list(0, a^2*sin(theta)^2)), list(theta, phi)), list(list(a^2, 0), list(0, a^2*sin(theta)^2)))

operators.name: eisenstein_e4_complex
operators.doc:
`eisenstein_e4_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `E_4(tau)`.

Normalized Eisenstein series `E_4(tau) = 1 + 240 * sum_{n>=1} n^3 q^n / (1 - q^n)`
with `q = exp(2*pi*i*tau)` for `Im(tau) > 0`.

operators.name: eisenstein_e6_complex
operators.doc:
`eisenstein_e6_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `E_6(tau)`.

Normalized Eisenstein series `E_6(tau) = 1 - 504 * sum_{n>=1} n^5 q^n / (1 - q^n)`
with `q = exp(2*pi*i*tau)` for `Im(tau) > 0`.

operators.name: electric_field_from_potential
operators.doc: `electric_field_from_potential(V, vars)`: electrostatic field `-grad V` from scalar potential `V`.

operators.name: electric_field_from_potentials
signatures: (Int, Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Tensor<1, Symbol>, Dyn<term>) -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
(Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Tensor<1, Symbol>, Dyn<term>) -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: `electric_field_from_potentials(V, A, vars, t)`: electric field `-(grad V + dA/dt)` from scalar potential `V` and vector potential `A`.
examples: electric_field_from_potentials(0, list(-E0*t, 0, 0), list(x, y, z), t)
electric_field_from_potentials(-E0*x, list(-E0*t, 0, 0), list(x, y, z), t)

operators.name: elliptic_e_complex
operators.doc:
`elliptic_e_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `E(m)`.

Complete elliptic integral of the second kind `E(m)` for complex parameter `m`.

operators.name: elliptic_e_inc_complex
operators.doc:
`elliptic_e_inc_complex(pr, pi, mr, mi)`: `list(re, im)` of `E(phi | m)`.

Incomplete elliptic integral of the second kind `E(phi | m)`.

operators.name: elliptic_f_complex
operators.doc:
`elliptic_f_complex(pr, pi, mr, mi)`: `list(re, im)` of `F(phi | m)`.

Incomplete elliptic integral of the first kind `F(phi | m)`.

operators.name: elliptic_k_complex
operators.doc:
`elliptic_k_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `K(m)`.

Complete elliptic integral of the first kind `K(m)` for complex parameter `m`.

operators.name: elliptic_pi_complex
signatures: (Real, Real, Real, Real, Real, Real) -> Tensor<1, Real>
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
`elliptic_pi_complex(nr, ni, pr, pi, mr, mi)`: `list(re, im)` of `Pi(n; phi | m)`.

Incomplete elliptic integral of the third kind `Pi(n; phi | m)`.

operators.name: em_energy_density
operators.doc: `em_energy_density(E, B)`: electromagnetic energy density `(epsilon_0 |E|^2 + |B|^2 / mu_0) / 2`.

operators.name: energy_band
operators.doc: `energy_band(k, m, E0)`: parabolic band dispersion `E0 + hbar^2 k^2 / (2 m)`.

operators.name: energy_eigenvalue
operators.doc: `energy_eigenvalue(H, psi, x)`: energy eigenvalue `E` satisfying `H psi = E psi` in variable `x`.

operators.name: entails
operators.doc: `entails(premise, conclusion)`: decides whether `premise` semantically entails `conclusion` (`true` or `false`).

operators.name: enthalpy
operators.doc: `enthalpy(U, P, V)`: enthalpy `H = U + P V`.

operators.name: entropy
operators.doc: `entropy(ps)`: Shannon entropy (in nats) `-sum p_i ln(p_i)` of probability list `ps`.

operators.name: entropy_bits
operators.doc: `entropy_bits(ps)`: Shannon entropy (in bits) `-sum p_i log2(p_i)` of probability list `ps`.

operators.name: entropy_from_helmholtz
operators.doc: `entropy_from_helmholtz(A, T)`: thermodynamic entropy `-dA/dT` from Helmholtz free energy `A`.

operators.name: entropy_of
operators.doc: `entropy_of(d)`: differential or discrete information entropy of distribution `d`.

operators.name: epsilon_0
operators.doc: `epsilon_0`: vacuum electric permittivity in F/m.

operators.name: eq
operators.doc: The equation `lhs = rhs`, as a term.

operators.name: equivalent
operators.doc: `equivalent(f, g)`: decides whether propositional formulas `f` and `g` are logically equivalent (`true` or `false`).

operators.name: erf
operators.doc: `erf(x)`: Gauss error function `(2 / sqrt(pi)) * int_0^x exp(-t^2) dt`.

operators.name: erf_complex
operators.doc:
`erf_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of the complex error function `erf(re + i*im)`.

Error function of a complex argument.

Maclaurin series for `|z| < 1.5`, otherwise `1 - exp(-z²) w(i z)` after
folding to `Re z >= 0` with `erf(-z) = -erf(z)`. The exponential is
scaled with the Faddeeva factor near the floating-point range limits.

operators.name: erfc
operators.doc: `erfc(x)`: complementary error function `1 - erf(x)`.

operators.name: erfc_complex
operators.doc:
`erfc_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `erfc(z)`.

Complex complementary error function `erfc(z) = 1 - erf(z)`.

operators.name: erfcinv
operators.doc: `erfcinv(y)`: inverse complementary error function solving `erfc(x) = y`.

operators.name: erfcx_complex
operators.doc:
`erfcx_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `exp(z^2) * erfc(z)`.

Scaled complementary error function `erfcx(z) = exp(z^2) * erfc(z) = w(i*z)`.

operators.name: erfi
operators.doc:
`erfi(x)`: imaginary error function `-i * erf(i * x)`.

The imaginary error function `erfi(x) = -i erf(ix) = (2/√π) ∫_0^x e^{t²}
dt`, from its everywhere-convergent power series (all terms of one
sign, so no cancellation).

operators.name: erfi_complex
operators.doc:
`erfi_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `erfi(z)`.

Imaginary error function `erfi(z) = -i * erf(i * z)`.

operators.name: euclidean_distance
operators.doc:
Computes the Euclidean distance between two coordinate lists `p` and `q`.

The Euclidean distance between two points.

operators.name: euler_gamma
operators.doc: `euler_gamma`: Euler-Mascheroni constant `gamma = lim_{n->infty} (H_n - ln n) ≈ 0.5772156649`.

operators.name: euler_lagrange
operators.doc: `euler_lagrange(L, y, x)`: computes the Euler-Lagrange residual expression `d/dx(dL/dy') - dL/dy` (with higher-order jet terms when present) for Lagrangian `L` and dependent variable(s) `y` of `x`.
examples: euler_lagrange(1/2*diff(x(t), t)^2 - x(t)*y(t) + 1/2*diff(y(t), t)^2, list(x(t), y(t)), t)

operators.name: euler_lagrange_equation
operators.doc: `euler_lagrange_equation(L, q, t)`: Euler-Lagrange residual `d/dt(dL/dq_dot) - dL/dq` for generalized coordinate `q(t)`.

operators.name: euler_number
operators.doc: `euler_number(n)`: `n`-th Euler number `E_n` (0 for odd `n`).

operators.name: eulerian
operators.doc: `eulerian(n, k)`: Eulerian number `A(n, k)`, counting permutations of `n` elements with `k` ascents.

operators.name: exists
operators.doc: `exists(var_or_list, formula)`: existentially quantifies Boolean variable(s) out of `formula`.

operators.name: exp
operators.doc:
`exp(x)`: natural exponential function `e^x`.

`exp(x)` as a ball.

# Errors
Fails when an exponent leaves the representable range.

operators.name: exp_integral_e1_complex
operators.doc:
`exp_integral_e1_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `E_1(z)`.

Complex exponential integral `E_1(z) = int_z^oo exp(-t)/t dt`, cut along `(-inf, 0]`.

operators.name: exp_integral_ei_complex
operators.doc:
`exp_integral_ei_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `Ei(z)`.

Complex exponential integral `Ei(z) = -E_1(-z) + i * pi * sign` (principal branch).

operators.name: exp_map
signatures: () -> Tensor<2, Dyn<term>> with 0... x Tensor<2, Int>
() -> Tensor<2, Int> with 0... x Tensor<2, Real>
() -> Tensor<2, Dyn<term>> with 0... x Tensor<2, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: `exp_map(A)` or `exp_map(A, n)`: matrix exponential `exp(A)` in closed form, or truncated Taylor polynomial `sum_{k<=n} A^k / k!`.

operators.name: expand
operators.doc: `expand(expr)`: expands products and integer powers in `expr` into a sum of terms.

operators.name: expand_binomial
operators.doc: `expand_binomial(a, b, n)`: expands `(a + b)^n` via the binomial theorem `sum_{j=0}^n C(n, j) a^{n-j} b^j`.

operators.name: expand_trig

operators.name: expect_of
operators.doc: `expect_of(d, x, expr)`: expected value `E[expr(x)]` under random variable `x ~ d`.

operators.name: expectation

operators.name: expectation_value
operators.doc: `expectation_value(A, psi, x)`: normalized expectation value `<psi|A|psi> / <psi|psi>`.

operators.name: exponential
operators.doc: `exponential(rate)`: exponential distribution with rate parameter `rate`.

operators.name: exterior_d
operators.doc: `exterior_d(omega, vars)`: exterior derivative `d omega` of differential form `omega` in variables `vars`.

operators.name: f_dist
operators.doc: `f_dist(d1, d2)`: Fisher-Snedecor F-distribution with degrees of freedom `d1` and `d2`.

operators.name: factor
operators.doc: `factor(expr)`: factors a polynomial or rational expression into irreducible factors over the rationals.

operators.name: factor_mod
operators.doc: Factors a polynomial expression `f` in variable `x` modulo prime `p` into a product `lc * g1^m1 * ...` with coefficients in `[0, p)`.

operators.name: factorial
operators.doc:
`factorial(n)`: factorial `n! = 1 * 2 * ... * n` for non-negative integer `n`.

Computes the factorial of `n` (`n!`) as an `f64`.

# Arguments
* `n` - The non-negative integer for which to compute the factorial.

# Returns
The factorial of `n` as an `f64`. Returns `f64::INFINITY` if `n` is too large to fit in `f64`.

operators.name: factorint
operators.doc: `factorint(n)`: prime factorization of `n` as `list(list(p, e), ...)`.

operators.name: faddeeva_w_complex
operators.doc:
`faddeeva_w_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of Faddeeva function `w(z)`.

Faddeeva / Voigt plasma dispersion function `w(z) = exp(-z^2) * erfc(-i * z)`.

operators.name: falling
operators.doc: `falling(x, k)`: falling factorial `x * (x - 1) * ... * (x - k + 1)`.

operators.name: false
operators.doc: `false`: Boolean falsity constant.

operators.name: farey
operators.doc: `farey(n)`: Farey sequence `F_n` of reduced fractions in `[0, 1]` with denominator `<= n`, as `list(list(p, q), ...)`.

operators.name: fermi_dirac_distribution
operators.doc: `fermi_dirac_distribution(E, mu, T)`: Fermi-Dirac mean occupation number at energy `E`, chemical potential `mu`, temperature `T`.

operators.name: fermi_energy_3d

operators.name: fermi_wavevector_3d

operators.name: fermion_propagator
operators.doc: `fermion_propagator(p, m)`: momentum-space Dirac fermion propagator `i (p_slash + m) / (p^2 - m^2)`.

operators.name: feynman_propagator_position_space
operators.doc: `feynman_propagator_position_space(x, y, m)`: 1D Fourier transform of the scalar Feynman propagator from `x` to `y`.

operators.name: feynman_slash

operators.name: fft_abs

operators.name: fft_im
operators.doc: `fft_im(x)`: imaginary part of the discrete Fourier transform of real sequence `x`.

operators.name: fft_re
operators.doc: `fft_re(x)`: real part of the discrete Fourier transform of real sequence `x`.

operators.name: fftconv
operators.doc: `fftconv(a, b)`: linear convolution of two real numeric sequences `a` and `b` via FFT.

operators.name: fgmres_solve
signatures: (Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>, Real) -> Tensor<1, Real>
operators.doc: `fgmres_solve(a, b, tol)`: solve general linear system `A x = b` by flexible GMRES to relative tolerance `tol`.

operators.name: fibonacci
operators.doc: `fibonacci(n)`: `n`-th Fibonacci number `F_n`.

operators.name: final_value_laplace
operators.doc: `final_value_laplace(F, s)`: applies the Laplace final-value theorem `lim_{s->0} s * F(s)`.

operators.name: final_value_z
operators.doc: `final_value_z(F, z)`: applies the Z-transform final-value theorem `lim_{z->1} (z - 1) * F(z)`.

operators.name: find_constrained_extrema
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Tensor<1, Symbol>) -> Tensor<1, { _0: Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, _1: Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, _2: Symbol, _3: Dyn<term> }>

operators.doc: `find_extrema(f, vars)`: finds unconstrained critical points of `f` with respect to `vars` and classifies them via the Hessian.

operators.name: first_integral
operators.doc: `first_integral(L, y, x)`: computes the Beltrami / energy first integral `L - y' * dL/dy'` for a first-order Lagrangian `L(x, y, y')`.

operators.name: first_law_thermodynamics
operators.doc: `first_law_thermodynamics(dU, Q, W)`: first law residual `dU - (Q - W)`.

operators.name: first_order_energy_correction

operators.name: fisher_exact
operators.doc: `fisher_exact(a, b, c, d)`: two-sided Fisher's exact test p-value for a 2x2 contingency table `[[a, b], [c, d]]`.

operators.name: floor
operators.doc: `floor(x)`: greatest integer less than or equal to `x`.

operators.name: forall
operators.doc: `forall(var_or_list, formula)`: universally quantifies Boolean variable(s) out of `formula`.

operators.name: form
operators.doc: `form(terms)`: differential form `sum c dx_i ^ ...` represented by `list(list(coeff, list(i, ...)), ...)`.

operators.name: fourier
operators.doc: `fourier(f, t, omega)`: continuous Fourier transform of `f(t)` into frequency `omega`.

operators.name: fourier_series
operators.doc: `fourier_series(f, x, L, n)`: trigonometric Fourier series of `f(x)` on `[-L, L]` up to `n` harmonics.

operators.name: fp_group
operators.doc: Constructs a `group(elements, table)` term for the finitely presented group `<gens | relators>` of order at most 720. The generator action satisfies the relators and has the same order as the enumerated coset count.
examples: fp_group(list(a, b), list(list(a^3), list(b^2), list(a, b, a, b)))

operators.name: fp_group_abelian_invariants
operators.doc: Computes the abelianization invariant factors (torsion factors `> 1` followed by `0` per free factor) of `<gens | relators>` via Smith normal form.

operators.name: fp_group_order
operators.doc: Computes the order of the finitely presented group `<gens | relators>` via Todd-Coxeter.

operators.name: frac
operators.doc: `frac(x)`: fractional part `x - floor(x)`.

operators.name: fredholm_eigenvalues
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
(Tensor<1, Symbol>, Tensor<1, Symbol>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, Int) -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
(Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, Dyn<term>) -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: `fredholm_eigenvalues(us, vs, x, t, a, b)`: eigenvalues of the separable Fredholm operator with kernel `sum u_i(x) v_i(t)` on `[a, b]`.

operators.name: fredholm_neumann
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc: `fredholm_neumann(f, lambda, K, x, t, a, b, n)`: `n`-th Neumann series iterate for `y(x) = f(x) + lambda int_a^b K(x, t) y(t) dt`.

operators.name: fredholm_separable
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc: `fredholm_separable(f, lambda, us, vs, x, t, a, b)`: exact solution of the Fredholm equation with separable kernel `sum u_i(x) v_i(t)`.

operators.name: fredholm_solve
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc: `fredholm_solve(f, lambda, K, x, t, a, b)`: exact solution of the Fredholm integral equation `y(x) = f(x) + lambda int_a^b K(x, t) y(t) dt`.

operators.name: fresnel_c_complex
operators.doc:
`fresnel_c_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of the complex Fresnel cosine integral `C(re + i*im)`.

`(S(z), C(z))` for a complex argument `z = re + i·im`, returned as
`((S.re, S.im), (C.re, C.im))`.

With `a = √π/2`, `E₁ = erf(a (1-i) z)`, `E₂ = erf(a (1+i) z)`:
`C(z) = (1+i)/4 · E₁ + (1-i)/4 · E₂`,
`S(z) = (1-i)/4 · E₁ + (1+i)/4 · E₂`.
Real arguments take the real kernels, so they keep full accuracy.

operators.name: fresnel_s_complex
operators.doc:
`fresnel_s_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of the complex Fresnel sine integral `S(re + i*im)`.

`(S(z), C(z))` for a complex argument `z = re + i·im`, returned as
`((S.re, S.im), (C.re, C.im))`.

With `a = √π/2`, `E₁ = erf(a (1-i) z)`, `E₂ = erf(a (1+i) z)`:
`C(z) = (1+i)/4 · E₁ + (1-i)/4 · E₂`,
`S(z) = (1-i)/4 · E₁ + (1+i)/4 · E₂`.
Real arguments take the real kernels, so they keep full accuracy.

operators.name: fresnelc
operators.doc: `fresnelc(x)`: Fresnel cosine integral `int_0^x cos(pi * t^2 / 2) dt`.

operators.name: fresnels
operators.doc: `fresnels(x)`: Fresnel sine integral `int_0^x sin(pi * t^2 / 2) dt`.

operators.name: frft_im
signatures: (Tensor<1, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>, Real) -> Tensor<1, Real>
operators.doc: `frft_im(re, im, a)`: imaginary part of the discrete fractional Fourier transform of order `a` of `re + i*im`.

operators.name: frft_re
signatures: (Tensor<1, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>, Real) -> Tensor<1, Real>
operators.doc: `frft_re(re, im, a)`: real part of the discrete fractional Fourier transform of order `a` of `re + i*im`.

operators.name: from_cartesian
operators.doc:
`from_cartesian(sys, coords)`: coordinates in system `sys` expressed in terms of Cartesian `coords`.

Converts a Cartesian point to the system `to`.

# Errors

Returns an error if `point` has the wrong number of components (2 for
polar, 3 for cylindrical and spherical).

operators.name: from_polar
operators.doc:
`from_polar(r, theta)`: reconstructs `r * (cos(theta) + I*sin(theta))`.

Reconstructs `r * exp(i * theta)`.

operators.name: from_riemann_sphere
operators.doc:
`from_riemann_sphere(X, Y, Z)`: inverse stereographic projection `(X + I*Y) / (1 - Z)` from `S^2` to `C`.

Inverse stereographic projection from `S^2` to `C`.
Returns `None` at the north pole `(0, 0, 1)` (infinity).

operators.name: fubini
operators.doc: `fubini(n)`: `n`-th ordered Bell (Fubini) number, counting weak orderings on `n` elements.

operators.name: function_inf_norm
operators.doc: `function_inf_norm(points)`: infinity (supremum) norm of a tabulated function `list(list(x, y), ...)`.

operators.name: function_inner
operators.doc: `function_inner(f, g)`: numerical L2 inner product of two tabulated functions `f` and `g`.

operators.name: function_l1_norm
operators.doc: `function_l1_norm(points)`: numerical L1 norm of a tabulated function `list(list(x, y), ...)`.

operators.name: function_l2_norm
operators.doc: `function_l2_norm(points)`: numerical L2 norm of a tabulated function `list(list(x, y), ...)`.

operators.name: function_normalize
operators.doc: `function_normalize(f)`: L2-normalized copy of tabulated function `f`.

operators.name: function_project
operators.doc: `function_project(f, g)`: orthogonal L2 projection of tabulated function `f` onto `g`.

operators.name: ga_apply_versor
operators.doc: `ga_apply_versor(V, X)`: versor sandwich product `V X^ V^-1` (grade-involuted `X^` for odd versor `V`).

operators.name: ga_commutator
operators.doc: `ga_commutator(A, B)`: commutator product `(A B - B A) / 2`.

operators.name: ga_conjugate
operators.doc: `ga_conjugate(A)`: Clifford conjugate scaling each grade-`k` part by `(-1)^(k*(k+1)/2)`.
examples: ga_conjugate(mv(list(3, 0, 0), list(list(0, s), list(1, a), list(3, b), list(7, c))))

operators.name: ga_dual
operators.doc: `ga_dual(A)`: dual `A I^-1` with respect to pseudoscalar `I` (or `A I` for degenerate metrics).

operators.name: ga_exp
operators.doc: `ga_exp(A)`: Clifford exponential `exp(A)` when `A^2` is a scalar.

operators.name: ga_gp
operators.doc: `ga_gp(A, B)`: geometric product `A B` of multivectors `A` and `B`.

operators.name: ga_grade
operators.doc: `ga_grade(A, k)`: grade-`k` projection `<A>_k` of multivector `A`.
examples: ga_grade(mv(list(3, 0, 0), list(list(0, s), list(1, a), list(3, b), list(7, c))), 0)

operators.name: ga_inner
operators.doc: `ga_inner(A, B)`: Hestenes inner product `sum_{r,s>0} <A_r B_s>_{|r-s|}`.

operators.name: ga_inverse
operators.doc: `ga_inverse(A)`: multiplicative inverse `A^-1` for a versor or blade with nonzero scalar square.

operators.name: ga_involute
operators.doc: `ga_involute(A)`: grade involution `A^` scaling each grade-`k` part by `(-1)^k`.
examples: ga_involute(mv(list(3, 0, 0), list(list(0, s), list(1, a), list(3, b), list(7, c))))

operators.name: ga_lcontract
operators.doc: `ga_lcontract(A, B)`: left contraction `sum_{r,s} <A_r B_s>_{s-r}`.

operators.name: ga_norm
operators.doc: `ga_norm(A)`: norm `sqrt(<A A~>_0)` of multivector `A`.

operators.name: ga_norm_squared
operators.doc: `ga_norm_squared(A)`: squared norm `<A A~>_0` of multivector `A`.

operators.name: ga_normalize
operators.doc: `ga_normalize(A)`: normalized multivector `A / ga_norm(A)`.

operators.name: ga_rcontract
operators.doc: `ga_rcontract(A, B)`: right contraction `sum_{r,s} <A_r B_s>_{r-s}`.

operators.name: ga_reverse
operators.doc: `ga_reverse(A)`: reversion `A~` scaling each grade-`k` part by `(-1)^(k*(k-1)/2)`.
examples: ga_reverse(mv(list(3, 0, 0), list(list(0, s), list(1, a), list(3, b), list(7, c))))

operators.name: ga_rotor
operators.doc: `ga_rotor(B, angle)`: rotor `exp(-angle * B_hat / 2)` for bivector `B` and rotation angle `angle`.

operators.name: ga_scalar_product
operators.doc: `ga_scalar_product(A, B)`: scalar product `<A B>_0` of multivectors `A` and `B`.

operators.doc: `ga_undual(A)`: undual `A I` with respect to pseudoscalar `I`.
examples: ga_undual(ga_dual(mv(list(3, 0, 0), list(list(0, s), list(1, a), list(3, b), list(7, c)))))

operators.name: ga_wedge
operators.doc: `ga_wedge(A, B)`: outer (exterior) product `A ^ B = sum_{r,s} <A_r B_s>_{r+s}`.

operators.name: gamma
operators.doc: `gamma(z)`: Euler gamma function `Gamma(z)`.

operators.name: gamma_complex
operators.doc:
`gamma_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of the complex Gamma function `Gamma(re + i*im)`.

`Γ(z)`; poles (non-positive integers) give `+∞`.

operators.name: gamma_dist
operators.doc: `gamma_dist(shape, rate)`: gamma distribution with shape parameter `shape` and rate parameter `rate`.

operators.name: gamma_lr
operators.doc: `gamma_lr(a, x)`: regularized lower incomplete gamma function `P(a, x) = gamma(a, x) / Gamma(a)`.

operators.name: gauss_theorem
operators.doc: `gauss_theorem(F, vars, bounds)`: outward flux integral of vector field `F` over box `bounds` via the divergence theorem.

operators.name: gaussian_curvature
operators.doc: `gaussian_curvature(g, vars)`: Gaussian curvature `K = R / 2` of a 2D metric `g` in `vars`.

operators.name: gcd
operators.doc:
`gcd(a, b)`: greatest common divisor of integers `a` and `b`.

Computes the greatest common divisor (GCD) of two numbers using Stein's binary GCD algorithm
after one initial Euclidean reduction step.

# Arguments
* `a` - The first number.
* `b` - The second number.

# Returns
The greatest common divisor of `a` and `b`.

operators.name: ge
operators.doc: `ge(a, b)`: greater-than-or-equal comparison `a >= b`.

operators.name: generalized_stokes
operators.doc: `generalized_stokes(omega, vars, M)`: evaluates both sides of `int_M d(omega) = int_{dM} omega` as an equation.
examples: generalized_stokes(form(list(list(x, list(2)))), list(x, y), cell(list(x, y), list(x, y), list(list(0, 1), list(0, 1))))

examples: geodesic_acceleration(christoffel(list(list(1, 0), list(0, r^2)), list(r, theta)), list(u, v))

operators.name: geometric

operators.name: geometric_mean

`geometric_mean(xs)`: geometric mean `(prod x_i)^(1/n)` of list `xs`.

GM = (x1 * x2 * ... * xn)^(1/n)

operators.name: geweke
operators.doc:
`geweke(chain)`: the Geweke convergence z-score of the first tenth against the last half of `chain`.

Geweke z-score comparing the first 10 % with the last 50 % of a chain.

The two segments are compared with a difference of means standardised by
their sample variances. Values far from zero in absolute value suggest that
the chain has not converged.

# Errors
Returns an error for fewer than twenty draws or a zero variance.

operators.name: gf256_add

Computes `a + b` (bitwise XOR) in GF(2^8).

Performs addition in GF(2^8).

In GF(2^8), addition is equivalent to a bitwise XOR operation.

operators.name: gf_add

operators.name: gf_div

operators.name: gf_inv

operators.name: gf_is_one

operators.name: gf_is_zero
operators.doc: Returns `true` if `a = 0 (mod p)` in GF(p).

operators.name: gf_mul
operators.doc: Computes `(a * b) mod p` in the prime field GF(p).

operators.name: gf_neg
operators.doc: Computes `(-a) mod p` in the prime field GF(p).

operators.name: gf_pow

operators.name: gf_sub
operators.doc: Computes `(a - b) mod p` in the prime field GF(p).

operators.name: gfp_divmod
signatures: (Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int) -> Tensor<2, Int>
operators.doc: Computes Euclidean polynomial division `f / g` over GF(p), returning `list(quotient, remainder)`.

operators.name: gfp_edf
operators.doc: Computes the equal-degree factorization (Cantor-Zassenhaus) of a squarefree polynomial `f` of degree `k*d` over GF(p) into irreducible factors of degree `d`.

operators.name: gfp_egcd
signatures: (Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int) -> Tensor<2, Int>
operators.doc: Computes the extended Euclidean algorithm on polynomials `f` and `g` over GF(p), returning `list(d, s, t)` with `s*f + t*g = d`.

operators.name: gfp_eval
operators.doc: Evaluates polynomial `f` at scalar `x` in GF(p).

operators.name: gfp_factor
operators.doc: Computes the complete factorization of polynomial `f` over GF(p) as `list(lc, list(g1, m1), ...)`, ordered by degree.

operators.name: gfp_gcd
operators.doc: Computes the monic greatest common divisor of polynomials `f` and `g` over GF(p).

operators.name: gfp_invmod
signatures: (Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Int>
operators.doc: Computes the inverse of polynomial `f` modulo `m` over GF(p) when `gcd(f, m) = 1`.

operators.name: gfp_isirreducible
operators.doc: Tests whether polynomial `f` is irreducible over GF(p) using Rabin's irreducibility test.

operators.name: gfp_monic
operators.doc: Divides polynomial `f` by its leading coefficient modulo prime `p` to produce the monic polynomial.

operators.name: gfp_mul
signatures: (Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
(Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Int>
operators.doc: Computes the product `f * g` of two polynomials over GF(p).

operators.name: gfp_norm
operators.doc: Normalizes a highest-degree-first polynomial `f` over GF(p) by reducing coefficients modulo `p` and stripping leading zeros.

operators.name: gfp_powmod
signatures: (Tensor<1, Int>, Int, Tensor<1, Int>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Int>
operators.doc: Computes `f^e mod m` for polynomial `f`, non-negative integer `e`, and modulus polynomial `m` over GF(p).

operators.name: gfp_squarefree
operators.doc: Computes the squarefree factorization of polynomial `f` over GF(p) as `list(list(g1, m1), ...)` using Yun's algorithm.

operators.name: gfp_sub
signatures: (Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: Computes the difference `f - g` of two polynomials over GF(p).

operators.name: gfx_add
signatures: (Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Int>
(Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Int>
(Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: Computes `(a + b) mod m` in the extension field GF(p)[x]/(m).

operators.name: gfx_div
signatures: (Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Int>
operators.doc: Computes `a * b^(-1) mod m` in the extension field GF(p)[x]/(m) when `b` is invertible modulo `m`.

operators.name: gfx_inv
operators.doc: Computes the multiplicative inverse `a^(-1) mod m` in the extension field GF(p)[x]/(m).

operators.name: gfx_mul
signatures: (Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Int>
operators.doc: Computes `(a * b) mod m` in the extension field GF(p)[x]/(m).

operators.name: gfx_neg
operators.doc: Computes `(-a) mod m` in the extension field GF(p)[x]/(m).

operators.name: gfx_pow
signatures: (Tensor<1, Int>, Int, Tensor<1, Int>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Int>
operators.doc: Computes `a^e mod m` in the extension field GF(p)[x]/(m) for integer exponent `e`.

operators.name: gfx_reduce
operators.doc: Reduces polynomial `a` modulo `m` over GF(p) in the extension field GF(p)[x]/(m).

operators.name: gfx_sub
signatures: (Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Int>
(Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Int>
operators.doc: Computes `(a - b) mod m` in the extension field GF(p)[x]/(m).

operators.name: gibbs_free_energy
operators.doc: `gibbs_free_energy(H, T, S)`: Gibbs free energy `G = H - T S`.

operators.name: gini
operators.doc: `gini(ps)`: Gini impurity `1 - sum p_i^2` of categorical distribution `ps`.

operators.name: gl_basis
operators.doc: `gl_basis(n)`: standard matrix basis `E_ij` of the general linear Lie algebra `gl(n)`.

operators.name: glm_fit
signatures: (Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>, Symbol, Symbol, Tensor<1, Real>, Real) -> { beta: Tensor<1, Real>, se: Tensor<1, Real>, deviance: Real, null_deviance: Real, aic: Real, iterations: Real, fitted: Tensor<1, Real> }
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
`glm_fit(x, y, family, link, weights, tol)`: `list(beta, se, deviance, null_deviance, aic, iterations, fitted)` of a generalised linear model fitted by iteratively reweighted least squares; `x` is a list of rows without an intercept, `weights` is empty for equal weights.

Fits a generalised linear model by iteratively reweighted least squares.

`x` holds one row of covariates per observation and must **not** contain an
intercept column; `fit` prepends one, so the returned coefficient vector has
`x[0].len() + 1` entries with the intercept first. `weights` are prior
weights (number of trials for a binomial proportion, exposure for a Poisson
rate); when `None` every observation weighs one.

Convergence is declared when `max |Δβ| / (1 + |β|) < tol`. Each step is
halved up to `MAX_HALVINGS` times while the deviance would increase.

# Errors
Returns a lowercase message when the design and response disagree in
length, the design is empty or non-finite, a weight is not strictly
positive, the response leaves the family's support, `max_iter` is zero,
`tol` is not positive, there are fewer observations than parameters, or a
linear system in the iteration is singular.

operators.name: glm_predict
signatures: (Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>, Symbol) -> Tensor<1, Real>
operators.doc:
`glm_predict(x, beta, link)`: the fitted mean of each row of `x` given the coefficients `beta` (intercept first) and the `link`.

Predicts response means from an intercept followed by fitted coefficients.

# Errors
Fails on an empty coefficient vector, a mismatched row, or a non-finite mean.

operators.name: grad
operators.doc: `grad(f, vars)`: gradient vector `[df/dx_1, ..., df/dx_n]` of scalar expression `f`.

operators.name: grad_in
operators.doc: `grad_in(f, sys, vars)`: physical-component gradient of scalar `f` in orthogonal coordinate system `sys(vars)`.

operators.name: gram_matrix
signatures: (Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Dyn<term>, Int, Int) -> Tensor<2, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: `gram_matrix(funcs, x, a, b)`: Gram matrix of `L^2([a, b])` inner products `<f_i, f_j>`.

operators.name: gram_schmidt
signatures: (Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Dyn<term>, Int, Int) -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc:
`gram_schmidt(funcs, x, a, b)`: orthogonal basis of `span(funcs)` on `[a, b]` in `L^2(x)`.

Performs the Gram-Schmidt process to orthogonalize a set of functions.
All functions must have the same sampling points.

# Errors
Returns an error if any pair of input functions has mismatched sample points.

operators.name: gram_schmidt_orthonormal
signatures: (Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Dyn<term>, Int, Int) -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc:
`gram_schmidt_orthonormal(funcs, x, a, b)`: orthonormal basis of `span(funcs)` on `[a, b]` in `L^2(x)`.

Performs the Gram-Schmidt process to orthonormalize a set of functions.

# Errors
Returns an error if any pair of input functions has mismatched sample points.

operators.name: graph
operators.doc: Undirected graph constructor `graph(n, edges[, hyperedges])` with vertices `0..n-1`, edge list `list(list(u, v[, w]), ...)`, and optional hyperedges.

operators.name: graph_add_edge
operators.doc: Returns a new graph with edge `(u, v)` (and optional weight `w`, default `1`) added to `g`.

operators.name: graph_add_hyperedge
operators.doc: Returns a new graph with hyperedge `(vs, w)` added to `g`.

operators.name: graph_add_node
operators.doc: Returns a new graph with one additional isolated vertex appended.

operators.name: graph_adjacency
operators.doc: Returns the weighted adjacency matrix of graph `g` as `list(list(...))`, summing parallel edge weights.
examples: graph_adjacency(graph(3, list(list(0, 1, a), list(1, 2, b), list(0, 2, c))))

operators.name: graph_automorphisms
signatures: (graph) -> { _0: Int, _1: Tensor<2, Int>, _2: Tensor<1, Tensor<1, Int>> }
operators.doc: Computes the automorphism group of graph `g` as `list(order, generators, orbits)`.
examples: graph_automorphisms(digraph(5, list(list(0, 1), list(1, 2), list(2, 3), list(3, 4), list(4, 0))))

operators.name: graph_bellman_ford
operators.doc: Computes single-source shortest paths from `s` in graph `g` using Bellman-Ford, returning `list(list(dist, prev), ...)` or `false` on a negative cycle.

operators.name: graph_bfs
operators.doc: Returns the breadth-first search vertex visitation order starting from vertex `s` in graph `g`.
examples: graph_bfs(graph(6, list(list(0, 1, 1), list(0, 2, 1), list(1, 3, 1), list(2, 3, 1), list(4, 5, 1))), 0)

operators.name: graph_bipartite_matching
operators.doc: Computes a maximum bipartite matching of graph `g` with bipartition coloring `part`, returning matched pairs `list(list(u, v), ...)`.

operators.name: graph_blossom
operators.doc: Computes a maximum cardinality matching of general undirected graph `g` using Edmonds' blossom algorithm.

operators.name: graph_bridges
operators.doc: Returns `list(bridges, articulation_points)` of an undirected graph. Bridges are in depth-first completion order, with the parent endpoint first. Articulation points are in vertex order. Parallel edges and self-loops are supported.

operators.name: graph_canonical_form
operators.doc: Computes the canonical labeling `list(order, adjacency)` of graph `g` (up to search budget).

operators.name: graph_cartesian
operators.doc: Computes the Cartesian product `g □ h` with vertex pairs `(u, v)` numbered `u * |V(h)| + v`.

operators.name: graph_chromatic_number
operators.doc: Computes the exact chromatic number of undirected graph `g` (up to 40 vertices, no self-loops).

operators.name: graph_complement
operators.doc: Returns the complement graph of simple graph `g`.

operators.name: graph_complete
operators.doc: Constructs the undirected complete graph K_n on `n` vertices.

operators.name: graph_components
operators.doc: Returns connected components as vertex lists in breadth-first order. For a digraph, each list is an outgoing reachability walk from the next previously unreached vertex, so lists can overlap.
examples: graph_components(graph(6, list(list(0, 1, 1), list(0, 2, 1), list(1, 3, 1), list(2, 3, 1), list(4, 5, 1))))

operators.name: graph_cycle
operators.doc: Constructs the undirected cycle graph C_n on `n` vertices (empty if `n < 3`).

operators.name: graph_dfs
operators.doc: Returns the depth-first search vertex visitation order starting from vertex `s` in graph `g`.
examples: graph_dfs(graph(6, list(list(0, 1, 1), list(0, 2, 1), list(1, 3, 1), list(2, 3, 1), list(4, 5, 1))), 0)

operators.name: graph_dijkstra
operators.doc: Computes single-source shortest paths from `s` in non-negatively weighted graph `g` using Dijkstra's algorithm, returning `list(list(dist, prev), ...)`.

operators.name: graph_dinic
operators.doc: Computes the maximum flow from source `s` to sink `t` in graph `g` using Dinic's algorithm.

operators.name: graph_disjoint_union
operators.doc: Returns the disjoint union of graphs `g` and `h`, shifting `h`'s vertices by `|V(g)|`.

operators.name: graph_edges
operators.doc: Returns the edge list `list(list(u, v, w), ...)` of graph `g` (undirected edges listed once with `u <= v`).

operators.name: graph_edmonds_karp
operators.doc: Computes the maximum flow from source `s` to sink `t` in graph `g` using the Edmonds-Karp algorithm.

operators.name: graph_empty
operators.doc: Constructs an undirected empty graph on `n` vertices with no edges.

operators.name: graph_floyd_warshall
operators.doc: Computes the all-pairs shortest-path distance matrix of graph `g` using the Floyd-Warshall algorithm.
examples: graph_floyd_warshall(graph(6, list(list(0, 2, 7), list(0, 3, 2), list(1, 2, 7), list(1, 3, 9), list(1, 4, 9), list(2, 4, 8), list(3, 4, 3))))

operators.name: graph_greedy_coloring
operators.doc: Computes a greedy Welsh-Powell vertex coloring of undirected graph `g` as color indices `0, 1, ...`.
examples: graph_greedy_coloring(graph(6, list(list(0, 2, 1), list(0, 5, 1), list(1, 3, 1), list(3, 4, 1), list(3, 5, 1))))

operators.name: graph_has_cycle
operators.doc: Returns `true` if graph `g` contains a cycle.

operators.name: graph_hopcroft_karp
operators.doc: Computes a maximum bipartite matching of graph `g` with bipartition coloring `part` using the Hopcroft-Karp algorithm.

operators.name: graph_hyperedges
operators.doc: Returns the list of hyperedges `list(list(vs, w), ...)` of graph `g`.

operators.name: graph_in_degree
operators.doc: Returns the in-degree (or degree for undirected graphs) of vertex `u` in graph `g`.

operators.name: graph_incidence
operators.doc: Returns the vertex-edge incidence matrix of graph `g` (`-1/+1` for directed edges, `1/1` for undirected edges).

operators.name: graph_intersection
operators.doc: Returns the graph intersection of `g` and `h` on `min(|V(g)|, |V(h)|)` vertices.

operators.name: graph_is_bipartite
operators.doc: Tests if graph `g` is bipartite, returning a 2-coloring list of `0`/`1` per vertex or `false`.

operators.name: graph_is_connected
operators.doc: Returns `true` when vertex zero can reach all vertices. A digraph uses outgoing arcs, and an empty graph returns `false`.
examples: graph_is_connected(graph(6, list(list(0, 1, 1), list(0, 2, 1), list(1, 3, 1), list(2, 3, 1), list(4, 5, 1))))

operators.name: graph_is_directed
operators.doc: Returns `true` if `g` is a directed graph (`digraph`) and `false` if undirected (`graph`).

operators.name: graph_isomorphic
operators.doc: Tests whether graphs `g` and `h` are isomorphic (ignoring edge weights) by canonical labeling with exhaustive fallback.
examples: graph_isomorphic(digraph(3, list(list(0, 1), list(1, 2))), digraph(3, list(list(2, 1), list(1, 0))))

operators.name: graph_isomorphic_heuristic
operators.doc: Tests a necessary condition for isomorphism between graphs `g` and `h` using 1-dimensional Weisfeiler-Lehman refinement.
examples: graph_isomorphic_heuristic(graph(4, list(list(1, 2, 1), list(2, 3, 1))), graph(4, list(list(2, 1, 1), list(1, 3, 1))))

operators.name: graph_join
operators.doc: Returns the graph join of `g` and `h` (disjoint union plus all edges between `V(g)` and `V(h)`).

operators.name: graph_kruskal
operators.doc: Computes a minimum spanning forest of undirected graph `g` using Kruskal's algorithm, returning edges `list(list(u, v, w), ...)`.
examples: graph_kruskal(graph(4, list(list(0, 1, 1), list(1, 2, 2), list(2, 3, 3), list(0, 3, 10), list(0, 2, 5))))

operators.name: graph_laplacian
operators.doc: Returns the weighted graph Laplacian matrix `D - A` of graph `g`.

operators.name: graph_min_cost_flow
operators.doc: Computes a minimum-cost maximum flow from `s` to `t` in graph `g` with `list(capacity, cost)` edge weights, returning `list(flow, cost)`.

operators.name: graph_neighbors
operators.doc: Returns the outgoing neighbors of vertex `u` in graph `g` as `list(list(v, w), ...)`.

operators.name: graph_node_count
operators.doc: Returns the number of vertices in graph `g`.

operators.name: graph_node_id
operators.doc: Validates and returns vertex index `v` if `0 <= v < n` in graph `g`.

operators.name: graph_nodes
operators.doc: Returns the list of vertex indices `0..n-1` of graph `g`.

operators.name: graph_out_degree
operators.doc: Returns the out-degree (or degree for undirected graphs) of vertex `u` in graph `g`.

operators.name: graph_path
operators.doc: Constructs the undirected path graph P_n on `n` vertices.

operators.name: graph_prim
operators.doc: Computes a minimum spanning tree of undirected graph `g` rooted at vertex `s` using Prim's algorithm.
examples: graph_prim(graph(4, list(list(0, 1, 1), list(1, 2, 2), list(2, 3, 3), list(0, 3, 10), list(0, 2, 5))), 0)

operators.name: graph_scc
operators.doc: Returns the strongly connected components of directed graph `g` as sorted vertex lists.
examples: graph_scc(digraph(6, list(list(0, 1, 1), list(1, 2, 1), list(2, 0, 1), list(2, 3, 1), list(3, 4, 1), list(4, 3, 1))))

operators.name: graph_shortest_path_unweighted
operators.doc: Computes unweighted shortest paths from `s` in graph `g` via BFS, returning `list(list(v, dist, prev), ...)` for reachable vertices.

operators.name: graph_tensor
operators.doc: Computes the tensor (direct) product `g × h` with vertex pairs `(u, v)` numbered `u * |V(h)| + v`.
examples: graph_tensor(graph(2, list(list(0, 1, a))), graph(2, list(list(0, 1, b))))

operators.name: graph_toposort
operators.doc: Computes a topological ordering of directed acyclic graph `g`, or `false` if `g` contains a cycle.

operators.name: graph_toposort_dfs
operators.doc: Computes a topological ordering of directed graph `g` using DFS post-order, or `false` if cyclic.

operators.name: graph_toposort_kahn
operators.doc: Computes a topological ordering of directed graph `g` using Kahn's algorithm, or `false` if cyclic.
examples: graph_toposort_kahn(digraph(6, list(list(5, 2), list(5, 0), list(4, 0), list(4, 1), list(2, 3), list(3, 1))))

operators.name: graph_union
operators.doc: Returns the graph union of `g` and `h` on `max(|V(g)|, |V(h)|)` vertices.

operators.name: graph_vertex_cover
operators.doc: Computes a minimum vertex cover of bipartite graph `g` from bipartition `part` and maximum `matching` via Konig's theorem.

operators.name: gravitational_force
operators.doc: `gravitational_force(m1, m2, r)`: Newtonian gravitational force magnitude `G_N m1 m2 / r^2`.

operators.name: gravitational_time_dilation
operators.doc: `gravitational_time_dilation(t, r, M)`: proper time `t sqrt(1 - r_s / r)` at radius `r` outside mass `M`.

operators.name: greens_theorem
operators.doc: `greens_theorem(P, Q, list(x, y), bounds)`: circulation integral of `(P, Q)` around rectangle `bounds` via Green's theorem.

operators.name: groebner
signatures: () -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>> with 0... x Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc:
`groebner(polys, vars)` computes the reduced Gröbner basis of the rational ideal generated by `polys` in lexicographic order.

An optional third argument selects `lex`, `grlex`, or `grevlex`.

The basis is returned as a list of polynomials over the listed `vars`.
examples: groebner(list(x + y - 3, x - y - 1), list(x, y))
groebner(list(x^3 - 2*x*y, x^2*y - 2*y^2 + x), list(x, y), grlex)

operators.name: groebner_f4
operators.doc: `groebner_f4(polys, vars, [order])`: computes a reduced Groebner basis of ideal `polys` over `vars` using Faugere's F4 matrix-reduction algorithm.

operators.name: groebner_f5
operators.doc: Computes the reduced Gröbner basis of `polys` over the listed `vars` with the signature-based F5 algorithm. Accepts `(polys, vars)`, `(polys, vars, order)`, `(polys, vars, p)`, or `(polys, vars, order, p)`. The default order is `lex`. Use `grlex` or `grevlex` to override it. Coefficients are rational by default or in GF(p) for prime p.

operators.name: group
operators.doc: Inert finite group constructor `group(elements, table)` storing element list and Cayley multiplication table.

operators.name: group_automorphism_count
operators.doc: Computes `|Aut(G)|`, the number of automorphisms of finite group `G`.

operators.name: group_center
operators.doc: Returns the center `Z(G)` of finite group `G` as a list of elements.

operators.name: group_character
operators.doc: Computes the character (list of matrix traces) of a matrix representation `mats`.
examples: group_character(list(list(list(1)), list(list(-1)), list(list(-1)), list(list(1)), list(list(1)), list(list(-1))))

operators.name: group_character_degrees
operators.doc: Returns the degrees (dimensions) of the irreducible characters of finite group `G`.
examples: group_character_degrees(fp_group(list(a, b), list(list(a^4), list(a, a, -2, -2), list(b, a, -2, a))))

operators.name: group_character_table
operators.doc: Computes the exact character table of finite group `G` via Burnside-Dixon's algorithm, returning irreducible characters as lists of class values.
examples: group_character_table(fp_group(list(a, b), list(list(a^4), list(a, a, -2, -2), list(b, a, -2, a))))

operators.name: group_class_count
operators.doc: Returns the number of conjugacy classes of finite group `G`.
examples: group_class_count(fp_group(list(a, b), list(list(a^4), list(a, a, -2, -2), list(b, a, -2, a))))

operators.name: group_class_index
operators.doc: Returns the 1-based conjugacy class index of element `x` in finite group `G`.

operators.name: group_class_representatives
operators.doc: Returns one representative element per conjugacy class of finite group `G`.

operators.name: group_class_sizes
operators.doc: Returns the sizes of the conjugacy classes of finite group `G`.

operators.name: group_conjugacy_classes
operators.doc: Returns the conjugacy classes of finite group `G` as lists of elements.

operators.name: group_cosets
operators.doc: Returns the left cosets of subgroup `H` in finite group `G`.

operators.name: group_derived_series
operators.doc: Computes the derived series `G > G' > G'' > ...` of finite group `G` as element lists down to the first repeat.

operators.name: group_derived_subgroup
operators.doc: Returns the commutator (derived) subgroup `G'` of finite group `G` as an element list.

operators.name: group_direct_product
operators.doc: Constructs the direct product `G × H` of finite groups `G` and `H` with elements `list(g, h)`.

operators.name: group_element_order
operators.doc: Computes the multiplicative order of element `a` in finite group `G`.

operators.name: group_element_orders
operators.doc: Returns the list of multiplicative orders of all elements of finite group `G`.

operators.name: group_elements
operators.doc: Returns the element list of finite group `G`.

operators.name: group_exponent
operators.doc: Computes the group exponent (LCM of all element orders) of finite group `G`.

operators.name: group_from_perms
operators.doc: Builds a `group(elements, table)` term from permutation generators `gens` (for group orders up to 720).

operators.name: group_from_table
operators.doc: Constructs `group(elements, table)` if the Cayley table satisfies the group axioms.
examples: group_from_table(list(e, x), list(list(e, x), list(x, e)))

operators.name: group_generate
operators.doc: Returns the element list of the subgroup generated by `gens` in finite group `G`.

operators.name: group_identity
operators.doc: Returns the identity element of finite group `G`.

operators.name: group_inner_automorphism_count
operators.doc: Computes `|Inn(G)| = |G / Z(G)|`, the number of inner automorphisms of finite group `G`.

operators.name: group_inverse
operators.doc: Returns the inverse `a^(-1)` of element `a` in finite group `G`.

operators.name: group_is_abelian
operators.doc: Returns `true` if finite group `G` is abelian (commutative).
examples: group_is_abelian(fp_group(list(a, b), list(list(a^3), list(b^2), list(a, b, a, b))))

operators.name: group_is_isomorphic
operators.doc: Returns `true` if finite groups `G` and `H` are isomorphic.

operators.name: group_is_nilpotent
operators.doc: Returns `true` if the lower central series of finite group `G` reaches the trivial subgroup.

operators.name: group_is_normal
operators.doc: Returns `true` if `H` is a normal subgroup of finite group `G`.

operators.name: group_is_simple
operators.doc: Returns `true` if finite group `G` is non-trivial and has no proper non-trivial normal subgroups.

operators.name: group_is_solvable
operators.doc: Returns `true` if the derived series of finite group `G` reaches the trivial subgroup.

operators.name: group_is_valid
operators.doc: Verifies closure, associativity, identity, and inverses for finite group `G`.
examples: group_is_valid(fp_group(list(a, b), list(list(a^3), list(b^2), list(a, b, a, b))))

operators.name: group_isomorphism
operators.doc: Finds a group isomorphism from `G` to `H`, returning the image elements of `H` aligned with `G`'s elements, or `false`.

operators.name: group_lower_central_series
operators.doc: Computes the lower central series `G = gamma_1 > [gamma_1, G] > ...` of finite group `G` down to the first repeat.

operators.name: group_mul
operators.doc: Computes the group product `a * b` in finite group `G`.

operators.name: group_nilpotency_class
operators.doc: Returns the nilpotency class of finite group `G` (length of lower central series minus 1), or `false` if `G` is not nilpotent.

operators.name: group_normal_subgroups
operators.doc: Enumerates all normal subgroups of finite group `G` as element lists.

operators.name: group_order
operators.doc: Returns the order (number of elements) of finite group `G`.
examples: group_order(fp_group(list(a, b), list(list(a^3), list(b^2), list(a, b, a, b))))

operators.name: group_order_statistics
operators.doc: Returns the distribution of element orders in finite group `G` as `list(list(order, count), ...)`.

operators.name: group_outer_automorphism_count
operators.doc: Computes `|Out(G)| = |Aut(G)| / |Inn(G)|`, the outer automorphism group order of `G`.

operators.name: group_quotient
operators.doc: Constructs the quotient group `G/N` as a `group(cosets, table)` term for normal subgroup `N`.

operators.name: group_subgroup
operators.doc: Constructs the subgroup generated by `gens` in finite group `G` as a `group(elements, table)` term.

operators.name: group_subgroups
operators.doc: Enumerates all subgroups of finite group `G` (for orders up to 48) as element lists.

operators.name: group_sylow_count
operators.doc: Returns the number `n_p = [G : N_G(P)]` of Sylow `p`-subgroups of finite group `G`.

operators.name: group_sylow_subgroup
operators.doc: Returns a Sylow `p`-subgroup of finite group `G` for prime `p` as an element list.

operators.name: group_sylow_subgroups
operators.doc: Enumerates all Sylow `p`-subgroups of finite group `G` as element lists.

operators.name: gt
operators.doc: `gt(a, b)`: strict greater-than comparison `a > b`.

operators.name: gumbel
operators.doc: `gumbel(mu, beta)`: Gumbel (type-I extreme value) distribution with location `mu` and scale `beta`.

operators.name: h_planck
operators.doc: `h_planck`: Planck constant in J*s (exact SI).

operators.name: hall_coefficient
operators.doc: `hall_coefficient(n, q)`: Hall coefficient `1 / (n q)` for carrier density `n` and charge `q`.

operators.name: hamilton_equations
operators.doc: `hamilton_equations(H, q, p)`: Hamilton's canonical equations `list(dH/dp, -dH/dq)` for `(q_dot, p_dot)`.

operators.name: hamiltonian
operators.doc: `hamiltonian(T, V)`: total mechanical energy `H = T + V` from kinetic energy `T` and potential energy `V`.

operators.name: hamiltonian_3d
operators.doc: `hamiltonian_3d(m, V, vars)`: multi-dimensional Hamiltonian `-(hbar^2 / (2 m)) nabla^2 + V` in coordinates `vars`.

operators.name: hamiltonian_free_particle
operators.doc: `hamiltonian_free_particle(m, x)`: 1D free-particle Hamiltonian `-(hbar^2 / (2 m)) d^2/dx^2`.

operators.name: hamiltonian_harmonic_oscillator
operators.doc: `hamiltonian_harmonic_oscillator(m, w, x)`: 1D quantum harmonic oscillator Hamiltonian with frequency `w`.

operators.name: hamiltonian_of
operators.doc: `hamiltonian_of(L, y, x)`: computes the Hamiltonian `sum(y' * dL/dy') - L` via Legendre transform of Lagrangian `L`.

operators.name: hamiltonian_operator
operators.doc: `hamiltonian_operator(m, V, x)`: 1D Hamiltonian operator `-(hbar^2 / (2 m)) d^2/dx^2 + V`.

operators.name: hamiltons_principle
operators.doc: `hamiltons_principle(L, q, t)`: applies Hamilton's principle to Lagrangian `L`, returning `euler_lagrange(L, q, t)`.
examples: hamiltons_principle(1/2*diff(x(t), t)^2 - x(t)*y(t) + 1/2*diff(y(t), t)^2, list(x(t), y(t)), t)

operators.name: hamming_check
operators.doc: Checks whether a 7-bit Hamming(7,4) codeword has a zero syndrome (no detected single-bit error).

operators.name: hamming_decode
operators.doc: Decodes a 7-bit Hamming(7,4) codeword, returning `list(data, position)` where `position` is the 1-based corrected bit index (`0` if error-free).

operators.name: hamming_distance
operators.doc: Computes the Hamming distance (number of differing positions) between two equal-length byte lists `a` and `b`.

operators.name: hamming_encode
operators.doc: Encodes a 4-bit data word into a 7-bit Hamming(7,4) codeword with parity bits at positions 1, 2, and 4.

operators.name: hamming_weight
operators.doc: Computes the Hamming weight (number of non-zero symbols) of a byte list `a`.

operators.name: hamming_window
operators.doc:
`hamming_window(n)`: `n`-point symmetric Hamming window sequence.

Generates a Hamming window of length `n`.

# Arguments
* `n` - The number of points in the output window.

operators.name: hankel_h1_complex
operators.doc:
`hankel_h1_complex(nu, re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `H_nu^(1)(z)`.

Complex Hankel function of the first kind `H_nu^(1)(z) = J_nu(z) + i * Y_nu(z)`.
Uses `K_nu(-i*z)` connection in the upper half-plane (`Im(z) > 1.0`) to avoid cancellation.

operators.name: hankel_h2_complex
operators.doc:
`hankel_h2_complex(nu, re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `H_nu^(2)(z)`.

Complex Hankel function of the second kind `H_nu^(2)(z) = J_nu(z) - i * Y_nu(z)`.
Uses `K_nu(i*z)` connection in the lower half-plane (`Im(z) < -1.0`) to avoid cancellation.

operators.name: hann_window
operators.doc:
`hann_window(n)`: `n`-point symmetric Hann window sequence.

Generates a Hann window of length `n`.

# Arguments
* `n` - The number of points in the output window.

operators.name: harmonic
operators.doc:
`harmonic(n)`: `n`-th harmonic number `H_n = sum_{k=1}^n 1/k` (analytically continued via `psi(x + 1) + gamma`).

The `n`-th harmonic number `sum_{k=1..n} 1/k`, with `H_0 = 0`.

operators.name: harmonic_conjugate
operators.doc: `harmonic_conjugate(u, x, y)`: constructs a harmonic conjugate `v(x, y)` of harmonic `u(x, y)`.

operators.name: harmonic_mean
operators.doc:
`harmonic_mean(xs)`: harmonic mean `n / (sum 1/x_i)` of list `xs`.

Computes the harmonic mean of a slice of positive data.
HM = n / (1/x1 + 1/x2 + ... + 1/xn)

operators.name: harmonic_oscillator_frequency
operators.doc: `harmonic_oscillator_frequency(k, m)`: angular frequency `sqrt(k / m)` of a simple harmonic oscillator.

operators.name: hbar
operators.doc: `hbar`: reduced Planck constant `h / (2 * pi)` in J*s.

operators.name: heat_capacity
operators.doc: `heat_capacity(U, T)`: heat capacity `dU/dT` at constant volume.

operators.name: heat_fd

operators.doc: `heat_fd(alpha, u0, bc_val, t_end, steps)`: finite-difference heat equation solver on the unit domain with uniform Dirichlet boundary value `bc_val`.
