operators.name: heaviside
operators.doc: `heaviside(x)`: Heaviside step function (`0` for `x < 0`, `1/2` at `0`, `1` for `x > 0`).

operators.name: helmholtz_free_energy
operators.doc: `helmholtz_free_energy(U, T, S)`: Helmholtz free energy `A = U - T S`.

operators.name: helmholtz_from_partition
operators.doc: `helmholtz_from_partition(Z, T)`: Helmholtz free energy `-k_B T ln(Z)` from partition function `Z`.

operators.name: henon_orbit
signatures: (Tensor<1, Int>, Int, Float, Float) -> Tensor<2, Float>
operators.doc: Computes an `n`-step orbit of the 2D Henon map `(p0, n, a, b)` starting from `p0`.

operators.name: hermite
operators.doc: `hermite(n, x)`: physicists' Hermite polynomial `H_n(x)`.

operators.name: hermite_differential_equation
operators.doc: `hermite_differential_equation(y, x, n)`: Hermite differential equation `y'' - 2 x y' + 2 n y = 0`.

operators.name: hermite_form
operators.doc: `hermite_form(A)`: Hermite normal form `list(H, U)` of integer matrix `A` with `U A = H`.

operators.name: hermite_rodrigues
operators.doc: `hermite_rodrigues(n, x)`: Rodrigues' formula for Hermite polynomials `(-1)^n exp(x^2) d^n/dx^n exp(-x^2)`.

operators.name: hessian
operators.doc: `hessian(f, vars)`: Hessian matrix `H_{ij} = d^2f/(dx_i dx_j)` of scalar expression `f`.

operators.name: hessian_definiteness
operators.doc: `hessian_definiteness(f, vars, point)`: classifies the Hessian of `f` with respect to `vars` at `point` (e.g. `positive_definite`, `negative_definite`, `indefinite`).

operators.name: hilbert
operators.doc:
`hilbert(n)` constructs the `n × n` Hilbert matrix.

With zero-based row and column indices its entries are `H_{ij} = 1 / (i + j + 1)`.
The entries are exact rational numbers.

operators.name: hilbert_transform
operators.doc: `hilbert_transform(f, x, y)`: symbolic Hilbert transform `(1/pi) PV int_{-oo}^{oo} f(x)/(y - x) dx`.

operators.name: hill_eigen
operators.doc: `hill_eigen(n, L, harmonics, potential_samples...)`: the `n`-th periodic Sturm-Liouville eigenvalue in ascending order. Uses 1–64 harmonics and at least eight finite, equally spaced potential samples on `[0, L)`.

operators.name: hill_mode
operators.doc: `hill_mode(n, x, L, harmonics, potential_samples...)`: the `n`-th normalized periodic eigenfunction at offset `x` from the start of the period. Shares the Fourier-Galerkin decomposition with `hill_eigen`.

operators.name: holonomic_equal
operators.doc: `holonomic_equal(f, g, x)`: decides whether holonomic expressions `f(x)` and `g(x)` are identically equal (`true` or `false`).

operators.name: holonomic_ode
operators.doc: `holonomic_ode(f, x)`: finds a linear homogeneous ODE annihilator for holonomic expression `f` in `x`, returned as a list of polynomial coefficients.

operators.name: holonomic_recurrence
operators.doc: `holonomic_recurrence(f, x, n)`: finds a linear recurrence relation for the Taylor coefficients of `f(x)` in index `n`, returned as `[shift, poly]` pairs.

operators.name: holonomic_series
operators.doc: `holonomic_series(f, x, k)` computes the Taylor terms of `f` at zero in `x` with degree below `k`.

operators.name: holonomic_zero
operators.doc: `holonomic_zero(f, x)`: decides whether holonomic expression `f(x)` is identically zero (`true` or `false`).

operators.name: holt_winters
signatures: (Tensor<1, Real>, Int, Real, Real, Real) -> { fitted: Tensor<1, Real>, level: Tensor<1, Real>, trend: Tensor<1, Real>, season: Tensor<1, Real>, sse: Real }
operators.doc:
`holt_winters(x, season, alpha, beta, gamma)`: `list(fitted, level, trend, season, sse)` of additive Holt–Winters smoothing.

Holt–Winters smoothing with an additive seasonal component.

The recursion is
`l_t = α(y_t - s_{t-m}) + (1-α)(l_{t-1} + b_{t-1})`,
`b_t = β(l_t - l_{t-1}) + (1-β)b_{t-1}` and
`s_t = γ(y_t - l_{t-1} - b_{t-1}) + (1-γ)s_{t-m}`, with the first two
seasons used for the starting values.

# Errors
Returns a lowercase message when the seasonal period is zero, the series
covers fewer than two seasons, a value is not finite, or a smoothing
parameter leaves `[0, 1]`.

operators.name: holt_winters_mul
signatures: (Tensor<1, Real>, Int, Real, Real, Real) -> { fitted: Tensor<1, Real>, level: Tensor<1, Real>, trend: Tensor<1, Real>, season: Tensor<1, Real>, sse: Real }
operators.doc:
`holt_winters_mul(x, season, alpha, beta, gamma)`: the multiplicative Holt–Winters form, `list(fitted, level, trend, season, sse)`.

Holt–Winters smoothing with a multiplicative seasonal component.

The recursion is
`l_t = α(y_t / s_{t-m}) + (1-α)(l_{t-1} + b_{t-1})`,
`b_t = β(l_t - l_{t-1}) + (1-β)b_{t-1}` and
`s_t = γ(y_t / (l_{t-1} + b_{t-1})) + (1-γ)s_{t-m}`.

# Errors
Returns a lowercase message when the seasonal period is zero, the series
covers fewer than two seasons, a value is not finite or not strictly
positive, a smoothing parameter leaves `[0, 1]`, or a level or seasonal
index is zero where the recursion divides by it.

operators.name: hooi
signatures: (Tensor<_, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>, Real, Real) -> { _0: Tensor<_, Real>, _1: Tensor<1, Tensor<2, Real>>, _2: Real }
operators.doc:
`hooi(t, ranks, sweeps, tol)`: Tucker approximation of tensor `t` by higher-order orthogonal iteration, returning `list(core, factors, error)`.

Refine a truncated HOSVD using higher-order orthogonal iteration.

Each coordinate step computes the leading singular subspace after
projecting all other modes. Ranks are upper bounds and may be clamped to
the available subspace. Initialization is deterministic HOSVD; HOOI can
converge to a local optimum or stationary point. Inspect `relative_error`
independently from `converged`. Exhausting the sweep budget returns the
best observed approximation with `converged = false`. Residuals near
floating-point roundoff also terminate the iteration.

Input normalization protects intermediate norm calculations at uniformly
small/large scales. No Gram matrices or condition-number squaring are used.
Zero tensors use a rank-one zero core.

# Errors
Non-finite data, empty modes, invalid
ranks/tolerance/budget, SVD failure, or arithmetic overflow return an error.

operators.name: hook_lengths
operators.doc: `hook_lengths(shape)`: Young diagram hook lengths for integer partition `shape`.

operators.name: hosvd
signatures: (Tensor<_, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>) -> { _0: Tensor<_, Real>, _1: Tensor<1, Tensor<2, Real>>, _2: Tensor<1, Tensor<1, Real>> }
operators.doc:
`hosvd(t, ranks)`: truncated higher-order SVD of tensor `t` returning `list(core, factors, singular_values)`.

The higher-order SVD (Tucker decomposition) of a dense tensor.

For each mode the tensor is unfolded to `n_k x prod(rest)`, the leading left
singular vectors of the unfolding become the factor, and the core is the
tensor contracted with every factor. `ranks` may be `None` for the numerical
multilinear rank of the unfoldings (at most `min(n_k, prod(rest))`, and less
when an unfolding is rank deficient in floating point); a requested rank
above that is clamped to it. The decomposition is exact before truncation
and gives `||T - C x U||_F <= sqrt(sum_k sum_{j > r_k} sigma_{k,j}^2)`.

# Errors
Fails when `ranks` does not have one entry per mode, when a requested rank
is zero, when a mode is empty, or when a mode unfolding has no nonzero
singular value.
examples: hosvd(list(list(list(6, -3), list(0, 0), list(2, -1)), list(list(12, -6), list(0, 0), list(4, -2))), list(0, 0, 0))

operators.name: huber_location
operators.doc:
`huber_location(x, k)`: Huber M-estimator of location for `x` with tuning constant `k`.

Huber M-estimator of location with tuning constant `k` (1.345 is the
classical choice), scale fixed to the normalised MAD.

NaNs are ignored. An invalid tuning constant or an empty effective sample
yields NaN. An undefined or zero MAD gives the sample median.

operators.name: hurwitz_zeta
operators.doc:
`hurwitz_zeta(s, q)`: Hurwitz zeta function `sum_{n=0}^infty (n + q)^{-s}`.

Computes the Hurwitz zeta function ζ(s, q) for real s and q.
Defined as Σ_{n=0}^∞ 1/(n+q)^s.

operators.name: hurwitz_zeta_complex
operators.doc:
`hurwitz_zeta_complex(sr, si, ar, ai)`: `list(re, im)` of `zeta(s, a)`.

Complex Hurwitz zeta function `zeta(s, a) = sum_{n>=0} (n + a)^(-s)`
via adaptive Euler-Maclaurin summation.

operators.name: hydrogen_energy
operators.doc: `hydrogen_energy(n)`: hydrogen atom energy level `-hbar^2 / (2 * m_e * a_0^2 * n^2)` for principal quantum number `n`.

operators.name: hydrogen_radial
operators.doc: `hydrogen_radial(n, l, r)`: normalized hydrogenic radial wavefunction `R_nl(r)` expressed in terms of the Bohr radius `a_0`.

operators.name: hydrogen_wavefunction
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc: `hydrogen_wavefunction(n, l, m, r, theta, phi)`: full hydrogen atom eigenfunction `R_nl(r) * Y_l^m(theta, phi)`.

operators.name: hyp0f1_complex
operators.doc:
`hyp0f1_complex(br, bi, zr, zi)`: `list(re, im)` of `0F1(; b; z)`.

Confluent hypergeometric limit function `0F1(; b; z)`.

operators.name: hyp1f1_complex
signatures: (Real, Real, Real, Real, Real, Real) -> Tensor<1, Real>
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
`hyp1f1_complex(ar, ai, br, bi, zr, zi)`: `list(re, im)` of `1F1(a; b; z)`.

Kummer's confluent hypergeometric function `M(a, b, z) = 1F1(a; b; z)`.

All arguments are complex. For `Re z < 0` Kummer's transformation
`M(a, b, z) = e^z M(b - a, b, -z)` is applied so that the dominant
solution is the one being continued.

operators.name: hyp2f1_complex
signatures: (Real, Real, Real, Real, Real, Real, Real, Real) -> Tensor<1, Real>
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
`hyp2f1_complex(ar, ai, br, bi, cr, ci, zr, zi)`: `list(re, im)` of `2F1(a, b; c; z)`.

Gauss hypergeometric function `2F1(a, b; c; z)` for complex parameters
and argument (principal branch, cut along `[1, inf)`; the value on the
cut is the limit from `Im z -> 0+`).

For positive real parameters at `z = 1`, the gamma ratio in
[Gauss's theorem](https://dlmf.nist.gov/15.4.E20) is evaluated in logarithmic
form without forming large gamma values.

operators.name: hyper1f1
operators.doc: `hyper1f1(a, b, z)`: Kummer confluent hypergeometric function `_1F_1(a; b; z)`.

operators.name: hyper2f1
operators.doc: `hyper2f1(a, b, c, z)`: Gauss hypergeometric function `_2F_1(a, b; c; z)`.

operators.name: hyperpfq
operators.doc: `hyperpfq(a_list, b_list, z)`: generalized hypergeometric function `_pF_q(a_1..a_p; b_1..b_q; z)`.

operators.name: ideal_gas_law
operators.doc: `ideal_gas_law(P, V, n, R, T)`: ideal gas equation of state residual `P V - n R T`.

operators.name: ideal_gas_pressure
operators.doc:
`ideal_gas_pressure(n, T, V)`: ideal gas pressure `n R_gas T / V`.

Ideal gas law: PV = nRT, solving for pressure.

# Arguments
* `n` - Amount of substance (mol)
* `t` - Temperature (K)
* `v` - Volume (m³)

operators.name: ideal_member
operators.doc: `ideal_member(poly, generators, vars)`: decides whether `poly` belongs to the polynomial ideal generated by `generators` over `vars` (`true` or `false`).
examples: ideal_member(x^3 - x*y^2, list(x^2 - y^2), list(x, y))

operators.name: identity
operators.doc:
`identity(n)`: `n x n` identity matrix `I_n`.

Identity matrix of size `n`.

operators.name: idwt
signatures: (Tensor<1, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>, Symbol) -> Tensor<1, Real>
operators.doc:
`idwt(approx, detail, wavelet)`: single-level inverse discrete wavelet transform.

Inverse of [`dwt`] (exact up to rounding).

[`WaveletError::Shape`] when the two coefficient lists differ in length or are empty.

operators.name: idwt2
signatures: (Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>, Symbol) -> Tensor<2, Real>
operators.doc:
`idwt2(ll, lh, hl, hh, wavelet)`: single-level 2D inverse discrete wavelet transform from four sub-bands.

Inverse of [`dwt2`]: `rows` and `cols` are the shape of the original array.

# Errors
[`WaveletError::Shape`] when the packed array does not have the expected
`(2*ra) x (2*ca)` size, or when a column or row transform fails.

operators.name: iff

operators.name: ifft_abs

operators.name: ifft_im

operators.name: ifft_re

operators.name: ifs_generate

operators.name: iid_mean

operators.name: iid_sum

operators.name: im

operators.name: implies

operators.name: inclusion_exclusion
operators.doc: `inclusion_exclusion(levels)`: alternating sum `sum_k (-1)^k levels[k]` for inclusion-exclusion counting.

operators.name: incomplete_beta_complex
signatures: (Real, Real, Real, Real, Real, Real) -> Tensor<1, Real>
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
`incomplete_beta_complex(ar, ai, br, bi, zr, zi)`: `list(re, im)` of `B_z(a, b)`.

Incomplete beta function `B_z(a, b) = (z^a / a) * 2F1(a, 1 - b; a + 1; z)`.

operators.name: indefinite_product
operators.doc:
`indefinite_product(f, k)`: symbolic indefinite product `P(k)` satisfying `P(k+1)/P(k) = f(k)`.

`P(k)` with `P(k + 1) / P(k) = f(k)`, checked.

operators.name: indefinite_sum
operators.doc:
`indefinite_sum(f, k)`: symbolic indefinite sum `T(k)` satisfying `T(k+1) - T(k) = f(k)`.

`T(k)` with `T(k + 1) - T(k) = f(k)`, checked.

operators.name: induced_subgraph
operators.doc: Returns the subgraph of `g` induced by the vertex list `vs`.

operators.name: initial_value_laplace
operators.doc: `initial_value_laplace(F, s)`: applies the Laplace initial-value theorem `lim_{s->oo} s * F(s)`.

operators.name: initial_value_z
operators.doc: `initial_value_z(F, z)`: applies the Z-transform initial-value theorem `lim_{z->oo} F(z)`.

operators.name: inner_product
operators.doc: `inner_product(f, g, x, a, b)`: inner product `<f, g> = int_a^b conj(f) g dx`.

operators.name: integral
operators.doc: `integral(f, x)`: symbolic indefinite integral (antiderivative) of `f` with respect to `x`.

operators.name: integrate_form
operators.doc: `integrate_form(omega, vars, M)`: integral `int_M omega` of differential form `omega(vars)` over cell or chain `M`.

operators.name: interleave
operators.doc:
Applies block interleaving of depth `depth` to byte list `data`.

Interleaves data to spread burst errors across multiple codewords.

This technique helps in correcting burst errors by distributing consecutive
symbols across different codewords.

# Arguments
* `data` - The data to interleave.
* `depth` - The interleaving depth (number of codewords to spread across).

# Returns
The interleaved data.

operators.name: internal_energy_from_partition
operators.doc: `internal_energy_from_partition(Z, T)`: internal energy `k_B T^2 d(ln Z)/dT` from partition function `Z`.

operators.name: interpolate
operators.doc: `interpolate(xs, ys, x)`: evaluate the Lagrange interpolating polynomial through `(xs, ys)` at `x`.

operators.name: invariant_factors
operators.doc: `invariant_factors(A)`: invariant factors (diagonal of Smith normal form) of integer matrix `A`.

operators.name: inverse
operators.doc:
`inverse(A)`: multiplicative inverse `A^{-1}` of square invertible matrix `A`.

Inverse of a square matrix through LU solves.

operators.name: inverse_erfc
operators.doc:
`inverse_erfc(x)`: inverse complementary error function solving `erfc(y) = x`.

Returns `y` such that `erfc(y) = p` for `0 < p < 2`.
The support endpoints return signed infinities. Inputs outside `[0, 2]`
return NaN. Refinement in the far tail uses a logarithmic residual.

operators.name: inverse_fourier
operators.doc: `inverse_fourier(F, omega, t)`: inverse Fourier transform recovering `f(t)` from `F(omega)`.

operators.name: inverse_laplace
operators.doc: `inverse_laplace(F, s, t)`: inverse Laplace transform recovering `f(t)` from `F(s)`.

operators.name: inverse_mellin_transform
operators.doc:
`inverse_mellin_transform(F, s, x)`: symbolic inverse Mellin transform.

Numerical inverse Mellin transform
$f(x) = \frac{1}{2\pi i} \int_{c - i T}^{c + i T} x^{-s} F(s) \, ds$.

operators.name: inverse_wavelet_packet
operators.doc:
`inverse_wavelet_packet(bands, wavelet)`: reconstruct the signal from the equal-width leaf bands of `wavelet_packet`.

Reconstructs a signal from the complete leaf level of [`wavelet_packet`].

# Errors
[`WaveletError::Shape`] when the number of bands is not a power of two,
their lengths differ, or they are empty.

operators.name: inverse_ztransform
operators.doc: `inverse_ztransform(F, z, n)`: inverse Z-transform recovering sequence `f(n)` from `F(z)`.

operators.name: inversions
operators.doc: `inversions(perm)`: number of inversions `(i < j, perm[i] > perm[j])` in permutation `perm`.

operators.name: invmod
operators.doc: `invmod(x, m)`: modular multiplicative inverse `x^-1 mod m` for positive `m` when `gcd(x, m) = 1`.

operators.name: involutions
operators.doc: `involutions(n)`: `n`-th telephone number, counting involutions (self-inverse permutations) on `n` elements.

operators.name: iqr
operators.doc:
`iqr(xs)`: interquartile range `Q3 - Q1` of list `xs`.

Computes the Interquartile Range (IQR) = Q3 - Q1.

operators.name: iroot
operators.doc: `iroot(n, k)`: integer `k`-th root `floor(n^(1/k))` for `n >= 0` and `k >= 1`.

operators.name: irrep_weights
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Int>) -> Tensor<1, { _0: Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, _1: Dyn<term> }>
operators.doc: `irrep_weights(T, hw)`: dominant weights with multiplicities `list(list(w, m), ...)` of irrep `V(hw)` of type `T`.

operators.name: is_attracting_fixed_point
operators.doc: `is_attracting_fixed_point(f, z, z0)`: returns `1` if `f(z0) = z0` and `|f'(z0)| < 1`, `0` otherwise.

operators.name: is_concave
operators.doc: `is_concave(f, vars)`: tests whether `f` is concave in `vars` via Hessian negative semidefiniteness.

operators.name: is_conformal_at
operators.doc: `is_conformal_at(f, z, z0)`: returns `1` if holomorphic `f` has `f'(z0) != 0`, `0` if `f'(z0) == 0`.

operators.name: is_convex
operators.doc: `is_convex(f, vars)`: tests whether `f` is convex in `vars` via Hessian positive semidefiniteness.

operators.name: is_entire
operators.doc: `is_entire(f, z)`: `true` if `f(z)` is holomorphic on all of `C` with no poles or branch cuts.

operators.name: is_inside_contour
operators.doc: `is_inside_contour(p, C)`: `true` if point `p` lies strictly inside contour `C`, `false` otherwise.

operators.name: is_irreducible_mod
operators.doc: Tests whether a polynomial expression `f` in variable `x` is irreducible modulo prime `p`.

operators.name: is_killing
signatures: (Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Tensor<2, Int>, Tensor<1, Symbol>) -> Bool
operators.doc: `is_killing(xi, g, vars)`: `true` if vector field `xi` is a Killing field (`L_xi g = 0`) of metric `g(vars)`.
examples: is_killing(list(x, y), list(list(1, 0), list(0, 1)), list(x, y))
is_killing(list(-y, x), list(list(1, 0), list(0, 1)), list(x, y))

operators.name: is_lie_algebra
operators.doc: `is_lie_algebra(basis[, coords])`: `true` if `span(basis)` is closed under the Lie bracket and satisfies the Jacobi identity.

operators.name: is_meromorphic
operators.doc: `is_meromorphic(f, z)`: `true` if `f(z)` is meromorphic on `C` (holomorphic away from isolated poles, no branch cuts).

operators.name: is_orthogonal
operators.doc:
`is_orthogonal(A)`: returns `1` if `A^T A = I` and `0` otherwise.

Checks if two vectors are orthogonal.

# Errors
Returns an error if the vectors have different lengths.

operators.name: is_positive_definite
operators.doc: `is_positive_definite(A)`: returns `1` if `A` is symmetric positive definite and `0` otherwise.

operators.name: is_square
operators.doc: `is_square(n)`: `true` if `n` is a perfect square (`n = k^2`), `false` otherwise.

operators.name: is_squarefree
operators.doc: `is_squarefree(n)`: `true` if `n` is divisible by no square of a prime, `false` otherwise.

operators.name: is_symmetric
operators.doc:
`is_symmetric(A)`: returns `1` if `A = A^T` and `0` otherwise.

Checks if the sparse matrix is symmetric ($A = A^T$).

operators.name: isoperimetric
operators.doc: `isoperimetric(L, G, y, x, lam)`: computes the constrained Euler-Lagrange expression `euler_lagrange(L + lam * G, y, x)` with Lagrange multiplier `lam`.

operators.name: isprime
operators.doc: `isprime(n)`: `true` if integer `n` is prime, `false` otherwise.

operators.name: isqrt
operators.doc:
`isqrt(n)`: integer square root `floor(sqrt(n))` for `n >= 0`.

Floor of the square root of `n`, exact for all `u64`.

operators.name: jacobi
operators.doc: `jacobi(x, n)`: Jacobi symbol `(x / n)` for odd positive integer `n`.

operators.name: jacobi_cn_complex
operators.doc:
`jacobi_cn_complex(ur, ui, mr, mi)`: `list(re, im)` of `cn(u | m)`.

Complex Jacobi elliptic functions `(sn(u | m), cn(u | m), dn(u | m))`
via the arithmetic-geometric mean (Landen descending transform).

operators.name: jacobi_dn_complex
operators.doc:
`jacobi_dn_complex(ur, ui, mr, mi)`: `list(re, im)` of `dn(u | m)`.

Complex Jacobi elliptic functions `(sn(u | m), cn(u | m), dn(u | m))`
via the arithmetic-geometric mean (Landen descending transform).

operators.name: jacobi_equation
operators.doc: `jacobi_equation(L, y, x, h)`: computes the Jacobi accessory differential expression for variation `h` around an extremal of Lagrangian `L(x, y, y')`.

operators.name: jacobi_sn_complex
operators.doc:
`jacobi_sn_complex(ur, ui, mr, mi)`: `list(re, im)` of `sn(u | m)`.

Complex Jacobi elliptic functions `(sn(u | m), cn(u | m), dn(u | m))`
via the arithmetic-geometric mean (Landen descending transform).

operators.name: jacobi_theta_complex
signatures: (Real, Real, Real, Real, Real) -> Tensor<1, Real>
operators.doc:
`jacobi_theta_complex(k, zr, zi, qr, qi)`: `list(re, im)` of `theta_k(z, q)`.

Complex Jacobi theta functions `theta_k(z, q)` for `k in 1..=4` and `|q| < 1`.

operators.name: jacobian
operators.doc: `jacobian(F, vars)`: Jacobian matrix `J_{ij} = dF_i/dx_j` of vector field `F`.

operators.name: joint_entropy
operators.doc: `joint_entropy(mat)`: joint Shannon entropy (in nats) of joint probability matrix `mat`.

operators.name: jordan
operators.doc: `jordan(A)`: Jordan canonical form `list(P, J)` with `A = P J P^{-1}`.

operators.name: jordan_blocks
operators.doc: `jordan_blocks(A)`: list of Jordan block sizes and eigenvalues of `A`.

operators.name: joukowsky
operators.doc:
`joukowsky(z)`: Joukowsky conformal map `(z + 1/z) / 2`.

Joukowsky airfoil transformation $J(z) = \frac{1}{2}(z + 1/z)$.

operators.name: julia_escape
operators.doc: Computes the Julia set escape time of `z^2 + c` starting at `z = zr + i*zi` with parameter `c = cr + i*ci` (`max_iter` if bounded).

operators.name: k_B
operators.doc: `k_B`: Boltzmann constant in J/K (exact SI).

operators.name: kalman_filter
signatures: (Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>) -> { filtered: Tensor<2, Real>, loglik: Real }
operators.doc:
`kalman_filter(y, transition, observation, process_cov, noise_cov)`: `list(filtered, loglik)` of a linear Gaussian state-space model from a zero initial state and the unit initial covariance; `y` is a list of observation vectors.

Runs the Kalman filter for a linear Gaussian state-space model

`x_t = F x_{t-1} + w_t` with `w_t ~ N(0, Q)` and
`y_t = H x_t + v_t` with `v_t ~ N(0, R)`, started from
`x_0 ~ N(x0, p0)`.

# Errors
Returns a diagnostic for invalid shapes, non-finite data, nonsymmetric
or indefinite model covariances and an innovation covariance that is not
positive definite. Model covariances may be positive semidefinite.

operators.name: kalman_gain
signatures: (Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>) -> Tensor<2, Real>
operators.doc:
`kalman_gain(a, c, w, v)`: the steady-state Kalman gain of `x+ = a x + w` observed through `c`, with process covariance `w` and noise covariance `v`.

Steady-state Kalman gain from the dual Riccati equation.

`W` is the process-noise covariance and `V` the measurement-noise
covariance. Returns `L = P C^T V^{-1}` where `P` solves
`A P + P A^T - P C^T V^{-1} C P + W = 0`.

# Errors
Returns an error for inconsistent dimensions or a singular `V`.

operators.name: kaplan_meier
signatures: (Tensor<1, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>, Real) -> { times: Tensor<1, Real>, at_risk: Tensor<1, Real>, events: Tensor<1, Real>, survival: Tensor<1, Real>, variance: Tensor<1, Real>, lower: Tensor<1, Real>, upper: Tensor<1, Real> }
operators.doc:
`kaplan_meier(time, event, conf)`: `list(times, at_risk, events, survival, variance, lower, upper)` of the product-limit estimator, with `event` a list of 1 (observed) and 0 (censored) and a `conf` confidence level.

Kaplan-Meier product-limit estimate of the survival function.

`time` holds the observed times and `event` is true when the observation
ended in the event of interest and false when it was censored. The inputs
are not modified; the estimate is computed on an internal sorted copy.
`conf` is the two-sided confidence level and must lie strictly between 0
and 1.

# Errors
Returns an error for empty or mismatched inputs, non-finite times, a
confidence level outside `(0, 1)`, or a sample in which every observation
is censored.

operators.name: kde
operators.doc: `kde(sample, x, h)`: Gaussian kernel density estimate of `sample` at `x` with bandwidth `h`.

operators.name: kei
operators.doc: `kei(n, x)`: Kelvin function `kei_n(x)` of integer order `n`.

operators.name: ker
operators.doc: `ker(n, x)`: Kelvin function `ker_n(x)` of integer order `n`.

operators.name: killing_form
operators.doc: `killing_form(basis[, coords])`: Killing form matrix `K_ab = tr(ad_a ad_b)` of the Lie algebra spanned by `basis`.

operators.name: killing_tensor
signatures: (Tensor<1, Symbol>, Tensor<2, Int>, Tensor<1, Symbol>) -> Tensor<2, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: `killing_tensor(xi, g, vars)`: Lie derivative `(L_xi g)_ij = nabla_i xi_j + nabla_j xi_i` of metric `g(vars)` along vector `xi`.
examples: killing_tensor(list(x, y), list(list(1, 0), list(0, 1)), list(x, y))

operators.name: kinematics
operators.doc: `kinematics(r, t)`: position, velocity `dr/dt`, and acceleration `d^2r/dt^2` as `list(r, v, a)`.

operators.name: kinetic_energy
operators.doc:
`kinetic_energy(m, v)`: translational kinetic energy `(1/2) m v^2`.

Kinetic energy `½ vᵀ M v` with the consistent mass matrix.

operators.name: kinetic_operator
operators.doc: `kinetic_operator(m, x)`: 1D kinetic energy operator `-(hbar^2 / (2 m)) d^2/dx^2`.

operators.name: kkt_minimum
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Tensor<1, Symbol>) -> { _0: Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, _1: Dyn<term> }
operators.doc: `kkt_minimum(f, constraints, vars)`: returns the KKT candidate point minimizing `f` subject to `constraints`.

operators.name: kkt_points
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Tensor<1, Symbol>) -> Tensor<1, { _0: Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, _1: Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, _2: Dyn<term> }>
operators.doc: `kkt_points(f, constraints, vars)`: enumerates Karush-Kuhn-Tucker candidate points and multipliers for inequality-constrained optimization.
examples: kkt_points(x^2 + y^2, list(ge(2, x + y)), list(x, y))

operators.name: kl_divergence
operators.doc: `kl_divergence(p, q)`: Kullback-Leibler divergence `D_KL(P || Q) = sum p_i ln(p_i / q_i)` from `q` to `p`.

operators.name: klein_four_group
operators.doc: Constructs the Klein four-group `V_4` on elements `e, a, b, c`.

operators.name: klein_gordon_equation
operators.doc: `klein_gordon_equation(phi, m, x)`: residual `(partial_mu partial^mu + m^2) phi` of the Klein-Gordon equation in natural units.

operators.name: klein_j_complex
operators.doc:
`klein_j_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `j(tau)`.

Klein modular j-invariant `j(tau)` on the upper half-plane `Im(tau) > 0`.

operators.name: knuth_bendix
signatures: () -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>> with 0... x Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: `knuth_bendix(equations, vars, [order])`: runs Knuth-Bendix completion on `equations` over `vars` (with optional symbol precedence `order`) and returns a confluent rewrite rule list.
examples: knuth_bendix(list(op(u, x) = x, op(inv(x), x) = u, op(op(x, y), z) = op(x, op(y, z))), list(x, y, z), list(u, op, inv))

operators.name: koebe
operators.doc: `koebe(z)`: Koebe univalent extremal map `z / (1 - z)^2`.

operators.name: kretschmann
operators.doc: `kretschmann(g, vars)`: Kretschmann curvature scalar `R_ijkl R^ijkl` of metric `g` in `vars`.

operators.name: kron
operators.doc: `kron(A, B)`: Kronecker product `A otimes B` of matrices `A` and `B`.

operators.name: kronecker
operators.doc: `kronecker(n)`: Kronecker delta `delta_{n, 0}`, equal to `1` when `n = 0` and `0` for nonzero integers.

operators.name: kronecker_symbol
operators.doc: `kronecker_symbol(a, n)`: Kronecker symbol `(a / n)` for arbitrary integer `n`.

operators.name: kurtosis
operators.doc:
`kurtosis(xs)`: Pearson kurtosis `m4 / m2^2` of list `xs`.

Computes the unbiased sample excess kurtosis `G2` (the estimator used by
Excel's `KURT` and `scipy.stats.kurtosis(fisher=True, bias=False)`); a
normal distribution has expected value 0.

With `g2 = m4 / m2^2 - 3` (central moments divided by `n`),
`G2 = (n - 1) / ((n - 2)(n - 3)) * ((n + 1) g2 + 6)`.

Returns `NaN` for fewer than four points and `0.0` for constant data.

operators.name: kurtosis_of
operators.doc: `kurtosis_of(d)`: excess kurtosis (standardized 4th central moment minus 3) of distribution `d`.

operators.name: l2_distance
operators.doc: `l2_distance(f, g, x, a, b)`: `L^2` distance `||f - g||_2` on `[a, b]`.

operators.name: l2_norm
operators.doc: `l2_norm(f, x, a, b)`: `L^2` norm `sqrt(int_a^b |f|^2 dx)`.

operators.name: lagrangian
operators.doc: `lagrangian(T, V)`: classical Lagrangian `L = T - V` from kinetic energy `T` and potential energy `V`.

operators.name: laguerre
operators.doc: `laguerre(n, x)`: Laguerre polynomial `L_n(x)`.

operators.name: laguerre_differential_equation
operators.doc: `laguerre_differential_equation(y, x, n)`: Laguerre differential equation `x y'' + (1 - x) y' + n y = 0`.

operators.name: laguerre_gen
operators.doc: `laguerre_gen(n, alpha, x)`: generalized Laguerre polynomial `L_n^(alpha)(x)`.

operators.name: laguerre_rodrigues
operators.doc: `laguerre_rodrigues(n, x)`: Rodrigues' formula for Laguerre polynomials `(exp(x) / n!) d^n/dx^n (exp(-x) x^n)`.

operators.name: lah
operators.doc: `lah(n, k)`: unsigned Lah number `L(n, k)`, counting partitions of `n` elements into `k` non-empty ordered lists.

operators.name: lambert_w_complex
operators.doc:
`lambert_w_complex(re, im, k)`: `list(re, im)` of branch `k` of the complex Lambert W function solving `w exp(w) = re + i*im`.

The branch `k` of the Lambert W function: the solution of `w e^w = z`
in the strip of branch `k`.

On the negative real axis, a positive zero imaginary part selects the
upper lip and a negative zero selects the lower lip.

`W_0(0) = 0` and `W_k(0) = -∞` for `k != 0`; the branch point `-1/e`
gives `-1`.

operators.name: lambertw
operators.doc: `lambertw(x)`: principal branch `W_0(x)` of the Lambert W function solving `w exp(w) = x`.

operators.name: lambertw_m1
operators.doc: `lambertw_m1(x)`: lower real branch `W_{-1}(x)` of the Lambert W function for `-1/e <= x < 0`.

operators.name: laplace
operators.doc: `laplace(f, t, s)`: unilateral Laplace transform `int_0^oo f(t) * exp(-s*t) dt`.

operators.name: laplace_ball
operators.doc: `laplace_ball(g, r, theta, R)`: harmonic solution of the Dirichlet Laplace equation on a 3D ball of radius `R` with boundary data `g`.

operators.name: laplace_beltrami
operators.doc: `laplace_beltrami(f, g, vars)`: Laplace-Beltrami operator `(1/sqrt|g|) d_i(sqrt|g| g^ij d_j f)` of `f` for metric `g(vars)`.

operators.name: laplace_disk
operators.doc: `laplace_disk(g, r, theta, R)`: harmonic solution of the Dirichlet Laplace equation on a disk of radius `R` with boundary data `g(theta)`.

operators.name: laplace_dist
operators.doc: `laplace_dist(mu, b)`: Laplace distribution with location `mu` and scale `b`.

operators.name: laplacian
operators.doc:
`laplacian(f, vars)` sums the second partial derivatives of a scalar expression `f`.

Pass the variables as `list(x_1, ..., x_n)`. The operator differentiates twice with respect to each variable.

For example, `laplacian(x^2 + y^2, list(x, y))` returns `4`.

operators.name: laplacian_in
operators.doc: `laplacian_in(f, sys, vars)`: scalar Laplacian of `f` in orthogonal coordinate system `sys(vars)`.

operators.name: lattice_volume
operators.doc: `lattice_volume(a1, a2, a3)`: primitive cell volume `a1 . (a2 x a3)` from basis vectors.

operators.name: laurent
operators.doc: `laurent(f, x, a, n)`: Laurent/Puiseux series expansion of `f` about `x = a` up to order `n`.

operators.name: laurent_analytic_part
operators.doc: `laurent_analytic_part(f, z, a, order)`: non-negative-power terms of the Laurent series of `f(z)` at `z = a`.

operators.name: laurent_principal_part
operators.doc: `laurent_principal_part(f, z, a, order)`: negative-power terms of the Laurent series of `f(z)` at `z = a`.

operators.name: lcm
operators.doc:
`lcm(a, b)`: least common multiple of integers `a` and `b`.

Computes the least common multiple (LCM) of two numbers.

Returns `0` when either argument is `0`, and `u64::MAX` when the true
value does not fit (use [`checked_lcm`] to tell the two apart).

operators.name: ldl
operators.doc: `ldl(A)`: LDL^T factorization `list(L, D)` of symmetric matrix `A`.

operators.name: le
operators.doc: `le(a, b)`: less-than-or-equal comparison `a <= b`.

operators.name: leading_coeff
operators.doc: `leading_coeff(poly, vars, [order])`: returns the leading coefficient of multivariate `poly` over `vars` under monomial `order`.

operators.name: leading_monomial
operators.doc: `leading_monomial(poly, vars, [order])`: returns the leading monomial of multivariate `poly` over `vars` under monomial `order`.

operators.name: leading_term
operators.doc: `leading_term(poly, vars, [order])`: returns the leading term of multivariate `poly` over `vars` under monomial `order`.

operators.name: left_nullspace
operators.doc: `left_nullspace(A)`: basis of the left nullspace `{y : y^T A = 0}` of matrix `A`.

operators.name: legendre
operators.doc: `legendre(n, x)`: Legendre polynomial `P_n(x)` of degree `n`.

operators.name: legendre_condition
operators.doc: `legendre_condition(L, y, x)`: computes the second partial derivative `d^2 L / d(y')^2` used in the Legendre necessary condition for an extremum.

operators.name: legendre_differential_equation
operators.doc: `legendre_differential_equation(y, x, n)`: Legendre differential equation `(1 - x^2) y'' - 2 x y' + n (n + 1) y = 0`.

operators.name: legendre_rodrigues
operators.doc: `legendre_rodrigues(n, x)`: Rodrigues' formula for Legendre polynomials `(1 / (2^n n!)) d^n/dx^n (x^2 - 1)^n`.

operators.name: legendre_symbol
operators.doc:
`legendre_symbol(a, p)`: Legendre symbol `(a / p)` for odd prime `p`.

Computes the Legendre symbol $\left(\frac{a}{p}\right)$ for an odd prime `p`.

Returns `0` if `p < 3`, `p` is composite, or `p` divides `a`; `1` if `a` is
a quadratic residue modulo `p`; and `-1` if `a` is a quadratic non-residue.

operators.name: legendre_transform
operators.doc: `legendre_transform(f, x, p)`: computes the Legendre-Fenchel transform `sup_x (p * x - f(x))`.

operators.name: lerch
operators.doc:
`lerch(z, s, a)`: Lerch transcendent `Phi(z, s, a) = sum_{n=0}^infty z^n / (n + a)^s`.

The Lerch transcendent `Φ(z, s, a) = Σ_{k=0}^∞ z^k / (k+a)^s` for real
`s`, real `a > 0` and `z < 1` (the standard range).

For `|z| <= 9/10` the defining series is summed directly. For `s > 0` and
`|z| > 9/10` the Euler integral
`Φ = 1/Γ(s) ∫_0^∞ t^(s-1) e^(-a t)/(1 - z e^(-t)) dt`
is evaluated by double-exponential quadrature, which covers `z < 0`
(`|z| > 1` included) as well as `z ↑ 1`. Non-positive integer `s` use the
rational form `(z d/dz + a)^n 1/(1-z)`. Non-integer orders in
`[-15.5, 0)` use an Euler integral with the order shifted above zero.
At `z = 1` the analytic continuation `ζ(s, a)` is returned. Outside
the implemented range the result is `NaN`.

operators.name: log_rank
signatures: (Tensor<1, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>) -> { chi2: Real, p_value: Real, observed: Tensor<1, Real>, expected: Tensor<1, Real> }
operators.doc:
`log_rank(time_a, event_a, time_b, event_b)`: `list(chi2, p_value, observed, expected)` of the two-sample log-rank test.

Log-rank test comparing the survival curves of two independent groups.

At every distinct event time the observed number of events in the first
group is compared with its hypergeometric expectation over the pooled risk
set; the squared standardised difference is referred to a chi-square
distribution with one degree of freedom.

# Errors
Returns an error for empty or mismatched inputs, non-finite times, or when
the pooled risk sets carry no variance (for example when a single subject
is at risk at every event time).

operators.name: logistic_bifurcation
signatures: (Float, Float, Int, Int, Int) -> Tensor<2, Float>
operators.doc:
Samples the logistic map bifurcation diagram over `[r_min, r_max]` in `steps` increments, discarding `transient` steps and returning `keep` `list(r, x)` points per `r`.

Generates data for a bifurcation diagram of the logistic map.

For each value of r, the map is iterated and the final values after
discarding transients are recorded.

# Arguments
* `r_range` - The range of r values `(r_min, r_max)`.
* `num_r_values` - Number of r values to sample.
* `transient` - Number of initial iterations to discard.
* `num_points` - Number of points to record after transient.
* `x0` - Initial x value.

# Returns
A `Vec` of `(r, x)` pairs for plotting the bifurcation diagram.

parameters and complex `z` (principal branch; see the module

operators.doc: `meijerg(m, n, list(a), list(b), z)`: Meijer G-function `G^{m,n}_{p,q}(z | a; b)`.

operators.name: mellin_barnes_to_meijer_g
operators.doc: `mellin_barnes_to_meijer_g(num_plus, num_minus, den_plus, den_minus, z)`: reduces a Mellin–Barnes Gamma-product integral to `meijer_g`.

operators.name: mellin_transform
operators.doc:
`mellin_transform(f, x, s)`: symbolic Mellin transform `int_0^oo x^(s-1) f(x) dx`.

Numerical Mellin transform `\mathcal{M}[f](s) = \int_0^\infty x^{s-1} f(x) \, dx`
via the substitution `x = e^u` (`u \in [-L, L]`).

operators.name: mesh_normals
operators.doc: Computes unit face normals for mesh `(vertices, faces)` from the first three vertices of each face.

operators.name: mesh_transform
operators.doc: Transforms a list of 3D mesh `vertices` by 4x4 homogeneous matrix `M` with perspective divide.

operators.name: mesh_triangulate
operators.doc: Triangulates polygonal mesh `faces` into triangles using a triangle fan from each face's first vertex.

operators.name: metric_geodesic_acceleration
signatures: (Tensor<2, Dyn<term>>, Tensor<1, Symbol>, Tensor<1, Int>) -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: `metric_geodesic_acceleration(g, vars, v)`: geodesic acceleration `-Gamma^k_ij v^i v^j` for metric `g(vars)` and velocity `v`.
examples: metric_geodesic_acceleration(list(list(1, 0), list(0, sin(t)^2)), list(t, p), list(0, 1))
metric_geodesic_acceleration(list(list(1, 0), list(0, sin(t)^2)), list(t, p), list(1, 0))

operators.name: mgf
operators.doc: `mgf(d, t)`: moment-generating function `M_X(t) = E[exp(t X)]` of distribution `d` at argument `t`.

operators.name: milp_solve
signatures: (Tensor<1, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<1, Symbol>, Tensor<1, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>, Int) -> { x: Tensor<1, Real>, objective: Real, nodes: Real, gap: Real, optimal: Real }
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
`milp_solve(c, a, rel, b, bounds, kinds, max_nodes)`: `list(x, objective, nodes, gap, optimal)` of a mixed-integer linear program by branch and bound; `kinds` is a list of `continuous`, `integer` or `binary`.

Solves a mixed-integer linear program.

# Errors
Returns `"infeasible"` when the root relaxation is infeasible (or when no
integer-feasible point exists), `"unbounded"` when a relaxation is
unbounded, and a descriptive string for dimension or finiteness errors.

operators.name: min_of
operators.doc: `min_of(xs)`: minimum element of list `xs`.

operators.name: minkowski_dot
operators.doc: `minkowski_dot(a, b)`: Minkowski inner product `a^mu b_mu` with signature `(+1, -1, -1, -1)`.

operators.name: minkowski_metric
operators.doc: `minkowski_metric`: 4x4 Minkowski metric tensor `diag(1, -1, -1, -1)`.

operators.name: minpoly
operators.doc: `minpoly(A, x)`: minimal polynomial of square matrix `A` in variable `x`.

operators.name: minres_solve
signatures: (Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>, Real) -> Tensor<1, Real>
operators.doc: `minres_solve(a, b, tol)`: solve symmetric linear system `A x = b` by MINRES to relative tolerance `tol`.

operators.name: mittag_leffler_complex
signatures: (Real, Real, Real, Real, Real, Real) -> Tensor<1, Real>
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
`mittag_leffler_complex(ar, ai, br, bi, zr, zi)`: `list(re, im)` of `E_{alpha, beta}(z)`.

Complex Mittag-Leffler function `E_{alpha, beta}(z) = sum_{k>=0} z^k / Gamma(alpha * k + beta)`
for `Re(alpha) > 0`.

operators.name: mittag_leffler_expansion
operators.doc: `mittag_leffler_expansion(f, z)`: Mittag-Leffler principal-part expansion over the poles of rational `f(z)`.

operators.name: mobius
operators.doc:
`mobius(n)`: Möbius function `mu(n)` (`0` if not squarefree, `(-1)^omega(n)` otherwise).

Möbius function `μ(n)`, extended to return zero for `n <= 0`.

operators.name: mobius_apply
operators.doc: `mobius_apply(M, z)`: apply Möbius transformation matrix `M = list(list(a, b), list(c, d))` to `z`.

operators.name: mobius_compose
operators.doc: `mobius_compose(M, N)`: composition of two Möbius transformation matrices `M` and `N`.

operators.name: mobius_inverse
operators.doc: `mobius_inverse(M)`: inverse Möbius transformation matrix of `M`.

operators.name: mod
operators.doc: `mod(x, m)`: least non-negative residue of `x` modulo `|m|` for `m != 0`.

operators.name: mode
operators.doc:
`mode(xs)`: most frequent value (mode) of list `xs`.

Finds the mode (most frequent value) of a slice of data.
For continuous data, rounds to a specified number of decimal places.
Returns None if no mode exists (all values unique or empty).

operators.name: mode_of
operators.doc: `mode_of(d)`: mode (point of maximum density or probability mass) of distribution `d`.

operators.name: modular_lambda_complex
operators.doc:
`modular_lambda_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `lambda(tau)`.

Modular lambda function `lambda(tau) = (theta_2(0, q) / theta_3(0, q))^4`, `q = exp(i*pi*tau)`.

operators.name: molecule_decomposition
signatures: () -> Tensor<2, Dyn<term>> with 0... x Tensor<2, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: Decomposes the 3N nuclear degrees of freedom of molecule `atoms` into `list(irrep, n_3N, n_trans, n_rot, n_vib)` rows.

operators.name: molecule_point_group
operators.doc: Identifies the Schoenflies point group symbol of molecule `atoms` (including `Cinfv` and `Dinfh` for linear molecules).

operators.name: molecule_spectroscopy
signatures: () -> Tensor<1, { _0: Symbol, _1: Dyn<term>, _2: Bool, _3: Bool }> with 0... x Tensor<2, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: Returns vibrational spectroscopy activity of molecule `atoms` as `list(irrep, multiplicity, ir_active, raman_active)`.

operators.name: molecule_symmetry_operations
signatures: () -> Tensor<3, Dyn<term>> with 0... x Tensor<2, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: Finds the 3x3 symmetry operation matrices of molecule `atoms` (optional trailing tolerance, default `1e-3`).

operators.name: molecule_vibrations
operators.doc: Computes the vibrational representation `Gamma_vib = Gamma_3N - Gamma_trans - Gamma_rot` of molecule `atoms` as a sum of irreps.

operators.name: molecule_vibrations_table
signatures: () -> Tensor<2, Dyn<term>> with 0... x Tensor<2, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: Returns the vibrational modes of molecule `atoms` as `list(list(irrep, multiplicity), ...)`.

operators.name: moment
operators.doc: `moment(xs, k)`: `k`-th central moment `(1/n) sum (x_i - mean)^k` of list `xs`.

operators.name: moment_of
operators.doc: `moment_of(d, k)`: `k`-th raw moment `E[X^k]` of distribution `d`.

operators.name: moment_of_inertia_point_mass
operators.doc: `moment_of_inertia_point_mass(m, r)`: moment of inertia `m r^2` of a point mass at distance `r`.

operators.name: momentum
operators.doc: `momentum(m, v)`: linear momentum `p = m * v`.

operators.name: momentum_operator
operators.doc: `momentum_operator(x)`: 1D momentum operator `-i hbar d/dx`.

operators.name: moran_dimension
operators.doc: Numerically solves the Moran equation `sum r_i^D = 1` by bisection for a list of contraction ratios.

operators.name: motzkin
operators.doc: `motzkin(n)`: `n`-th Motzkin number, counting non-intersecting chords on `n` points on a circle.

operators.name: mp_add
operators.doc:
`mp_add(a, b, digits)`: the sum of two decimal numbers, to `digits` significant digits.

Applies one of the four arithmetic operations to two decimal literals.

`operation` is `add`, `sub`, `mul` or `div`.

# Errors
Fails on malformed text, division by zero, an unknown operation, or when an
exponent leaves the range.

operators.name: mp_ball
operators.doc:
`mp_ball(expr, digits)`: `list(low, high)`, a rigorous enclosure of `expr` at `digits` significant digits.

Evaluates decimal expression `text` to a rigorous enclosure at `digits`
significant digits, rounded outward, as `(low, high)`.

# Errors
Fails on malformed text, a domain error, or when an exponent leaves the
range.

operators.name: mp_compare
operators.doc:
`mp_compare(a, b)`: `-1`, `0` or `1` as the decimal `a` is below, equal to or above `b`, compared exactly.

Compares two decimal literals: `-1`, `0` or `1`.

# Errors
Fails on malformed text or when an exponent leaves the range.

operators.name: mp_complex_ball
operators.doc:
`mp_complex_ball(expr, digits)`: `list(list(re_lo, re_hi), list(im_lo, im_hi))`, a rigorous complex enclosure of `expr` at `digits` significant digits.

Evaluates a complex expression `text` to a rigorous enclosure at `digits`
significant decimal digits, returning `((re_lo, re_hi), (im_lo, im_hi))`.

# Errors
Fails on syntax errors, branch cuts/poles, or exponent overflow.

operators.name: mp_complex_eval
operators.doc:
`mp_complex_eval(expr, digits)`: `list(re, im)` of the complex expression `expr` to `digits` significant decimal digits.

Evaluates a complex expression `text` to `digits` significant decimal digits
for both real and imaginary parts, using Ziv's strategy.

# Errors
Fails on syntax errors, branch cuts/poles, or if digits cannot be certified
within [`MAX_BITS`].

operators.name: mp_const
operators.doc:
`mp_const(name, digits)`: the constant `pi`, `e`, `tau`, `ln2`, `sqrt2` or `phi` to `digits` significant decimal digits.

A constant by name, to `digits` significant digits.

# Errors
Fails for an unknown name or when an exponent leaves the range.

operators.name: mp_digits
operators.doc:
`mp_digits(x)`: the number of significant decimal digits the literal `x` carries.

The number of significant decimal digits a literal carries.

# Errors
Fails on malformed text.

operators.name: mp_div
operators.doc:
`mp_div(a, b, digits)`: the quotient of two decimal numbers, to `digits` significant digits.

Applies one of the four arithmetic operations to two decimal literals.

`operation` is `add`, `sub`, `mul` or `div`.

# Errors
Fails on malformed text, division by zero, an unknown operation, or when an
exponent leaves the range.

operators.name: mp_eval
operators.doc:
`mp_eval(expr, digits)`: the value of the expression `expr` to `digits` significant decimal digits, as text, correctly rounded.

Evaluates decimal expression `text` to `digits` significant digits.

Plain decimal literals are rounded directly. Other expressions use
progressively higher precision until the enclosure pins the digits.

# Errors
Fails on malformed text, a domain error, or when the digits cannot be
pinned within [`MAX_BITS`].

operators.name: mp_from_float
operators.doc:
`mp_from_float(x, digits)`: the decimal expansion of the double `x` to `digits` significant digits; the double is exact, so the digits are its true value.

The exact decimal expansion of an `f64`, to `digits` significant digits.

# Errors
Fails for a non-finite value or when an exponent leaves the range.

operators.name: mp_mul
operators.doc:
`mp_mul(a, b, digits)`: the product of two decimal numbers, to `digits` significant digits.

Applies one of the four arithmetic operations to two decimal literals.

`operation` is `add`, `sub`, `mul` or `div`.

# Errors
Fails on malformed text, division by zero, an unknown operation, or when an
exponent leaves the range.

operators.name: mp_round
operators.doc:
`mp_round(x, digits)`: the decimal `x` rounded to `digits` significant digits, nearest even.

Rounds decimal text to `digits` significant digits in `mode`.

# Errors
Fails on malformed text or when an exponent leaves the range.

operators.name: mp_round_mode
operators.doc:
`mp_round_mode(x, digits, mode)`: `x` rounded to `digits` significant digits in `mode` (`nearest`, `zero`, `away`, `up`, `down`).

Rounds decimal text to `digits` significant digits in `mode`.

# Errors
Fails on malformed text or when an exponent leaves the range.

operators.name: mp_sub
operators.doc:
`mp_sub(a, b, digits)`: the difference of two decimal numbers, to `digits` significant digits.

Applies one of the four arithmetic operations to two decimal literals.

`operation` is `add`, `sub`, `mul` or `div`.

# Errors
Fails on malformed text, division by zero, an unknown operation, or when an
exponent leaves the range.

operators.name: mp_to_float
operators.doc:
`mp_to_float(x)`: the decimal `x` narrowed to a double, correctly rounded (no double rounding through an intermediate).

The correctly rounded `f64` value of a decimal literal.

# Errors
Fails on malformed text or when an exponent leaves the range.

operators.name: mpc_plan
signatures: (Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>, Int, Tensor<1, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>) -> { u: Tensor<1, Real>, predicted_states: Tensor<2, Real>, objective: Real, iterations: Real }
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
`mpc_plan(a, b, c, d, x0, reference, horizon, q, r)`: `list(u, predicted_states, objective, iterations)` of one receding-horizon step solved as a condensed quadratic program.

Computes one MPC step.

The quadratic program is condensed: the predicted states are eliminated
with the prediction matrices, leaving only the control moves over the
control horizon. Moves beyond the control horizon are held at zero.

# Errors
Returns an error for a continuous model, inconsistent option lengths, or a
failed quadratic program.

operators.name: mpow
operators.doc: `mpow(A, n)`: matrix power `A^n` for integer or rational exponent `n`.

operators.name: mseries
operators.doc: `mseries(f, vars, point, N)`: multivariate series expansion of `f` in `vars` about `point` truncated at total degree `N`.

operators.name: mtaylor
operators.doc: `mtaylor(f, vars, point, N)`: multivariate Taylor polynomial of `f` in `vars` about finite `point` up to total degree `N`.

operators.name: mu_0
operators.doc: `mu_0`: vacuum magnetic permeability in N/A^2.

operators.name: mul
operators.doc:
`mul(a, b, ...)` forms the product of any number of terms and is printed with `*`.

Multiplication is associative and commutative. Numeric operands are multiplied directly.

The empty product is `1`.

operators.name: mult_order
operators.doc: `mult_order(a, n)`: multiplicative order of `a` modulo `n` (smallest `k >= 1` with `a^k = 1 (mod n)`).

operators.name: multibrot_escape
operators.doc: Computes the Multibrot escape time of `z^d + c` for exponent `d` and parameter `c = cr + i*ci` up to `max_iter` iterations.

operators.name: multinomial
operators.doc: `multinomial(ks)`: multinomial coefficient `(sum k_i)! / prod(k_i!)` for a list of non-negative integers `ks`.

operators.name: multiplier
operators.doc: `multiplier(f, z, z0, period)`: symbolic periodic-point multiplier `d/dz (f^{o p})(z) |_{z=z0}`.

operators.name: mutual_information
operators.doc: `mutual_information(mat)`: mutual information `I(X; Y) = H(X) + H(Y) - H(X, Y)` for joint probability matrix `mat`.

operators.name: mv
operators.doc: `mv(sig, terms)`: canonical multivector over metric signature `sig = list(p, q, r)` with `terms = list(list(blade_mask, coeff), ...)`.

operators.name: mv_add
operators.doc: `mv_add(A, B, ...)`: sum of multivectors in the same signature.
examples: mv_add(mv(list(3, 0, 0), list(list(0, a1*b1 + a2*b2 + a3*b3))), mv(list(3, 0, 0), list(list(3, a1*b2 - a2*b1), list(5, a1*b3 - a3*b1), list(6, a2*b3 - a3*b2))))

operators.name: mv_basis
operators.doc: `mv_basis(sig, k)`: `k`-th basis vector `e_k` (1-based) in signature `sig`.

operators.name: mv_blade
operators.doc: `mv_blade(sig, mask, c)`: single-blade multivector `c * e_mask` in signature `sig`.

operators.name: mv_coeff
operators.doc: `mv_coeff(A, mask)`: coefficient of blade `mask` in multivector `A` (0 if absent).

operators.name: mv_pseudoscalar
operators.doc: `mv_pseudoscalar(sig)`: unit pseudoscalar `e_1 ... e_n` of the Clifford algebra with signature `sig`.

operators.name: mv_scalar
operators.doc: `mv_scalar(sig, s)`: scalar multivector with value `s` in Clifford algebra with signature `sig`.

operators.name: mv_scalar_part
operators.doc: `mv_scalar_part(A)`: grade-0 scalar part `<A>_0` of multivector `A`.

operators.name: mv_scale
operators.doc: `mv_scale(c, A)`: multivector `A` scaled by scalar `c`.

operators.name: mv_sub
operators.doc: `mv_sub(A, B)`: difference `A - B` of two multivectors.

operators.name: mv_vector
operators.doc: `mv_vector(sig, coords)`: grade-1 vector multivector from coordinate list `coords` in signature `sig`.

operators.name: narayana
operators.doc: `narayana(n, k)`: Narayana number `N(n, k) = C(n, k) * C(n, k - 1) / n`, counting Dyck paths of semilength `n` with `k` peaks.

operators.name: natural_boundary
operators.doc: `natural_boundary(L, y, x)`: returns the natural boundary expression `canonical_momentum(L, y, x)`.

operators.name: ne
operators.doc: `ne(a, b)`: inequality comparison `a != b`.

operators.name: necklaces
operators.doc: `necklaces(n, k)`: number of distinct `k`-ary necklaces of length `n` under cyclic rotation.

operators.name: neg
operators.doc:
`neg(a)`: the negation `-a`.

Rewritten to `mul(-1, a)` and printed as `-a`.

operators.name: negative_binomial
operators.doc: `negative_binomial(r, p)`: negative binomial distribution for `r` successes with probability `p`.

operators.name: nelson_aalen
signatures: (Tensor<1, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>) -> { times: Tensor<1, Real>, hazard: Tensor<1, Real>, cumulative_hazard: Tensor<1, Real> }
operators.doc:
`nelson_aalen(time, event)`: `list(times, hazard, cumulative_hazard)` of the Nelson–Aalen estimator.

Nelson-Aalen estimate of the cumulative hazard function.

The increment at a time with `d` events among `n` subjects at risk is
`d / n`. The inputs are not modified.

# Errors
Returns an error for empty or mismatched inputs, non-finite times, or a
sample in which every observation is censored.

operators.name: nested_dissection_order
operators.doc:
`nested_dissection_order(adjacency)`: fill-reducing elimination ordering `perm` of a symmetric graph by multilevel nested dissection.

Multilevel nested dissection ordering of the pattern `adj` (see the
module documentation). Returns `perm` with `perm[new] = old`.

operators.name: newton_cg_minimize
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Symbol>, Tensor<1, Int>) -> Tensor<1, Float>
operators.doc: `newton_cg_minimize(f, vars, x0)`: minimiser of `f(vars)` starting from `x0` by trust-region Newton-CG with symbolic gradient and Hessian.

operators.name: newton_fractal_root
operators.doc: Runs Newton's method on polynomial `coeffs` (highest degree first) from `zr + i*zi` up to `max_iter`, returning `list(re, im, iterations)` or `false`.

operators.name: newtons_second_law
operators.doc: `newtons_second_law(m, a)`: net force `F = m * a` for mass `m` and acceleration `a`.

operators.name: nextprime
operators.doc: `nextprime(n)`: smallest prime strictly greater than `n`.

operators.name: nmaximize
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Symbol>, Tensor<1, Float>) -> { _0: Tensor<1, Float>, _1: Float }
operators.doc: `nmaximize(f, vars, start)`: numerically maximizes `f(vars)` from initial point `start` using BFGS with compiled gradient.

operators.name: nmaximize_global
operators.doc: `nmaximize_global(f, vars, bounds)`: numerically finds the global maximum of `f(vars)` over box `bounds`.

operators.name: nminimize
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Symbol>, Tensor<1, Int>) -> { _0: Tensor<1, Float>, _1: Float }
(Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Symbol>, Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>) -> { _0: Tensor<1, Float>, _1: Float }
operators.doc: `nminimize(f, vars, start)`: numerically minimizes `f(vars)` from initial point `start` using BFGS with compiled gradient.
examples: nminimize(100*(y - x^2)^2 + (1 - x)^2, list(x, y), list(-1.2, 1))

operators.name: nminimize_global
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Symbol>, Tensor<2, Int>) -> { _0: Tensor<1, Float>, _1: Float }
operators.doc: `nminimize_global(f, vars, bounds)`: numerically finds the global minimum of `f(vars)` over box `bounds`.
examples: nminimize_global(x^2 + y^2 - 10*cos(2*x*pi) - 10*cos(2*y*pi) + 20, list(x, y), list(list(-5, 5), list(-5, 5)))

operators.name: nnf
operators.doc: `nnf(formula)`: converts propositional `formula` to negation normal form.

operators.name: noether_current
operators.doc: `noether_current(L, u, generator)`: conserved Noether current `list(J^x, J^t)` for Lagrangian `L` and symmetry `generator`.
examples: noether_current(1/2*diff(u(x, t), t)^2 - 1/2*diff(u(x, t), x)^2, u(x, t), list(0, 1, 0))

operators.name: nonlinear_regression
signatures: (Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Symbol>) -> Tensor<2, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: `nonlinear_regression(xs, ys, model, x, params)`: non-linear least-squares fit returning normal equations as a solve request.
examples: nonlinear_regression(list(0, 1), list(1, 2), a*exp(b*x), x, list(a, b))
nonlinear_regression(list(0, 1, 2), list(1, 3, 5), a*x + b, x, list(a, b))

operators.name: norm
operators.doc: `norm(v)`: Euclidean (L2) norm `||v||_2` of vector `v`.

operators.name: normal
operators.doc: `normal(mu, sigma)`: normal (Gaussian) distribution with mean `mu` and standard deviation `sigma`.

operators.name: normal_form
operators.doc: `normal_form(poly, basis, vars)`: reduces `poly` modulo a Groebner `basis` over `vars`.

operators.name: normal_known_sd
operators.doc: `normal_known_sd(sigma)`: inert normal likelihood descriptor with known standard deviation `sigma` for Bayesian updates.

operators.name: normalize
operators.doc: `normalize(v)`: unit vector `v / ||v||_2` in the direction of `v`.

operators.name: normalize_wavefunction
operators.doc: `normalize_wavefunction(psi, x)`: normalizes `psi` by `sqrt(<psi|psi>)` over `x in (-oo, oo)`.

operators.name: not
operators.doc: `not(p)`: logical negation of `p`.

operators.name: nsolve
operators.doc: `nsolve(eq_or_system, var_or_vars, guess)`: numerically finds a root of `eq_or_system` starting from `guess`.

operators.name: nsolve_certified
operators.doc: `nsolve_certified(eq, var, interval)`: computes a certified enclosure for a root of `eq` in `interval` via interval arithmetic.

operators.name: nth_prime
operators.doc: `nth_prime(k)`: the `k`-th prime number (1-based, so `nth_prime(1) = 2`).

operators.name: nullspace
operators.doc: `nullspace(A)`: basis of the kernel `{x : A x = 0}` of matrix `A`.

operators.name: num_ad_forward_gradient
signatures: (String, Tensor<1, String>, Tensor<1, Float>) -> Tensor<1, Float>
operators.doc: Forward-mode gradient of an elementary scalar expression at a finite point. Variable order determines output order; no step-size parameter is used.

operators.name: num_ad_gradient_scaled
signatures: (String, Tensor<1, String>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Float[_], Float[_], String) -> Tensor<1, Float[_]>
operators.doc:
Exact forward/reverse AD of a dimensionless expression in normalized coordinates x/coordinate_scale. value_scale assigns physical output units. Returns physical gradient in output/coordinate units. Homogeneous physical coordinates; mode is forward or reverse.

Reverse-mode gradient of an elementary scalar expression in one reverse sweep.

# Errors
As [`forward_gradient`].

operators.name: num_ad_hessian
signatures: (String, Tensor<1, String>, Tensor<1, Float>) -> Tensor<2, Float>
operators.doc: Hessian of an elementary scalar expression by the existing hyper-dual tape. Returns a square matrix in variable order, without finite differences.

operators.name: num_ad_hessian_scaled
signatures: (String, Tensor<1, String>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Float[_], Float[_]) -> Tensor<2, Float[_]>
operators.doc:
Exact second-order AD on normalized coordinates, restored to physical output/coordinate-squared units. Expression output is multiplied by value_scale.

Hessian of an elementary scalar expression by the existing hyper-dual tape.
Returns a square matrix in variable order, without finite differences.

operators.name: num_analysis_convergence_levin_condition_number
operators.doc:
Native convergence levin_condition_number; normalized dimensionless arguments unless the declared contract preserves measured signal units. Enum arguments use exact Rust variant names.

Condition number `kappa = sum_j |w_j|` at the highest order the term
count supports. [`LevinVariant::V`] consumes one extra look-ahead term.

The transform is a weighted mean of the partial sums,
`L = sum_j w_j s_j` with `sum_j w_j = 1`. Those weights are the solution
of the Vandermonde-type system in the nodes `beta + n + j` that the
Fessler-Ford-Smith recurrence inverts implicitly, so `kappa` — the 1-norm
of that solution — is the factor by which rounding in `s_j` is amplified
into the estimate, and a lower bound for the 1-norm condition number of
the system. The accuracy floor of the transform is `kappa * eps`.

`kappa` depends on the series, which is why `terms` is an argument:
alternating terms give a convex combination with `kappa = 1`, while
positive logarithmically convergent terms give weights of alternating
sign whose absolute sum grows by a factor `~3.5` per order (for
`1/(n+1)^2`: `4.6e5` at order 11, `2.3e8` at order 16).
Returns infinity for a nonpositive or non-finite `beta`, an invalid
remainder in the required prefix, or a singular or unrepresentable
condition number. Fewer than two terms return `1.0` by convention.

operators.name: num_analysis_convergence_levin_condition_numbers
operators.doc:
Returns one dimensionless Levin condition number per available order, from order zero. Infinite values indicate an undefined or unbounded condition number. Measured terms may share any dimension, beta is dimensionless, and the input budget is 4096 terms.

Estimates the Levin weight condition number for each order starting at zero.

Each entry is the absolute sum of the normalized weights for its order.
This measures sensitivity to the partial sums with fixed remainder
estimates.
A singular or unrepresentable order contributes infinity at its original
position. The profile ends at the first invalid remainder estimate.
[`LevinVariant::V`] uses one additional term beyond each order's prefix.
A nonpositive or non-finite `beta` gives an empty profile. The recurrence
uses quadratic time in the valid prefix length and linear workspace in the
number of terms.

```
use rssn::kernels::convergence::LevinVariant;
use rssn::kernels::convergence::levin_condition_numbers;
let profile = levin_condition_numbers(&[1.0, -0.5, 0.25], LevinVariant::T, 1.0);
assert_eq!(profile.len(), 3);
assert!(profile.iter().all(|kappa| (kappa - 1.0).abs() < 1e-14));
```

operators.name: num_analysis_convergence_levin_sum_lazy
signatures: (Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Int, String, Float) -> { item0: Float[_], item1: Float[_] }
operators.doc:
Native convergence levin_sum_lazy; normalized dimensionless arguments unless the declared contract preserves measured signal units. Enum arguments use exact Rust variant names.

Sums a series whose terms arrive lazily, one at a time.

Pulls at most `max_terms` items from `terms` — an unbounded generator is
fine — and transforms the terms directly with [`levin_transform_terms`],
so the acceleration never depends on differencing rounded partial sums.
`beta` is the shift of the remainder estimate (`1.0` is usual).

Returns `(estimate, error_estimate)`, chosen by the same
smallest-successive-difference rule as [`levin_sum`].

# Errors
Returns an error if `max_terms` is below four, if the iterator yields
fewer than four terms, if a term is not finite, or if no finite transform
can be formed.

operators.name: num_analysis_convergence_levin_transform
operators.doc:
Native convergence levin_transform; normalized dimensionless arguments unless the declared contract preserves measured signal units. Enum arguments use exact Rust variant names.

Levin-type sequence transformation of the partial sums `s_0, s_1, ...`.

With the term `a_n = s_n - s_{n-1}` (`a_0 = s_0`) and the remainder
estimate `omega_n` of the chosen [`LevinVariant`], the transform
`L_k^{(0)}` is computed with the stable
Fessler-Ford-Smith recurrence for numerator and denominator,
`L_k^{(n)} = N_k^{(n)} / D_k^{(n)}` with
`N_{k+1}^{(n)} = N_k^{(n+1)} - (beta+n)(beta+n+k)^{k-1} / (beta+n+k+1)^k N_k^{(n)}`.
Order zero uses the first partial sum and later orders use more
terms. `beta` is the shift (`1.0` is the usual choice). The result lists
finite estimates in order and omits any non-finite estimates.

The terms are recovered by differencing, which cancels the leading
digits that consecutive partial sums share; when the terms are available
directly, [`levin_transform_terms`] avoids that loss.

operators.name: num_analysis_convergence_levin_transform_terms
operators.doc:
Native convergence levin_transform_terms; normalized dimensionless arguments unless the declared contract preserves measured signal units. Enum arguments use exact Rust variant names.

Levin-type transformation of the terms `a_0, a_1, ...` themselves.

Same transform as [`levin_transform`], but the terms are used as given
instead of being recovered from rounded partial sums by
`a_n = s_n - s_{n-1}`. That difference throws away the leading digits
`s_n` and `s_{n-1}` share — most of them late in a slowly converging
series — so this entry point keeps the full precision of the terms. The
partial sums are accumulated in the order the terms are given.

This is the entry point for a series whose terms are known in closed form
or produced one at a time (see [`levin_sum_lazy`]).

operators.name: num_analysis_coordinates_cartesian_to_spherical
operators.doc:
Converts the fixed shape [x, y, z] to [radius, polar angle from +z, azimuth from +x]. Express all lengths in one reference and use radians for both angles. The polar angle is zero at the origin.

Converts Cartesian `[x, y, z]` to spherical `[r, theta, phi]`.

`theta` is measured from the positive z axis in `[0, π]` and `phi` is
the azimuth from the positive x axis in `[-π, π]` (both in radians).
With horizontal length `h = hypot(x, y)`, the polar angle is
`atan2(h, z)`. It is zero at the origin. Finite coordinates can produce
an infinite radius if the norm overflows, with both angles still defined.
An infinite z component produces a NaN polar angle.

operators.name: num_analysis_coordinates_jacobian_determinant
operators.doc:
Normalized coordinate conversion: radial/Cartesian coordinates are expressed in one chosen positive reference length, angles in radians. Result coordinates and Jacobians use the same normalization; mixed physical units are not erased silently.

Determinant of the Jacobian of the map `from -> to` at `at_point`.

This is the local volume-element factor `dV_to = |det J| dV_from` of the
two coordinate charts: for example `r` for polar-to-Cartesian and
`r^2 sin(theta)` for spherical-to-Cartesian, while the inverse maps carry
the reciprocal determinant. It is built from the central-difference
Jacobian of [`numerical_jacobian`] and inherits its accuracy and precision
caveat (no analytic Jacobian).

# Errors
As [`numerical_jacobian`].

operators.name: num_analysis_cubature_genz_malik_compiled
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Float, Int, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Native Genz-Malik cubature: physical same-unit coordinates, independently measured output, explicit evaluation limit and volume-dimensioned absolute tolerance.

Adaptive Genz-Malik cubature over the box `[lo, hi]`.

Each region is integrated with the degree-7 Genz-Malik rule
(`1 + 4n + 2n(n-1) + 2^n` points) whose embedded degree-5 rule gives
the error estimate; the region with the largest error is bisected
along the axis with the largest fourth divided difference. The box
is first split uniformly into a few sub-boxes so that narrow peaks
are not missed. Stops when the total error is below
`max(abs_tol, rel_tol * |value|)` or after `max_evals` integrand
evaluations (`converged == false`). Intended for 2 to about 8
dimensions.

A bisection only replaces a region by its two halves, so the regions
always tile the box exactly: their volumes sum to the box volume and no
two overlap. `value` and `error` are the sums of the region values and
of the region estimates; the estimate is the embedded degree-5/7
difference, a heuristic rather than a rigorous bound (see the module
limitations).

operators.name: num_analysis_dae_consistent_index1
signatures: (rssn/native/analysis/dae/model/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Float, Int, Int) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Actual native index1 DAE consistency projection with independently measured variables, explicit constraint metric and original oracle errors.

Computes consistent initial algebraic states `z0` and differential derivatives `dy0`
for a semi-explicit Index-1 DAE system `y' = f(t, y, z)`, `0 = g(t, y, z)` at `t0`.

Given fixed initial differential variables `y0` and an initial guess `z0_guess`,
solves `g(t0, y0, z0) = 0` via damped Newton-Raphson iteration (`dg/dz` must be
nonsingular for an index-1 DAE). Returns `(dy0, z0)`.

# Errors

[`OdeGeomError::Domain`] for non-finite values, [`OdeGeomError::ShapeMismatch`] for
mismatched lengths, [`OdeGeomError::Singular`] if `dg/dz` is singular (e.g. higher-index DAE),
and [`OdeGeomError::NotConverged`] if Newton iteration does not converge.

operators.name: num_analysis_dae_consistent_index2
signatures: (rssn/native/analysis/dae/model/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Float, Int, Int) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Actual native index2 DAE consistency projection with independently measured variables, explicit constraint metric and original oracle errors.

Computes consistent initial conditions `(y0, z0)` for a semi-explicit Hessenberg
Index-2 DAE system `y'(t) = f(t, y, z)`, `0 = g(t, y)` at `t0`.

An index-2 DAE has two constraint manifolds:
1. The explicit position/state constraint `g(t, y) = 0`.
2. The hidden velocity/index-1 constraint obtained by differentiating `g(t, y) = 0`
   with respect to time: `G(t, y) f(t, y, z) + \partial_t g(t, y) = 0`, where
   `G = \partial g / \partial y` and `(G \cdot \partial f / \partial z)` is nonsingular.

This function first projects `y0_guess` onto `g(t0, y) = 0` via minimum-norm
Gauss–Newton projection, then solves the hidden constraint for `z0`.

# Errors

[`OdeGeomError::Empty`] if `y0_guess` or `z0_guess` is empty,
[`OdeGeomError::Singular`] if `G (\partial f / \partial z)` is singular, and
[`OdeGeomError::NotConverged`] if projection fails to converge.

signatures: (Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>

History tape(time)->state sets the initial condition; RHS tape receives(time,state,delayed state). tau/h are physical times, tau>=h, and the final native step clips the endpoint. Returned samples carry true physical coordinates, not an invented dense interpolant.

Constant-delay DDE integrator (method of steps with RK4).

`hist(t)` for `t <= t0`, integrated by classical RK4 (method of steps)

floating-point time.

operators.name: num_analysis_dde_state_dependent
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int) -> rssn/native/analysis/dde/solution/v1
operators.doc:
Actual native state-dependent DDE. Each query tape(time,state)->physical past time invokes the native scoped history lookup at that stage; RHS tape receives(time,state,queried states in declared order). No lookup closure escapes or is retained. Independent state/history/rate references and explicit query/RHS evaluation budgets are preserved.

Solves a general (possibly state-dependent or time-dependent) Delay Differential
Equation (DDE) system `y'(t) = rhs(t, y(t), &|t_past| ...)` over `span = (t0, t1)`.

The third argument passed to `rhs` is a continuous state lookup closure `&dyn Fn(f64) -> Vec<f64>`
that evaluates `history(t_past)` for `t_past <= t0` and the continuous cubic Hermite
extension of the solution for `t0 < t_past <= t`.

# Errors

[`OdeGeomError::Empty`] if `y0` is empty, [`OdeGeomError::Domain`] for invalid span or
tolerances, [`OdeGeomError::ShapeMismatch`] for mismatched state dimensions, and
[`OdeGeomError::NotConverged`] if step size collapses.

operators.name: num_analysis_filon2d_compiled
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Bool, Dyn<term>, Int, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Native2D Filon cosine/sine quadrature: phase coefficients have one dimension P,omega has1/(P*coordinate),amplitude references preserve arbitrary ordinate units.

Two-dimensional Filon quadrature of an oscillatory integrand over a box.

The integrand is `f(x, y) * cos(omega * phi(x, y))` (`cosine = true`) or
`f(x, y) * sin(omega * phi(x, y))` (`cosine = false`), for the linear phase
`phi(x, y) = a x + b y` with `phase = [a, b]`.

The amplitude is interpolated by a tensor product of quadratic Lagrange
polynomials, one per double panel and axis, and each oscillatory moment is
integrated exactly (it is the 1-D [`filon`] functional), so the accuracy
does not degrade as `|omega|` grows. The panel count is doubled from one
until the difference between successive sweeps is at most
`tol * max(|value|, 1)`, so `omega = 0` reproduces the classical Simpson
rule (exact for a quadratic amplitude).

Invalid input (a box dimension list other than two, `hi <= lo`, a
non-finite frequency/slope/tolerance, `tol <= 0`) returns `NaN` values
with `converged == false`; it never panics.

operators.doc:

Two-dimensional complex-exponential Filon quadrature,
`integral f(x, y) exp(i omega (a x + b y)) dx dy` over the box `[lo, hi]`,
with `phase = [a, b]`.

Same method and validity rules as [`filon2d`]; the value is returned as a
complex number so both the cosine and sine components are available, and
the error is the norm of the complex error.

operators.name: num_analysis_homotopy_system_scaled
signatures: (Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<2, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Float[_], Float[_]) -> { roots: Tensor<1, Complex[_]>, offsets: Tensor<1, Int>, finite: Tensor<1, Bool>, residuals: Tensor<1, None | Some(Float[_])> }

Actual native square polynomial homotopy for normalized coefficients/exponent rows/checked polynomial offsets. Positive coordinate/output references restore physical complex roots/residuals. Maximum6variables,4096terms,degree16,and256total-degree paths. Failed paths retain false status and optional residual; their undefined roots occupy empty offset ranges.

Solves a square polynomial system by total-degree homotopy
continuation with the default (fixed, generic) `gamma`; see
[`homotopy_system_with_gamma`].

# Errors
[`RootError::Invalid`] for a non-square or malformed system.

operators.name: num_analysis_homotopy_system_with_gamma_scaled
signatures: (Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<2, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Float[_], Float[_], Complex) -> { roots: Tensor<1, Complex[_]>, offsets: Tensor<1, Int>, finite: Tensor<1, Bool>, residuals: Tensor<1, None | Some(Float[_])> }
operators.doc:
Actual gamma-selected native homotopy using normalized polynomial descriptors and independent physical root/residual references; all path statuses and defined coordinates are retained.

Total-degree homotopy continuation for a square polynomial system
`f_i(x_1..x_n) = 0` (`system[i]` lists the terms of `f_i`).

The start system is `g_i = x_i^{d_i} - 1` with `d_i` the total degree
of `f_i`; its `prod d_i` solutions are tracked along
`H(x, t) = (1-t) gamma g(x) + t f(x)` from `t = 0` to `t = 1` with an
RK4 predictor, a Newton corrector and adaptive step control. The
complex constant `gamma` (the "gamma trick") makes the paths
non-crossing with probability one. One [`PathResult`] is returned per
start solution; paths diverging to infinity are marked
`finite == false`.

# Errors
[`RootError::Invalid`] for a non-square or malformed system, a zero
or nonfinite gamma, or more than 200 000 total-degree paths.

Native hypergeometric hyp1f1_cplx; normalized dimensionless arguments unless the declared contract preserves measured signal units. Enum arguments use exact Rust variant names.

Kummer's confluent hypergeometric function `M(a, b, z) = 1F1(a; b; z)`.

All arguments are complex. For `Re z < 0` Kummer's transformation
`M(a, b, z) = e^z M(b - a, b, -z)` is applied so that the dominant
solution is the one being continued.

Gauss hypergeometric function `2F1(a, b; c; z)` for complex parameters
and argument (principal branch, cut along `[1, inf)`; the value on the
cut is the limit from `Im z -> 0+`).

For positive real parameters at `z = 1`, the gamma ratio in
[Gauss's theorem](https://dlmf.nist.gov/15.4.E20) is evaluated in logarithmic
form without forming large gamma values.

The generalised hypergeometric function `pFq(a; b; z)`.

See the module documentation for the algorithm. `z = 0` gives `1`. Returns NaN for
divergent series (`p > q + 1` without termination, `z != 0`), a denominator
parameter at a non-positive integer (without earlier termination), and `+inf` at `z = 1` when
`Re(sum b - sum a) <= 0`; [`hyp_pfq_checked`] tells which.

termination), or a divergent series (`p > q + 1`, `z != 0`). `z = 0` gives `1` in every case.

operators.name: num_analysis_importance_sampling_gaussian_compiled
signatures: (rssn/native/analysis/gaussian/v1, rssn/native/analysis/gaussian/v1, Int, Int, Int, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Native Gaussian importance sampling using measured target/proposal models; integrand references match their coordinate domain. Output has ordinate units, not ordinate times length; ESS remains dimensionless.

Importance-sampling estimate of `∫ f(x) p_target(x) dx`.

Draws `n` points from `proposal` and averages `f(x) * p_target(x) /
p_proposal(x)`. Because the weight has mean one under the proposal, the
estimator is unbiased for the target integral whatever the shift; what
the shift costs is variance, visible in the effective sample size. The
proposal must be non-degenerate and have at least the support of the
target, otherwise the weights are not finite and the estimate is not
defined.

The error is the sample standard error of the weighted terms, and the
effective sample size is `(Σ w)^2 / Σ w^2`.
