operators.name: num_finite_field_slice_scale_mod
operators.doc: `num_finite_field_slice_scale_mod(values, scalar, modulus)` multiplies an exact u64 vector by a scalar modulo an integer of at least 2.

operators.name: num_finite_field_slice_sub_mod
signatures: (Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Int>
operators.doc: `num_finite_field_slice_sub_mod(a, b, modulus)` subtracts two equal-length vectors of exact u64 integers, returning residues in [0, modulus). The modulus must be at least 2.

operators.name: num_flow_inflow_velocity
operators.doc:
Actual native unit-height inflow profile evaluated at normalized y; amplitude is normalized by the mechanical L/T reference and result retains velocity units.

Axial velocity at height `y` in `[0, 1]`.

operators.name: num_flow_run_channel
signatures: (rssn/native/mechanical-references/v1, Int, Int, Float, Float, Int, Tensor<1, Bool>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Native square unit-domain channel with original free-slip walls and uniform unit inflow; normalized dt uses the explicit Time reference, output velocities and pressure have mechanical units. The native rectangular rejection is preserved.

Solves the 2D Navier-Stokes equations for channel flow with an obstacle.

Free-slip walls and a uniform unit inflow; see [`run_channel_flow_with`]
for no-slip walls and a Poiseuille inflow, and for the boundary
treatment.

# Arguments
* `nx` - Grid width.
* `ny` - Grid height.
* `re` - Reynolds number.
* `dt` - Time step.
* `n_iter` - Number of iterations.
* `obstacle_mask` - A boolean mask where true indicates an obstacle (u=0).

# Returns
Tuple of (u, v, p) arrays.

The solver works on a square `nx` x `nx` grid (`ny` must equal `nx`).

# Errors
Returns an error if the grid is smaller than 3 points, not square, or if
the obstacle mask does not have shape `(ny, nx)`; also if the pressure
solver fails.

operators.name: num_flow_run_channel_with
signatures: (rssn/native/mechanical-references/v1, Int, Float, Float, Int, Tensor<1, Bool>, String, Float, String) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Actual native configurable channel model on a square unit domain; inflow, no-slip/slip wall, obstacle mask, Reynolds number and normalized time step are passed unchanged. Physical outputs retain independent velocity/pressure references.

Solves the 2D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in the unit square
with an optional no-slip obstacle, by Chorin's projection method.

Each step
1. advances an intermediate velocity explicitly (first-order upwind
   advection, central diffusion) at every fluid point; solid points and
   boundary points are then set by the boundary conditions,
2. imposes the boundary conditions: the inflow profile on the left,
   zero-gradient outflow on the right, the [`WallCondition`] on top and
   bottom, and *no slip* (`u = v = 0`) on every point of the obstacle
   mask (so fluid points next to the obstacle see zero velocity in
   their diffusion and advection stencils),
3. solves the pressure Poisson equation `lap(p) = div(u*) / dt` over the
   fluid points only, with `dp/dn = 0` on the inflow, the walls and all
   obstacle faces and `p = 0` at the outflow, by preconditioned
   conjugate gradients, and
4. corrects `u = u* - dt grad(p)` at fluid points, where a gradient
   across an obstacle face uses the Neumann (mirrored) pressure.

The explicit scheme needs `dt <= h^2 re / 4` and `dt <= h / |u|`.

# Errors
Returns an error for invalid grid size, mask shape, time step, Reynolds
number or inflow, non-finite fields, incompatible flux in a closed
fluid region, or an unconverged pressure solve.

operators.name: num_flow_run_lid_cavity
signatures: (rssn/native/mechanical-references/v1, Int, Int, Float, Float, Int, Float) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Actual native legacy staggered cavity on a square unit domain. Lid velocity and time are normalized by explicit mechanical references. Native pressure/multigrid behavior is retained and work is bounded before invocation.

Main solver for the 2D lid-driven cavity problem.

Chorin's projection method on a staggered (MAC) grid: `p[j][i]` lives at
cell centres, `u[j][i]` on the left face of cell `(j, i)` and `v[j][i]` on
its bottom face. Each step
1. advances the intermediate velocity explicitly with first-order upwind
   advection and central diffusion with `nu = 1 / re`,
2. solves `lap(phi) = div(u*) / dt` with the multigrid solver (the same
   solver and zero-Dirichlet closure as [`run_channel_flow`]), and
3. corrects `u = u* - dt grad(phi)` and sets `p = phi`.

The top row of `u` is the moving lid (`lid_velocity`), the bottom row and
the side faces are at rest. The explicit scheme needs
`dt <= h^2 re / 4` (diffusion) and `dt <= h / |u|` (advection) to stay stable.

# Errors

Returns an error if the grid is smaller than 3 points, if the cells are
not square (`nx != ny`), or if the multigrid solver fails.

operators.name: num_flow_save_lid_cavity_scenario
operators.doc:
Runs the actual native fixed 65x65, 200-step cavity scenario and writes its three native NPY files to the explicitly provided output directory. This legacy routine reports failures itself; the result only acknowledges return from the routine, not successful file creation.

An example scenario for the lid-driven cavity simulation.

The fields are written as `cavity_u_velocity.npy`, `cavity_v_velocity.npy`
and `cavity_pressure.npy` inside `output_dir`, which is created if missing.

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_barnsley_fern_ifs
signatures: () -> { item0: Tensor<2, Float>, item1: Tensor<1, Float> }
operators.doc: Creates the Barnsley fern IFS.

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_box_counting_dimension
operators.doc:
Box-counting dimension of a finite N x 2 point tensor; both coordinate axes share units. Scale/work counts are bounded before native execution.

Estimates the box-counting (Minkowski) dimension from a set of 2D points.

The box-counting dimension is estimated by:
D = lim(ε→0) [log(N(ε)) / log(1/ε)]

where N(ε) is the number of boxes of side ε needed to cover the set.

# Arguments
* `points` - A slice of 2D points.
* `num_scales` - Number of different box sizes to use.

# Returns
An estimate of the box-counting dimension.

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_correlation_dimension
operators.doc:
Correlation dimension of a finite N x 2 coordinate tensor. Pair allocation and radius-work counts are bounded.

Estimates the correlation dimension from the log-log slope of the fraction
of pairs closer than each of `num_radii` logarithmically spaced radii.

Returns zero when fewer than two scales can determine a slope, and NaN for
non-finite coordinates or distances outside the range of `f64`.

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_correlation_dimension_with_radii
operators.doc:
Correlation dimension from an N x 2 point tensor and explicit positive finite radii. Radii have the same units as the coordinates. Returns None when fewer than two radii determine a slope.

Estimates correlation dimension from caller-supplied positive, finite radii.

Radii can be supplied in any order. At radius `r`, only pairs strictly
closer than `r` contribute. At least two distinct radii with close pairs
are needed for a fit.

Returns `None` for non-finite coordinates or when the radii cannot determine
a slope.

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_generate_burning_ship
signatures: (Int, Int, { item0: Float, item1: Float }, { item0: Float, item1: Float }, Int) -> Tensor<2, Int>
operators.doc:
Generates the Burning Ship fractal.

Similar to the Mandelbrot set but uses absolute values:
`z = (|Re(z)| + i|Im(z)|)^2 + c`

The resulting fractal resembles a burning ship.

# Arguments
* `width`, `height` - The dimensions of the output image.
* `x_range`, `y_range` - The region in the complex plane to plot.
* `max_iter` - The maximum number of iterations per point.

# Returns
A 2D vector where each element is the escape time.

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_generate_henon_map
signatures: ({ item0: Float, item1: Float }, Int, Float, Float) -> Tensor<2, Float>
operators.doc:
Native Henon map in normalized dimensionless coordinates. Returns an N x 2 point tensor with a checked finite allocation budget.

Generates the Henon map trajectory.

The Henon map is a discrete-time dynamical system that exhibits chaotic behavior.

The map is:
- x_{n+1} = 1 - a*`x_n^2` + `y_n`
- y_{n+1} = b*`x_n`

Classic parameter values: a = 1.4, b = 0.3

# Arguments
* `start_point` - The initial `(x, y)` coordinates.
* `num_steps` - The number of iterations.
* `a`, `b` - The Henon map parameters.

# Returns
A `Vec` of `(f64, f64)` tuples representing the trajectory.

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_generate_ifs_fractal
signatures: (Tensor<2, Float>, Tensor<1, Float>, { item0: Float, item1: Float }, Int, Int) -> Tensor<2, Float>
operators.doc:
Runs the affine chaos game in dimensionless coordinates with historical seed 12345. Provide N x 6 rows (a,b,c,d,e,f), N finite nonnegative weights including a positive weight, and the starting coordinates. Returns one two-coordinate row per retained step after burn-in.

Generates an IFS fractal using the chaos game algorithm.

# Arguments
* `transforms` - The affine transformations.
* `probabilities` - Probabilities for selecting each transformation.
* `start_point` - Initial point.
* `num_points` - Number of points to generate.
* `skip` - Number of initial points to skip (for convergence).

# Returns
A vector of 2D points on the fractal. Invalid input or a nonfinite orbit
yields an empty vector. Use [`AffineIfs`] to reuse preparation or choose a seed.

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_generate_julia_set
signatures: (Int, Int, { item0: Float, item1: Float }, { item0: Float, item1: Float }, { item0: Float, item1: Float }, Int) -> Tensor<2, Int>
operators.doc:
Generates the data for a Julia set image.

The Julia set is defined by iterating `z = z*z + c` for a fixed c parameter.
Unlike the Mandelbrot set, c is constant and z varies.

# Arguments
* `width`, `height` - The dimensions of the output image.
* `x_range`, `y_range` - The region in the complex plane to plot.
* `c` - The constant c parameter `(real, imaginary)`.
* `max_iter` - The maximum number of iterations per point.

# Returns
A 2D vector where each element is the escape time.

# Example
```
use rssn::kernels::fractal_geometry_and_chaos::generate_julia_set;

// Julia set for c = -0.4 + 0.6i
let data = generate_julia_set(100, 100, (-2.0, 2.0), (-2.0, 2.0), (-0.4, 0.6), 50);

assert_eq!(data.len(), 100);
```

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_generate_lorenz_attractor
signatures: ({ item0: Float, item1: Float, item2: Float }, Float, Int) -> Tensor<2, Float>
operators.doc:
Generates the points for a Lorenz attractor simulation.

The Lorenz attractor is a set of chaotic solutions for a simplified model of atmospheric
convection. This function numerically integrates the Lorenz system of differential equations
to produce a sequence of points that trace out the attractor.

The system is defined by:
- dx/dt = σ(y - x)
- dy/dt = x(ρ - z) - y
- dz/dt = xy - βz

Uses standard parameters: σ = 10, ρ = 28, β = 8/3

# Arguments
* `start_point` - The initial `(x, y, z)` coordinates.
* `dt` - The time step for the integration.
* `num_steps` - The number of integration steps to perform.

# Returns
A `Vec` of `(f64, f64, f64)` tuples representing the trajectory of the attractor.

# Example
```
use rssn::kernels::fractal_geometry_and_chaos::generate_lorenz_attractor;

let points = generate_lorenz_attractor((0.1, 0.0, 0.0), 0.01, 1000);

assert_eq!(points.len(), 1000);
```

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_generate_lorenz_attractor_custom
signatures: ({ item0: Float, item1: Float, item2: Float }, Float, Int, Float, Float, Float) -> Tensor<2, Float>
operators.doc:
Generates a Lorenz attractor with custom parameters.

# Arguments
* `start_point` - The initial `(x, y, z)` coordinates.
* `dt` - The time step for the integration.
* `num_steps` - The number of integration steps.
* `sigma`, `rho`, `beta` - The Lorenz system parameters.

# Returns
A `Vec` of `(f64, f64, f64)` tuples representing the trajectory.

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_generate_mandelbrot_set
signatures: (Int, Int, { item0: Float, item1: Float }, { item0: Float, item1: Float }, Int) -> Tensor<2, Int>
operators.doc:
Generates the data for a Mandelbrot set image.

The Mandelbrot set is a fractal defined by the iteration `z = z*z + c`.
Points `c` for which the iteration remains bounded form the set.
This function computes the escape time for each point in a given region.

# Arguments
* `width`, `height` - The dimensions of the output image.
* `x_range`, `y_range` - The region in the complex plane to plot.
* `max_iter` - The maximum number of iterations per point.

# Returns
A 2D vector where each element is the number of iterations it took for that point to escape.

# Example
```
use rssn::kernels::fractal_geometry_and_chaos::generate_mandelbrot_set;

let data = generate_mandelbrot_set(100, 100, (-2.5, 1.0), (-1.5, 1.5), 50);

assert_eq!(data.len(), 100);
```

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_generate_multibrot
signatures: (Int, Int, { item0: Float, item1: Float }, { item0: Float, item1: Float }, Float, Int) -> Tensor<2, Int>
operators.doc:
Generates the Multibrot set with exponent d.

The Multibrot set is a generalization where `z = z^d + c`.
d=2 gives the standard Mandelbrot set.

# Arguments
* `width`, `height` - The dimensions of the output image.
* `x_range`, `y_range` - The region in the complex plane to plot.
* `d` - The exponent (power).
* `max_iter` - The maximum number of iterations per point.

# Returns
A 2D vector where each element is the escape time.

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_generate_newton_fractal
signatures: (Int, Int, { item0: Float, item1: Float }, { item0: Float, item1: Float }, Int, Float) -> Tensor<2, Int>
operators.doc:
Generates a Newton fractal for `z^3 - 1 = 0`.

Newton's method applied to finding roots of `f(z) = z^3 - 1` produces
a fractal pattern. Each pixel is colored based on which root it converges to.

# Arguments
* `width`, `height` - The dimensions of the output image.
* `x_range`, `y_range` - The region in the complex plane to plot.
* `max_iter` - The maximum number of iterations per point.
* `tolerance` - The convergence tolerance.

# Returns
A 2D vector where each element indicates which root (0, 1, or 2) was reached,
or 3 if no convergence.

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_generate_rossler_attractor
signatures: ({ item0: Float, item1: Float, item2: Float }, Float, Int, Float, Float, Float) -> Tensor<2, Float>
operators.doc:
Generates the Rossler attractor.

The Rossler attractor is a system of three non-linear ordinary differential equations
that exhibits chaotic dynamics. It is simpler than the Lorenz system.

The system is defined by:
- dx/dt = -y - z
- dy/dt = x + ay
- dz/dt = b + z(x - c)

Common parameter values: a = 0.2, b = 0.2, c = 5.7

# Arguments
* `start_point` - The initial `(x, y, z)` coordinates.
* `dt` - The time step for the integration.
* `num_steps` - The number of integration steps.
* `a`, `b`, `c` - The Rossler system parameters.

# Returns
A `Vec` of `(f64, f64, f64)` tuples representing the trajectory.

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_generate_tinkerbell_map
signatures: ({ item0: Float, item1: Float }, Int, Float, Float, Float, Float) -> Tensor<2, Float>
operators.doc:
Native Tinkerbell map in normalized dimensionless coordinates. Returns an N x 2 tensor under a finite path budget.

Generates the Tinkerbell map trajectory.

The Tinkerbell map is a two-dimensional iterated map:
- x_{n+1} = `x_n^2` - `y_n^2` + `ax_n` + `by_n`
- y_{n+1} = `2x_n`*`y_n` + `cx_n` + `dy_n`

Classic parameter values: a = 0.9, b = -0.6013, c = 2.0, d = 0.5

# Arguments
* `start_point` - The initial `(x, y)` coordinates.
* `num_steps` - The number of iterations.
* `a`, `b`, `c`, `d` - The map parameters.

# Returns
A `Vec` of `(f64, f64)` tuples representing the trajectory.

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_julia_escape_time
operators.doc: Computes the escape time for a single point in a Julia set.

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_logistic_bifurcation
signatures: ({ item0: Float, item1: Float }, Int, Int, Int, Float) -> Tensor<2, Float>
operators.doc:
Logistic bifurcation samples in normalized coordinates; transient and retained iterations share a finite work budget. Returns columns r and x.

Generates data for a bifurcation diagram of the logistic map.

For each value of r, the map is iterated and the final values after
discarding transients are recorded.

# Arguments
* `r_range` - The range of r values `(r_min, r_max)`.
* `num_r_values` - Number of r values to sample.
* `transient` - Number of initial iterations to discard.
* `num_points` - Number of points to record after transient.
* `x0` - Initial x value.

# Returns
A `Vec` of `(r, x)` pairs for plotting the bifurcation diagram.

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_logistic_map_iterate
operators.doc:
Iterates the logistic map.

The logistic map is defined by: x_{n+1} = r * `x_n` * (1 - `x_n`)

It is a classic example of how complex behavior can arise from simple nonlinear
dynamical equations. For r between 0 and 4, the dynamics range from stable
fixed points to period doubling to chaos.

# Arguments
* `x0` - Initial value (should be between 0 and 1).
* `r` - The growth rate parameter.
* `num_steps` - The number of iterations.

# Returns
A `Vec` of x values representing the orbit.

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_lyapunov_exponent_logistic
operators.doc:
Computes the Lyapunov exponent for the logistic map.

The Lyapunov exponent λ measures the rate of separation of infinitesimally
close trajectories. For the logistic map:
λ = lim (1/n) * sum(ln|r(1-2x_i)|)

Positive λ indicates chaos.

# Arguments
* `r` - The growth rate parameter.
* `x0` - Initial value.
* `transient` - Number of iterations to discard.
* `num_iterations` - Number of iterations for averaging.

# Returns
The estimated Lyapunov exponent.

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_lyapunov_exponent_lorenz
signatures: ({ item0: Float, item1: Float, item2: Float }, Float, Int, Float, Float, Float) -> Float
operators.doc:
Computes the largest Lyapunov exponent for a 3D flow (e.g., Lorenz system).

Uses the method of tracking the evolution of a small perturbation.

# Arguments
* `start_point` - Initial point `(x, y, z)`.
* `dt` - Time step.
* `num_steps` - Number of integration steps.
* `sigma`, `rho`, `beta` - Lorenz system parameters.

# Returns
The estimated largest Lyapunov exponent.

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_mandelbrot_escape_time
operators.doc:
Computes the escape time for a single point in the Mandelbrot set.

# Arguments
* `c_real` - Real part of the complex number c
* `c_imag` - Imaginary part of the complex number c
* `max_iter` - Maximum iterations

# Returns
The number of iterations before escape, or `max_iter` if the point is in the set.

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_orbit_density
signatures: (Tensor<2, Float>, Int, Int, { item0: Float, item1: Float }, { item0: Float, item1: Float }) -> { offsets: Tensor<1, Int>, indices: Tensor<1, Int> }
operators.doc:
Normalized phase-space point histogram. N x 2 input points and bounded bin counts produce CSR integer rows (offsets/indices); entries are counts, preserving empty rows without padding.

Computes the density distribution of orbit points in a 2D histogram.

# Arguments
* `points` - The orbit trajectory.
* `x_bins` - Number of bins in x direction.
* `y_bins` - Number of bins in y direction.
* `x_range` - Range for x axis.
* `y_range` - Range for y axis.

# Returns
A 2D vector of counts for each bin.

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_orbit_entropy
signatures: ({ offsets: Tensor<1, Int>, indices: Tensor<1, Int> }) -> Float
operators.doc:
Computes the entropy of an orbit from its density distribution.

Uses Shannon entropy: H = -`sum(p_i` * `log(p_i)`)

# Arguments
* `density` - A 2D density histogram from `orbit_density`.

# Returns
The Shannon entropy of the distribution.

operators.name: num_fractal_geometry_and_chaos_sierpinski_triangle_ifs
signatures: () -> { item0: Tensor<2, Float>, item1: Tensor<1, Float> }
operators.doc: Creates the Sierpinski triangle IFS.

operators.name: num_fresnel_c
operators.doc: Fresnel cosine integral `C(x) = ∫_0^x cos(π t² / 2) dt`.

operators.name: num_fresnel_erf_complex
operators.doc:
Error function of a complex argument.

Maclaurin series for `|z| < 1.5`, otherwise `1 - exp(-z²) w(i z)` after
folding to `Re z >= 0` with `erf(-z) = -erf(z)`. The exponential is
scaled with the Faddeeva factor near the floating-point range limits.

operators.name: num_fresnel_faddeeva_w
operators.doc: The Faddeeva function `w(z) = exp(-z²) erfc(-i z)`.

operators.name: num_fresnel_fresnel_f
operators.doc: Auxiliary function `f(x)` of DLMF 7.2.10 (`≈ 1/(π x)` for large `x`).

operators.name: num_fresnel_fresnel_fg
operators.doc: Auxiliary functions `(f(x), g(x))` of DLMF 7.2.10: `f = (1/2 - S) cos θ - (1/2 - C) sin θ`, `g = (1/2 - C) cos θ + (1/2 - S) sin θ`, `θ = π x² / 2`.

operators.name: num_fresnel_fresnel_g
operators.doc: Auxiliary function `g(x)` of DLMF 7.2.10 (`≈ 1/(π² x³)` for large `x`).

operators.name: num_fresnel_fresnel_sc
operators.doc: Fresnel integrals `(S(x), C(x))` together.

operators.name: num_fresnel_fresnel_sc_complex
signatures: (Float, Float) -> { item0: { item0: Float, item1: Float }, item1: { item0: Float, item1: Float } }
operators.doc: `(S(z), C(z))` for a complex argument `z = re + i·im`, returned as `((S.re, S.im), (C.re, C.im))`.

operators.name: num_fresnel_s
operators.doc: Fresnel sine integral `S(x) = ∫_0^x sin(π t² / 2) dt`.

operators.name: num_fresnel_sc_interval
operators.doc:
Returns the dimensionless Fresnel sine and cosine integrals from a to b as item0 and item1. Narrow intervals and far-field tails use direct differences. Infinite bounds give improper integrals. Reversing the bounds negates both results.

Normalised Fresnel sine and cosine integrals `(S, C)` over `[a, b]`.

Both integrands use the phase `π t² / 2`. Narrow intervals are integrated
directly, and far from the origin the common endpoint limit cancels before
rounding, so differences can survive even when the values from
[`fresnel_sc`] round to the same number.

Reversing the limits negates both results. Infinite limits are interpreted
as improper integrals. Equal limits give zero, including equal infinities.
A NaN limit gives two NaNs.

```
use rssn::kernels::fresnel::fresnel_sc_interval;

let (s, c) = fresnel_sc_interval(1.0, 1.0_f64.next_up());
assert_eq!(s, f64::EPSILON);
assert!(c < 0.0);
```

operators.name: num_fresnel_sin_cos_half_pi_square
operators.doc: `(sin(π x² / 2), cos(π x² / 2))` with the phase reduced exactly.

operators.name: num_fujiwara_root_bound
operators.doc:
Fujiwara upper bound from ascending complex coefficients with a common ordinate dimension. The polynomial coordinate and the result are dimensionless.

Fujiwara upper bound on the modulus of all polynomial roots:
$R = 2 \max_{1 \le k \le n} \left|\frac{c_{n-k}}{c_n}\right|^{1/k}$ with factor $1/2$ on $k=n$.

operators.name: num_functional_gram_schmidt
signatures: ({ item0: Tensor<2, Float[_]>, item1: Tensor<2, Float[_]> }) -> { item0: Tensor<2, Float[_]>, item1: Tensor<2, Float[_]> }
operators.doc: Performs the Gram-Schmidt process to orthogonalize a set of functions. All functions must have the same sampling points.

operators.name: num_functional_gram_schmidt_orthonormal
signatures: ({ item0: Tensor<2, Float[_]>, item1: Tensor<2, Float[_]> }) -> { item0: Tensor<2, Float[_]>, item1: Tensor<2, Float[_]> }
operators.doc:
Performs the Gram-Schmidt process to orthonormalize a set of functions.

# Errors
Returns an error if any pair of input functions has mismatched sample points.

operators.name: num_functional_infinity_norm
signatures: ({ item0: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, item1: Tensor<1, Float[_]> }) -> Float[_]
operators.doc:
Calculates the L-infinity norm of a function represented by discrete points.

The L-infinity norm (or Chebyshev norm) is defined as `max(|f(x)|)`. For discrete points,
it is simply the maximum absolute value among the sampled points.

# Arguments
* `points` - A slice of `(x, y)` tuples representing the function's samples.

# Returns
The numerical value of the L-infinity norm.

operators.name: num_functional_inner_product
signatures: ({ item0: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, item1: Tensor<1, Float[_]> }, { item0: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, item1: Tensor<1, Float[_]> }) -> Float[_]
operators.doc:
Calculates the inner product of two functions, `<f, g> = ∫f(x)g(x)dx`.

Both functions must be sampled at the same x-coordinates. For discrete points,
it is approximated as `Σ f(x_i)g(x_i)Δx_i`.

# Arguments
* `f_points` - A slice of `(x, y)` tuples representing the first function's samples.
* `g_points` - A slice of `(x, y)` tuples representing the second function's samples.

# Returns
A `Result` containing the numerical value of the inner product.

# Errors
Returns an error if the input functions have different numbers of sample points.

operators.name: num_functional_l1_norm
signatures: ({ item0: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, item1: Tensor<1, Float[_]> }) -> Float[_]
operators.doc:
Calculates the L1 norm of a function represented by discrete points.

The L1 norm (or Manhattan norm) is defined as `∫|f(x)|dx`. For discrete points,
it is approximated as `Σ|y_i|Δx_i`.

# Arguments
* `points` - A slice of `(x, y)` tuples representing the function's samples.

# Returns
The numerical value of the L1 norm.

operators.doc:
Prepares trapezoidal L2 weights for finite nondecreasing coordinates. The result can be reused for independent sampled fields on the same axis. Repeated coordinates contribute zero panel width.

operators.name: num_functional_l2_grid_norm
operators.doc:
Returns the sampled L2 norm, with dimension equal to the ordinates' dimension times the square root of the axis dimension. Returns a domain error if the norm overflows Float.

Returns an error for the wrong number of ordinates or a nonfinite one.

operators.name: num_functional_l2_grid_norm_and_normalize
operators.doc:
Returns {norm, normalized} from one reduction. The measured norm is None if it overflows Float. Normalized ordinates carry the inverse square root of the axis dimension and are None for zero measure. Normalization uses the unrounded scale, including when the norm underflows or overflows.

Returns the L2 norm and normalized ordinates from one reduction.

Zero measure leaves the ordinates as supplied. If the rounded norm
overflows or underflows, normalization still uses its internal scale.

# Errors
Returns an error for the wrong number of ordinates or a nonfinite one.

operators.name: num_functional_l2_norm
signatures: ({ item0: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, item1: Tensor<1, Float[_]> }) -> Float[_]
operators.doc:
Calculates the L2 norm of a function represented by discrete points.

The L2 norm is `sqrt(∫|f(x)|²dx)`. For samples, the integral is the
trapezoidal rule applied to the squared ordinates. On a finite
nondecreasing grid, repeated coordinates give zero-width panels.

# Arguments
* `points` - A slice of `(x, y)` tuples representing the function's samples.

# Returns
The numerical value of the L2 norm.

operators.doc:

Zero measure leaves the samples as supplied. Normalization uses the

centres, and re-derives [`Acoustics::dt`] and the PML from the result.

The density on a face is the harmonic mean of the two cells it
separates and the bulk modulus of a cell is `ρc²`, which is what keeps
the scheme second order across an interface (an interface is exact when
it lies on a face). Call this before stepping: the fields, the clock and
the sources are left alone.

signatures: (rssn/native/bem-mesh/v1, Tensor<1, String>, Tensor<1, Float>, Bool) -> rssn/native/bem-solution/v1
operators.doc:
Solves the interior or exterior Laplace problem with linear elements. Each vertex has one Potential or Flux coefficient in the supplied frame's field or field-per-length reference. Use the boundary-field accessor for the resulting vertex coefficients.

Solves the interior Laplace problem with **continuous piecewise-linear**
potential and flux on the triangulated surface, by collocation at the
vertices (dense LU).

`bcs` gives the data per **vertex**: the potential or the derivative along
the outward normal. Single-layer integrals use adaptive subdivision away
from the collocation point and a Duffy transformation for the elements
that contain it; the double-layer kernel vanishes on those (planar)
elements, and the free-term/diagonal is fixed by the rigid-body identity
`Σ_j H_ij = 0`. Exterior problems: pass `exterior = true` (orientation
reversed and the flux sign convention of
[`solve_laplace_bem_3d_exterior`]).

# Errors
For an invalid mesh, wrong data length, or a singular system (pure Neumann
interior problems are singular).

operators.name: num_grid_bem_p1_aca
signatures: (rssn/native/bem-mesh/v1, Tensor<1, String>, Tensor<1, Float>, Bool, Int, Float, Float, Int, Int) -> rssn/native/bem-solution/v1
operators.doc:
Solves the interior or exterior Laplace problem with ACA-compressed linear elements and GMRES. Each vertex has one Potential or Flux coefficient in the supplied frame's field or field-per-length reference. The positive tolerance, at most one, controls both ACA and GMRES.

Solves the Laplace problem with **linear (P1) elements** like
[`solve_laplace_bem_3d_p1`], but with hierarchical-matrix compression.

The vertex collocation matrices `G` and `H` are assembled lazily from the
element integrals (adaptive subdivision away from the collocation point,
Duffy transformation on elements containing it), far blocks of the vertex
cluster tree are compressed by adaptive cross approximation, the rigid-body
diagonal of `H` follows from one compressed matrix-vector product with the
vector of ones, and the system is solved by Jacobi-preconditioned GMRES.

# Errors
For an invalid mesh, wrong data length, non-finite data, a pure Neumann
interior problem (singular) or GMRES failure.

This function discretizes the boundary of the domain into elements and applies

# Arguments

* `bcs` - A `Vec` of `BoundaryCondition` for each element, specifying known potential or flux.

# Returns

if the system is ill-posed or has no unique solution.

operators.name: num_grid_bem_solve3
operators.doc:
Native BEM call. Numeric coordinates are normalized by the supplied PDE frame length, potentials by its field reference, and fluxes by field/length. Outputs retain explicit physical reference witnesses.

Solves the 3D Laplace equation inside a closed triangulated surface by
the collocation Boundary Element Method with constant elements.

The potential `u` and flux `q = du/dn` (outward normal) are piecewise
constant on the triangles and collocated at their centroids. Per
element, `bcs` prescribes either the potential (Dirichlet) or the flux
(Neumann); the other quantity is solved for. The discretised boundary
integral equation is
`sum_j Hhat_ij u_j = sum_j G_ij q_j`, with the single-layer kernel
`G = 1 / (4 pi r)` integrated over each triangle by adaptive
subdivision with a 7-point Gauss rule (the singular self term analytically),
the double-layer coefficients `H_ij = -Omega_ij / (4 pi)` given exactly by
the solid angle subtended by element `j` at the collocation point `i`, and
the free-term diagonal fixed by the rigid-body-motion identity
`sum_j Hhat_ij = 0`.

With Neumann data on every element the potential is determined only up
to an additive constant; it is then fixed by the condition that the
area-weighted mean of `u` vanishes, and the fluxes must satisfy the
compatibility condition `sum_j q_j A_j = 0` to within `1e-6` of the flux
scale.

For repeated values with the same mesh and boundary kinds, use
[`PreparedLaplaceBem3d`].

# Errors
Fails for an invalid mesh (see [`SurfaceMesh3D::validate`]), a number of
boundary conditions different from the number of triangles, non-finite
data, an incompatible pure-Neumann problem, or a singular system. Reports
cancellation.

operators.name: num_grid_bem_solve3_prepared
operators.doc:
Solves for new per-triangle boundary values using prepared Laplace operators. Potentials are expressed in the mesh's field reference and fluxes in field per length. * `dx` - The spatial step size.
* `dt` - The time step.

operators.name: num_grid_cnm_solve_heat_equation_2d_cn_adi
signatures: (rssn/native/pde-frame/v1, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<1, Float>, Float, Float, Int) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:

operators.doc:
Advances a 2D heat field with Crank–Nicolson ADI. The x-fastest initial field provides all four fixed Dirichlet edges, which retain their values throughout the solve. Supply spacing in units of length_reference, diffusivity in length_reference^2/time_reference, the time step in time_reference, and temperature in value_reference. The returned field keeps its grid references.

Evolves a two-dimensional heat field with fixed Dirichlet boundaries.

The x-fastest initial field supplies the four boundary edges. They remain
fixed during both ADI half-steps. The grid has `nx * ny` nodes, including
the boundaries. Spacings must be positive, and diffusivity and the time
step must be nonnegative. A grid without interior nodes is stationary.

# Errors

Returns an error for shape mismatches, non-finite data or results, invalid
physical parameters, unrepresentable coefficients, or cancellation.

operators.name: num_grid_dimensional_heat_adi
signatures: (rssn/native/pde-frame/v1, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<1, Float>, Float, Float, Int) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Actual native grid/transform method in explicit Length/Time/field references; arrays and coefficients are normalized in that frame and native x-fastest storage is retained. Method identity, FFT normalization, boundary semantics and bounded work/history are preserved.

Crank-Nicolson heat equation `u_t = D Δu` with zero Dirichlet boundaries on
a 1D, 2D or 3D grid, advanced `steps` steps of size `dt`.

The step is the factorised (Beam-Warming) approximate-factorisation form
`Π_a (I - ρ_a δ²_a) uⁿ⁺¹ = Π_a (I + ρ_a δ²_a) uⁿ` with `ρ_a = D dt / (2 h_a²)`:
unconditionally stable, second order in space and time, one tridiagonal solve
per line and axis. For data that is a product of functions of the single axes
it equals the product of the 1D Crank-Nicolson solutions. Boundary entries of
`u0` are ignored (treated as zero).

# Errors
For inconsistent shapes, non-positive `dt`, negative diffusivity, or an
unrepresentable diffusion coefficient at the given spacing and time step.
A cancelled computation also returns an error.

operators.name: num_grid_dimensional_poisson
signatures: (rssn/native/pde-frame/v1, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<1, Float>, String, None | Some(Float), Int, Float) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Actual native grid/transform method in explicit Length/Time/field references; arrays and coefficients are normalized in that frame and native x-fastest storage is retained. Method identity, FFT normalization, boundary semantics and bounded work/history are preserved.

Solves `∇²u = f` on a 1D, 2D or 3D grid by a stationary iteration.

`u0` is the initial guess; its boundary nodes are the (fixed) Dirichlet
data. Iteration stops when the largest update is below `tolerance` or after
`max_iter` sweeps. With a 1D grid this is the scalar tridiagonal iteration,
with `dims = [nx, ny]` it reproduces
[`crate::sim::physics_cfd::solve_poisson_2d_jacobi`] and friends.

# Errors
For inconsistent shapes, spacings or lengths.

operators.name: num_grid_dimensional_schrodinger
signatures: (rssn/native/pde-frame/v1, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<1, Complex>, Tensor<1, Float>, Float, Int) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Native nondimensional Crank-Nicolson Schrodinger equation i*psi_t=-Delta(psi)/2+V*psi. The explicit frame restores kinetic coefficient L²/(2T), potential frequency 1/T and complex amplitude units; it does not silently choose SI hbar or mass. Native spacing, method, layout and work bounds are retained.

Schrodinger equation `i ψ_t = -½ Δψ + V ψ` (ħ = m = 1) with zero Dirichlet
boundaries on a 1D, 2D or 3D grid.

One step is the symmetric splitting `e^{-iV dt/2} · Π_a C_a · e^{-iV dt/2}`
where `C_a = (I + i dt/2 K_a)⁻¹ (I - i dt/2 K_a)` is the Crank-Nicolson
(Cayley) step of the one-dimensional kinetic operator `K_a = -½ δ²_a`. The
kinetic factors commute, every factor is unitary, so the scheme is second
order in space and time and conserves the norm to round-off. For `V = 0` and
separable data it equals the product of 1D Crank-Nicolson solutions.

# Errors
For inconsistent shapes, non-positive `dt`, or cancellation.

signatures: (rssn/native/transport-equation/v1, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<1, Float>, Float, Int) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Actual native grid/transform method in explicit Length/Time/field references; arrays and coefficients are normalized in that frame and native x-fastest storage is retained. Method identity, FFT normalization, boundary semantics and bounded work/history are preserved.

Advances a [`Transport`] equation `steps` explicit Euler steps on a 1D, 2D
or 3D grid and returns all `steps + 1` snapshots (the first is `u0`).

The scheme is only conditionally stable: keep `Σ|c_a| dt/h_a <= 1` and
`2 α dt Σ 1/h_a² <= 1`.

# Errors
For inconsistent shapes, a velocity list of the wrong length, invalid time
controls, too many snapshots, or cancellation.

operators.doc:
Advance the retained transport equation and record step 0, positive multiples of save_every, and the final step. Data, spacings, and time steps are normalized in the equation's Length/Time/field frame. Returns x-fastest fields as rows with their physical reference. Work and retained history are bounded independently.

Advances a [`Transport`] equation and retains snapshots at a fixed step cadence.

The result holds step 0, every positive multiple of `save_every` through
`steps`, and the final step if it is off cadence. The initial and final state
share one snapshot when `steps` is zero. Boundary and stability conventions
are those of [`solve_transport_nd`].

# Errors
For an inconsistent grid or equation, zero cadence, or an unrepresentable
snapshot count, or cancellation.

operators.name: num_grid_dimensional_wave
signatures: (rssn/native/pde-frame/v1, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<1, Float>, Float, Float, Int) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Actual native grid/transform method in explicit Length/Time/field references; arrays and coefficients are normalized in that frame and native x-fastest storage is retained. Method identity, FFT normalization, boundary semantics and bounded work/history are preserved.

Explicit leapfrog for `u_tt = c² Δu` with zero Dirichlet boundaries on a
1D, 2D or 3D grid. Returns the `steps + 1` snapshots (`u0`, `u1`, ...), the
first step using the initial velocity `ut0` (Taylor start).

# Errors

speed or invalid time step, cancellation, or a violated CFL condition
`|c| dt sqrt(Σ 1/h_a²) <= 1` (with a `10⁻¹²` rounding allowance).

operators.name: num_grid_fdm_adaptive_evolve
signatures: (rssn/native/pde-frame/v1, Tensor<1, Float>, Int, Tensor<1, Float>, { t0: Float, t1: Float, rtol: Float, atol: Float, h0: Float, h_min: Float, h_max: Float, max_steps: Int, max_step_calls: Int, max_rejections: Int }, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, Int) -> Dyn<term>

Actual generic native adaptive controller over caller-provided compiled step/stability/event functions. Each scalar step output takes coherent [time,step,state...] and has field units; stability takes [time,state...] and returns Time, optional event returns dimensionless. Controls/state arrays are normalized in the explicit frame; order is the supplied stepper's actual order. Native step doubling, rejection/work budgets and terminal-event localization are preserved.

Adapt any restartable PDE step kernel with a step-doubling error estimate.

one positive entry per state coefficient. `stability` returns the maximum
stable step for the current state, or positive infinity for an implicit
scheme. Temporal control cannot certify spatial discretization error.
An accepted endpoint on the event uses its existing validated state.

# Errors

kernel, or a non-finite event. Tolerance violations are never force-accepted.

operators.name: num_grid_fem_error_indicators
operators.doc:
Native simplex finite-element method with explicit geometry/time/field references. Diffusivity is normalized by L²/T, reaction by1/T, source by U/T; compiled callbacks use coherent coordinates and retained physical output domains. Mesh/DOF/refinement/callback work bounds are checked.

Residual error indicators `η_T`, one per cell, of a P1 or P2 solution.

`η_T² = h_T² ∫_T (f(t,·) - c u_h + ∇·(k ∇u_h))² dx
      + Σ_{e ⊂ ∂T} ½ h_e ∫_e [k ∂_n u_h]² ds`,

with `h_T` and `h_e` the diameters of the cell and of its faces. The face
sum runs over interior faces only, so the estimator measures the
discretisation error of the differential equation, not the approximation
of non-homogeneous boundary data. For P1 the element term is `f - c u_h`
(`∇·(k ∇u_h) = 0`); for P2 the constant `k Δu_h` is included. In 1D the
face term is empty (the jump lives on a set of measure zero).

operators.name: num_grid_fem_error_indicators_var
operators.doc:
Native simplex finite-element method with explicit geometry/time/field references. Diffusivity is normalized by L²/T, reaction by1/T, source by U/T; compiled callbacks use coherent coordinates and retained physical output domains. Mesh/DOF/refinement/callback work bounds are checked.

[`error_indicators`] for spatially varying `k(x)`, `c(x)`:

`η_T² = h_T² ∫_T (f - c(x) u_h + ∇·(k ∇u_h))² + Σ_e ½ h_e ∫_e [k(x) ∂_n u_h]²`,

with `∇·(k ∇u_h) = k Δu_h + ∇k · ∇u_h` (the gradient of `k` by central differences of
the closure at the quadrature points, nominal step `10⁻⁶ h_T`) and `k`
evaluated at the quadrature points of the face in the jump. At floating-
point limits the difference uses distinct finite representable coordinates
and their actual spacing.

operators.name: num_grid_fem_solve_adaptive

A conservative worst-case refinement/DOF bound is checked before native allocation; actual returned space, field and estimator history are retained.

Adaptive solution of the static problem: solve, estimate, mark and refine.

Starting from `mesh`, the loop solves `-∇·(k ∇u) + c u = f(t, x)` with
[`solve_static`], estimates the error with [`error_indicators`], marks the
smallest set of cells whose indicators carry the fraction `theta` of
`Σ η_T²` (Dörfler marking), refines them with
[`SimplexMesh::refine_marked`] and repeats. It stops when the total
estimate is at most `tolerance` or after `max_steps` refinements (so at
most `max_steps + 1` solves). `degree` selects P1 or P2.

# Errors
If `degree` is not 1 or 2, `theta` is outside `(0, 1]`, `max_steps` is
zero, or one of the solves fails.

Static solution by load stepping and Newton iterations.

The load is applied in `steps` equal increments (the displacement data, tractions and body force

signatures: (rssn/native/legacy-fdm-grid/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, Int) -> { steps: Tensor<1, Int>, grid_shape: Tensor<1, Int>, data: Dyn<term> }
operators.doc:
Advances a 2D or 3D homogeneous Dirichlet wave from a measured displacement grid and a flat rate tensor in displacement/time. Give measured length spacings, a speed, a signed time step, a step count and a positive save cadence. Samples contain step zero, cadence multiples and the final step. Each row of data is a measured displacement field with x fastest. grid_shape gives the field extents and steps gives the completed step indices.

Evolves a two- or three-dimensional Dirichlet wave and retains step samples.

Initial displacement and velocity share a grid. Faces are zero from the
initial sample onward. Retains step zero, every multiple of `save_every`,
and the last step. Time advances by the signed step `dt`.

# Errors
Invalid shapes, spacing, speed, time step or cadence, a violated leapfrog
CFL bound, non-finite data or states, allocation limits, or cancellation.

Explicit native Float FDM-grid and sampled-initializer specialization. Measured field/coefficient/time/spacing inputs are normalized by retained physical references. Grid, CFL, work and data bounds precede native work; BC callbacks retain native errors.

Positive step counts impose homogeneous Dirichlet values from the
initial time. With zero steps the function returns the raw initial samples.
Use time steps satisfying `(c dt / dx)^2 + (c dt / dy)^2 <= 1`.

step counts. With zero steps the function returns the raw initial samples.

signatures: (rssn/native/legacy-fvm-mesh/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Advances a retained 1D finite-volume mesh with an upwind flux. Supply a one-entry measured Length/Time velocity, a positive measured Time step, an integer step count, and the left and right ghost-cell values in the mesh field dimension. Both ghost values are validated.

CFL must be at most one. The upwind face uses the ghost value on the side from which the flow enters. Step count and cell-step work are bounded.

The measured field is returned in increasing cell order and replaces the retained field on success. An invalid input or unrepresentable output leaves the previous field intact.

operators.name: num_grid_legacy_fvm_advection2
operators.doc:
Actual native finite-volume specialization. Measured field, velocity, length and time retain explicit reference units. Sampled initializer arrays and finite boundary masks instantiate generic native functions; masks must cover exterior cells. Returned values update the retained mesh. Native CFL, work and allocation bounds are checked.

Solves the 2D linear advection equation using the Finite Volume Method.

operators.name: num_grid_legacy_fvm_advection3
operators.doc:
Advances the retained 3D finite-volume mesh using measured velocity and timestep. The Boolean mask is flat in x-fastest order or shaped [depth, height, width]. True cells are set to zero on each step. Unmarked exterior cells use zero inflow and free outflow. Returns a flat measured field in x-fastest order. CFL and work bounds are checked.

Advances the 3D linear advection equation with first-order upwind fluxes.

The callback marks cells to set to zero on each time step. All other cells
use a zero exterior state at an inflow face and their own state at an
outflow face. The returned values use the mesh's x-fastest storage order.

For stability, choose `dt` so that the sum of the three directional
Courant numbers `dt * |velocity| / spacing` is at most one.

# Panics
Panics if a mesh advanced for at least one step has inconsistent extents
and cell storage.

operators.doc:
Actual native finite-volume specialization. Measured field, velocity, length and time retain explicit reference units. Native CFL, work and allocation bounds are checked.

2D shallow water equations `h_t + (hu)_x + (hv)_y = 0`, ...

On a grid of `dims = [nx, ny]` cells (flat, `x` fastest) with the Lax-Friedrichs flux and
zero-gradient boundaries. 2D counterpart of [`solve_shallow_water_1d`]; the
numerical viscosity is shared between the two axes (unsplit scheme), so it
smears slightly more than the 1D routine on y-independent data. Stable for
`(|u| + sqrt(g h)) dt (1/dx + 1/dy) <= 1` (roughly).

# Errors
For a length mismatch or non-positive step sizes.

3D barotropic shallow-water system `h_t + ∇·(h u) = 0`,
`(h u)_t + ∇·(h u ⊗ u) + ∇(g h²/2) = 0`.

Euler with `γ = 2`, `p = g h²/2` and no
energy equation: the 3D analogue of the planar shallow-water equations.

three axes (unsplit scheme). Stable for

# Errors
For a length mismatch or non-positive step sizes.

This function implements the Jacobi iterative method to solve the Poisson equation
on a 2D grid with Dirichlet boundary conditions (implicitly handled by the iteration
not updating boundary points). It is suitable for steady-state problems.

# Arguments
* `f` - Source term (2D grid) as a `Matrix<f64>`.
* `u0` - Initial guess for `u` (2D grid) as a `Matrix<f64>`.
* `dx`, `dy` - Grid spacing in x and y directions.
* `max_iter` - Maximum number of iterations.
* `tolerance` - Convergence tolerance for the maximum difference between successive iterations.

# Returns
A `Matrix<f64>` representing the solution `u`.

signatures: (rssn/native/pde-frame/v1, Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int, Int) -> Float
operators.doc:
Returns the dimensionless open fraction along one, two, or three distinct zero-based axes. Normalize the three origin and length slots by the frame's Length reference and supply positive lengths on the active axes.

The compiled field takes three coherent Length coordinates and returns Length. Positive signed distances are open. One active axis uses segment root refinement. Two or three active axes use adaptive subdivision and simplex clipping.

The depth cap is 12 and depth times the number of axes is at most 18. The independent callback budget accepts 1 through 8,388,608 evaluations. Invalid geometry, callback units or arity, nonfinite samples and budget exhaustion produce errors.

operators.doc:
Returns the dimensionless open fraction of an axis-aligned segment. Axis indices are zero based. Normalize the three origin coordinates and positive segment length by the frame's Length reference.

The compiled field takes three coherent Length coordinates and returns Length. Positive distances are open. The kernel samples the segment, then bisects intervals where its sampled sign changes.

The callback budget accepts 1 through 8,388,608 evaluations, including refinement. Invalid geometry, callback units or arity, nonfinite samples, and exhausted evaluation budgets produce errors.

The cells are stored flat, with x fastest. Uses the multi-dimensional
Lax–Friedrichs flux with equal numerical-viscosity shares per axis and
zero-gradient outflow boundaries. The one-dimensional stencil agrees with

signatures: (rssn/native/pde-frame/v1, Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Float>, Float, Int, Tensor<1, String>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Solves the multidimensional Burgers equation by conservative Lax–Friedrichs fluxes. Use a velocity-valued frame. The flat initial field is in units of value_reference with x fastest, spacing in units of length_reference, and dt in units of time_reference. Supply Periodic or Outflow for both faces of each axis. The CFL bound holds separately on each axis. The returned field keeps all three references.

Advances Burgers' equation with a boundary choice for each active axis.

Uses the same Lax–Friedrichs flux on both sides of an interface. A
fully periodic grid conserves the sum of cell averages up to roundoff.
Zero-gradient faces allow the boundary physical flux to leave or enter
the grid. For the equal viscosity shares used here, a sufficient
monotonicity condition is `D * dt * max|u| <= h[a]` on each active axis,
where `D` is the number of axes. At fixed grid spacing, the one-step
limit as `dt` tends to zero retains Lax–Friedrichs averaging.

# Errors
An invalid grid, boundary count, initial field, or step size, or a flux
or state that cannot be represented.

Refines the cells flagged in `marked` by conforming edge bisection.

Every marked tetrahedron is split at the midpoints of its six edges
into eight tetrahedra. The split is carried out as recursive
bisection: a cell is cut along its longest split edge (ties broken by
vertex indices) and the two halves are cut again until no split edge
is left.
Only midpoints of edges of marked cells are inserted, so an unmarked
neighbour is cut along exactly the edges it shares with marked cells
(**red–green closure**) and a cell without a split edge is kept. Both
cells sharing a face cut that face from the same edge midpoints to the
opposite vertex of the face, hence there are no hanging nodes.
Boundary facets inherit the marker of the parent facet containing
them. The refinement level of every produced cell is one more than the
level of its parent; cells that are not touched keep their level.

In 1D and 2D the same scheme splits a marked cell into 2 or 4 cells.
Entries of `marked` past the last cell are ignored.

operators.name: num_homology_abelianization
operators.doc:
Native exact algebraic topology with session-owned, kind/version checked complex, chain and presentation handles. Complex inputs/exports use CSR offsets/indices. Handles are invalid in other sessions and after release; all objects own their data. Finite construction bounds: 4096 simplices, 12 vertices per simplex, 65536 face/storage words, 256 generators per chain group and 128 x 128 exact matrix elimination. Presentation simplification accepts sixteen generators and 256 input word coefficients with the native 4000-word intermediate limit; product frontiers are bounded to 1048576 coefficient slots. Cubical chains accept 64 pixels; direct cubical Betti accepts 4096. Filtrations carry a canonical value_unit witness verified against stored radius dimensions. Bars use explicit essential flags and zero death placeholders; bottleneck inputs are births/deaths/essential records and unequal essential counts give positive infinity. Products return None on their native simplex limit; malformed inputs and adapter budget exhaustion are errors. Pure source algorithms are invoked in RSSN kernels; opaque payloads contain only session handles, never serialized pointers.
