signatures: (rssn/native/sim/particle-cloud/v1, rssn/native/sim/gaussian-stream/v1, Dyn<term>, Int, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, ({ masses: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, positions: Tensor<2, Float[_]>, velocities: Tensor<2, Float[_]>, forces: Tensor<2, Float[_]>, charges: Tensor<1, Float[_]> }) -> Tensor<2, Float[_]>) -> Dyn<term>

half kick (B), half drift (A), exact Ornstein–Uhlenbeck velocity update

operators.name: num_native_md_integrate_nose_hoover
signatures: (rssn/native/sim/particle-cloud/v1, Dyn<term>, Int, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, ({ masses: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, positions: Tensor<2, Float[_]>, velocities: Tensor<2, Float[_]>, forces: Tensor<2, Float[_]>, charges: Tensor<1, Float[_]> }) -> Tensor<2, Float[_]>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Physical particle adapter. Coordinates, velocity, mass, charge, force, energy and thermal targets use checked reference units; count, shape and work bounds precede native work.

The Nosé–Hoover thermostat:

the friction `ξ` obeys `Q dξ/dt = Σ m v² - N_f kT`, a deterministic
extended system whose invariant `H + Q ξ²/2 + N_f kT s` (with `ds/dt =
ξ`) is conserved. Velocity-Verlet with the friction applied as an exact
exponential scaling in half steps. Returns the final `(ξ, s)`.

# Errors
Propagates errors of the force calculation.

operators.name: num_native_md_integrate_velocity_verlet
signatures: (rssn/native/sim/particle-cloud/v1, Dyn<term>, Int, Int, ({ masses: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, positions: Tensor<2, Float[_]>, velocities: Tensor<2, Float[_]>, forces: Tensor<2, Float[_]>, charges: Tensor<1, Float[_]> }) -> Tensor<2, Float[_]>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Physical particle adapter. Coordinates, velocity, mass, charge, force, energy and thermal targets use checked reference units; count, shape and work bounds precede native work.

Integrates the equations of motion for a system of particles using the Velocity Verlet algorithm.

The Velocity Verlet algorithm is a popular numerical integration scheme for molecular dynamics
simulations. It is time-reversible and preserves phase space volume, making it suitable
for long-term simulations.

# Arguments
* `particles` - A mutable vector of `Particle`s.
* `dt` - The time step.
* `num_steps` - The number of simulation steps.
* `force_calculator` - A closure that computes the total force on each particle.
  It takes `&mut Vec<Particle>` and returns `Result<(), String>`.

# Returns
A `Vec<Vec<Particle>>` representing the trajectory of the particles over time.

# Errors
Returns an error if the force calculator fails or if vector operations fail due to dimension mismatch.

The Lennard-Jones potential is a simple mathematical model that describes the
interaction between a pair of neutral atoms or molecules. It has a repulsive
term at short distances and an attractive term at long distances.

# Arguments
* `p1`, `p2` - The two particles.
* `epsilon` - The depth of the potential well.
* `sigma` - The finite distance at which the inter-particle potential is zero.

# Returns
A tuple `(potential, force_on_p1)` where `potential` is the scalar potential energy
and `force_on_p1` is the force vector acting on `p1` due to `p2`.

# Errors

# Arguments
* `p1`, `p2` - The two particles
* `de` - Dissociation energy
* `a` - Controls the width of the potential well
* `re` - Equilibrium bond distance

Separations below `1e-9` return infinite energy and a zero force vector.
[`morse_radial`] evaluates the scalar curve at all nonnegative distances.


# Errors
Returns an error if the particles have different dimensions.

operators.name: num_native_md_morse_radial
operators.doc:
Evaluate the Morse energy and signed radial force in a checked reference frame. Energy is zero at the equilibrium distance. Positive force points toward increasing separation. A zero separation returns the one-sided radial force.

Returns the Morse energy and the force along increasing distance.

The minimum is zero at `r = re`. At `r = 0` the scalar force is the
one-sided radial derivative with a negative sign. There is no direction
to assign to that force at coincident particle positions.

# Errors
The distance, depth and equilibrium distance must be finite and
nonnegative. The inverse length `a` must be finite and positive.
Returns an error when the energy or radial force exceeds finite range.

operators.name: num_native_mtm_solve_poisson_1d_multigrid
operators.doc:
Actual native zero-Dirichlet multigrid on its unit interval/cube, mapped to an explicit physical coordinate and solution reference. RHS has solution/coordinate^2 units.1D input contains interior values;2D/3D input includes boundary nodes. Output is flattened in native x-fastest order with explicit shape.

Solves the 1D Poisson equation `-u_xx = f` using the multigrid method.

# Arguments
* `n` - Number of interior points on the finest grid. Must be `2^k - 1`.
* `f` - The right-hand side function values on the finest grid.
* `num_cycles` - The number of V-cycles to perform.

# Returns
The solution vector `u`.

# Errors

This function will return an error if the grid size `n` is not of the form `2^k - 1`.

operators.name: num_native_mtm_solve_poisson_2d_multigrid
operators.doc:
Actual native zero-Dirichlet multigrid on its unit interval/cube, mapped to an explicit physical coordinate and solution reference. RHS has solution/coordinate^2 units.1D input contains interior values;2D/3D input includes boundary nodes. Output is flattened in native x-fastest order with explicit shape.

Solves `-∇²u = f` on the unit square by running `num_cycles` multigrid V-cycles.

Input and output are both flattened with x varying fastest. All boundary
values are fixed to zero, and source entries on those boundaries are ignored.
With zero cycles, or with a boundary-only 2×2 grid, the result is all zeros.

# Errors

Returns an error if `n` is not of the form `2^k + 1` for a nonnegative integer
`k`, or if `f` does not have exactly `n * n` entries.

operators.name: num_native_mtm_solve_poisson_3d_multigrid
operators.doc:
Actual native zero-Dirichlet multigrid on its unit interval/cube, mapped to an explicit physical coordinate and solution reference. RHS has solution/coordinate^2 units.1D input contains interior values;2D/3D input includes boundary nodes. Output is flattened in native x-fastest order with explicit shape.

Solves the 3D Poisson equation `-Δu = f` on the unit cube.

Zero Dirichlet boundary, `n` nodes per axis including the boundary, `x` fastest, `n = 2^k + 1`)
with `num_cycles` multigrid V-cycles. 3D counterpart of
[`solve_poisson_2d_multigrid`]; the general 1D/2D/3D entry point with any
boundary conditions is [`solve_poisson_multigrid_nd`].

# Errors

This function will return an error if `n` is not of the form `2^k + 1`, if
`f.len() != n^3` or if the multigrid hierarchy cannot be built.

Shape, unit, and allocation bounds are checked at construction.

Prepares a shared grid for calls to [`Self::evaluate`].

# Errors
Returns an error if there are no axes, any axis has fewer than two
finite strictly increasing nodes, the size overflows, or the values
are non-finite or have the wrong length.

Wait, `reverse(e_i` `e_j`) = `e_j` `e_i` = -`e_i` `e_j`. So bivectors are negated.

Native scaled global/constrained optimization with shared actual host evaluation limit. Nelder: x,xscale,yscale,step,tol,iterations,budget,f. Differential evolution: lo,hi,xscale,yscale,population,generations,budget,seed,f. Annealing: x,xscale,yscale,step,temperature,cooling,iterations,budget,seed,f. Constrained: x,xscale,yscale,equality_scale,inequality_scale,tol,iterations,budget,f,eq,ineq. Constraints independently carry C/H units; SQP returns physical multipliers E/C and E/H, native status and second-order verdict. Second-order: x,lambda,mu,xscale,yscale,eqscale,ineqscale,budget,f,eq,ineq. No global-optimality claim; native iteration/status semantics retained.

Each row contains [`Self::dimension`] values. Large batches use bounded
shards and combine them in row order, independent of worker count.
An empty batch leaves the accumulator unchanged.

# Errors

operators.name: num_native_online_covariance_push_frequency_batch

Atomically incorporate a row-major tensor of observations with the accumulator's coordinate units and one nonnegative, dimensionless integer frequency per row. Each frequency counts repeated observations without expanding the tensor.

Incorporate a flat row-major batch with an integer frequency per row.

Each row represents as many identical observations as its frequency,
with no need to expand those observations. A zero frequency adds no
observations. All row values must be finite. The resulting count is the
sum of frequencies and the previous count. Sample covariance divides
by the resulting count minus one. Floating-point results can differ
from pushing each repetition individually. Shards and their merge order
are independent of worker count.

# Errors
An incomplete row, a frequency vector of the wrong length, a non-finite
value, count or arithmetic overflow, or a shard allocation failure
leaves the accumulator unchanged.

`perm[new] = old` names the original vertex at each reordered position.

entries leave both metrics unchanged. The work is linear in the number

accumulated profile does not fit a `usize`.

operators.name: num_native_qs_factor
operators.doc:
Checked native method over explicitly normalized values. Session/kind, shape and work/allocation bounds are enforced.

Finds a non-trivial divisor of the odd composite `n`.

Returns `Some(d)` with `1 < d < n` and `d | n`, or `None` for invalid
input, for a prime, when `n` has more than [`QsLimits::MAX_DIGITS`]
decimal digits, when the relation matrix would exceed
[`QsLimits::MAX_FACTOR_BASE_COLUMNS`], and when the polynomial or
[`QsLimits::max_sieve_positions`] budget is exhausted. An even `n > 2`
returns `2` directly.

The input may contain small factors: trial division by the primes
below 1000 runs first and returns a factor directly. The digit limit is
checked before that trial division, so an oversized request never does
any sieving work. Perfect powers, prime input and even input are
otherwise handled before the sieve. The limits are not clamped upwards
or downwards to hide a bad choice: they are used as given, apart from a
safety clamp on `bound` and `interval`.

operators.name: num_native_qs_factor_pair
signatures: (Int, rssn/native/discrete/qs-limits/v1) -> None | Some({ item0: Int, item1: Int })
operators.doc:

Splits `n` into two proper factors in ascending order.

Uses the same limits and early factor checks as [`qs_factor`]. The
product of the returned factors is exactly `n`. Either may be composite.

operators.name: num_native_qs_factor_with
operators.doc:
Checked native method over explicitly normalized values. Session/kind, shape and work/allocation bounds are enforced.

The same guarantees hold: the returned divisor is always in
`(1, n)` and divides `n`; `None` means "no factor found", not "n is
composite" or "n is prime".

operators.name: num_native_qs_is_probable_prime
operators.doc:
Checked native method over explicitly normalized values. Session/kind, shape and work/allocation bounds are enforced.

A Baillie-PSW probable-prime test.

Deterministic Miller-Rabin with the first twelve prime bases for
machine words (which is a proof for all of `u64`), and a base-2 strong
probable-prime test plus a strong Lucas test with Selfridge's
parameters for larger integers. No composite is known to pass the
latter, in particular the smallest strong pseudoprime to those twelve
Miller-Rabin bases (318665857834031151167461) does not.

operators.name: num_native_qs_limits_for_digits
operators.doc:
Checked native method over explicitly normalized values. Session/kind, shape and work/allocation bounds are enforced.

Parameter set for a `digits`-digit number.

The factor-base bound is the standard QS optimum
`L_n[1/2, 1/2] = exp(0.5 sqrt(ln n ln ln n))`, rounded up to two
significant digits; the sieve interval is of the same order. The
large-prime multiplier grows with the size, the relation margin is
a small fraction of the estimated factor-base width, and the work
bound is `L_n[1/2, 1] = exp(sqrt(ln n ln ln n))` capped at
`2 * 10^10` positions so that even a hopeless input has a bounded
cost.

For 80 digits this yields a factor base around five million and a
sieve interval of two million, which is beyond the column limit:
the attempt returns `None` before allocating the sieve. At 65 digits
the matrix is already large (tens of thousands of columns and
hundreds of megabytes at the peak), but the work bound still
terminates. Beyond about 66 digits the factor base typically exceeds
the column limit. The remaining primes are checked for direct
divisors before the attempt returns.

operators.doc: Checked native method over explicitly normalized values. Session/kind, shape and work/allocation bounds are enforced.

An example scenario simulating a wave packet hitting a double slit.

# Errors

This function will return an error if the underlying `run_schrodinger_simulation` fails
or if the final state cannot be written to the NPY file.
The last sampled density is saved as `schrodinger_double_slit.npy` inside

Advances the two-dimensional periodic Schrödinger model with a positive time increment. Input lengths, mass, reduced Planck constant and potential use SI dimensions. Returns inverse-length final amplitudes, inverse-square-length density after steps 1, 11, 21 and so on, and their measured times. Samples have the x coordinate varying fastest.

Evolves the periodic 2D wave by Strang splitting and returns density frames.

Frames are sampled after steps 1, 11, 21, and so on. Each frame has `ny`
rows and `nx` columns. On success the supplied wave becomes the final state.

# Errors
Invalid geometry or samples, an unrepresentable phase, wave or density,
failed allocations, or cancellation.

operators.doc:
Evolves a complex wavefunction with inverse-length amplitudes on a prepared periodic grid. The input and final_psi are flattened with x varying fastest. Returns the final wavefunction and time equal to steps multiplied by the signed time increment. Zero steps preserve the initial wave. Uniform potentials can evolve directly to the final state.

Returns the final wave and optionally streams earlier wave samples.

With a stride `s`, the observer sees completed steps `1, 1 + s, ...`
within the requested interval. A zero step count emits no samples.
Pass `None` for final-state-only evolution. A uniform potential can
then be advanced directly in one pair of Fourier transforms.

# Errors
Invalid initial samples or shape, an unrepresentable evolved state,
failed allocations, cancellation or an error from the observer.

Prepares periodic two-dimensional Strang split-step evolution for repeated wavefunctions. Supply positive lengths, mass and reduced Planck constant in physical units, a signed measured time increment, and one energy sample per grid point in x-fast order. Every grid extent is positive. A zero increment gives the identity.

Prepares the signed time increment, grid and physical potential.

The evolution call supplies the step count. The `time_steps` field
controls the legacy snapshot-returning entry point.

# Errors
Returns an error for invalid geometry or coefficients, an
unrepresentable phase angle, or failure to reserve phase storage.

signatures: (rssn/native/relativity-frame/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Float, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Bool) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Trace one Kerr null geodesic from the given observer radius and inclination in radians. Mass, spin, radius and xi use frame lengths and eta uses squared lengths. Returns Captured or Escaped with dimensionless arrival angles.

Traces a null geodesic backwards from the observer.

The impact parameters are `xi = L/E`, `eta = Q/E^2` from the observer at
`(r_o, theta_o)` inwards (initial direction: decreasing `r`, polar motion toward larger
`theta` if `polar_down`) by integrating the Mino-time equations with RK4.

the step budget is exhausted.

the step budget is exhausted.

operators.name: num_native_release

Linear quantity values use coherent units; addition requires matching dimensions, products/quotients and gradients propagate physical powers; transcendental arguments must be dimensionless. No native pointer/state is serialized.

Reverse callbacks use checked NativeAdVar handles on an ephemeral session tape; native operations enforce same-tape identity and a65536-node limit. Output derivatives restore E/D; no numerical differencing or opaque-callback finite-difference fallback.

Exact value and gradient `(f(x), grad f(x))` of `f(&[Var]) -> Var` at `x`
in a single reverse-mode pass.

The first derivative of `f` at `x`, by a central difference with one
Richardson extrapolation step.

operators.doc:
Execute the actual native named scenario with bounded JSON parameters. The contract must be native-schema: JSON numbers use the units documented by that scenario's schema and preserve native defaults. Typed physical quantity APIs are separately exposed for each numerical engine.

Arrays are encoded the way `ndarray` serialises them:

An unknown scenario, parameters that do not parse, or a failure of the
simulation itself.

operators.name: num_native_scenario_run_many

request order.

Every request is evaluated exactly as by [`run`]; the requests share
nothing, so the result is the same as `requests.iter().map(run)` for any
thread count (scenarios that take an explicit `seed` are reproducible;
unseeded stochastic ones are as random as in [`run`]). Nested parallelism
inside a scenario runs on the same rayon pool (work stealing).

operators.name: num_native_second_derivative_scaled
operators.doc:
Native finite-difference calculus with physical reference scales: point,coordinate_scale,value_scale,max_evaluations,[partial index or Jacobian output count],callback. Independent D/E units; derivative E/D, Hessian/Laplacian E/D^2. References are positive. Shared callback errors and finite evaluation budgets are preserved.

operators.name: num_native_second_order_check_scaled
signatures: (Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Float[_], Float[_], Float[_], Float[_], Int, (Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> Float[_], (Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> Tensor<1, Float[_]>, (Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> String
operators.doc:
Native scaled global/constrained optimization with shared actual host evaluation limit. Nelder: x,xscale,yscale,step,tol,iterations,budget,f. Differential evolution: lo,hi,xscale,yscale,population,generations,budget,seed,f. Annealing: x,xscale,yscale,step,temperature,cooling,iterations,budget,seed,f. Constrained: x,xscale,yscale,equality_scale,inequality_scale,tol,iterations,budget,f,eq,ineq. Constraints independently carry C/H units; SQP returns physical multipliers E/C and E/H, native status and second-order verdict. Second-order: x,lambda,mu,xscale,yscale,eqscale,ineqscale,budget,f,eq,ineq. No global-optimality claim; native iteration/status semantics retained.

Second-order sufficiency check at a KKT point `x`.

Builds the dense Hessian of the Lagrangian
`L = f + sum_i lambda_i h_i + sum_j mu_j g_j` by central differences of `L`
itself (so no analytic gradient is required), projects it onto the null
space of the active constraint Jacobian and tests the reduced Hessian for
positive definiteness. Active inequalities are those with `g_j(x)` at least
`-1e-8` or with a strictly positive reported multiplier.

Returns [`SecondOrderStatus::Sufficient`] when the smallest eigenvalue of the
reduced Hessian is larger than a finite-difference margin, and
[`SecondOrderStatus::NotSufficient`] when it is more negative than that
margin. Returns [`SecondOrderStatus::Inconclusive`] when the active
constraint gradients span the whole space (no feasible direction), when the
null space or the eigenproblem cannot be formed, or when the eigenvalue is
inside the margin.

The cost is `O(n^2)` evaluations of `f`, `h` and `g` for the Hessian (each
call is counted as one evaluation), plus the finite-difference Jacobians of
the constraints, and dense `O(n^3)` linear algebra.

operators.name: num_native_sequence_limit
signatures: (Int, Float[_], Float[_], Int, (Float) -> Float[_]) -> { value: Float[_], evaluations: Int }
operators.doc:
Physical native series/sequence convergence. sum_series: start,max_terms,tolerance,value_scale,max_evaluations,term(Float)->E. sequence_limit omits start. Levin: max_terms,value_scale,max_evaluations,term(Int)->E; result includes native error estimate. References/tolerances are positive physical E; callback failures propagate and budgets bound actual host calls.

Finds the limit of the sequence `term(0), term(1), ..., term(max_terms-1)`
by applying Aitken's process repeatedly until the last two accelerated
values differ by less than `tolerance`.

# Errors

Returns an error if a term is not finite, or if the tolerance is not
reached with the given number of terms.

operators.name: num_native_sim_elliptic_elliptic_pi
operators.doc:
Incomplete elliptic integral of the third kind.

`Pi(n; phi, m) = int_0^phi dt / ((1 - n sin^2 t) sqrt(1 - m sin^2 t))` for any real `phi`
(`Pi(phi + j pi) = Pi(phi) + 2 j Pi(n, m)`). Continuation across whole
periods requires `n < 1` and `m < 1`. A principal-interval path is real
when both `n sin^2 t < 1` and `m sin^2 t < 1` throughout the interval.

operators.name: num_native_sim_elliptic_elliptic_pi_complete
operators.doc: Complete elliptic integral of the third kind `Pi(n, m)` with `n < 1`, `m < 1`.

operators.name: num_native_sim_elliptic_jacobi_int_inv_sq
operators.doc: `int_0^u dv / (1 - n sn^2(v, m))^2` with `u = F(phi, m)`, in closed form (Byrd-Friedman 336.02) through `E`, `F` and `Pi`; requires `n != 1` and `n != m`.

operators.name: num_native_sim_elliptic_jacobi_int_sn2
operators.doc: `int_0^u sn^2(v, m) dv` for the amplitude `phi = am(u)` (any real `phi`): `(u - E(phi, m)) / m` with `u = F(phi, m)`.

operators.name: num_native_spin_heat_bath_direction_n1
operators.doc:
Checked native method over explicitly normalized values. Session/kind, shape and work/allocation bounds are enforced.

Draws a heat-bath direction for an O(N) spin.

The unit vector has density `P(s) ~ exp(beta s . f)` on the sphere `S^(N-1)`: the heat-bath conditional distribution of an O(N) spin in the local field `f`
(von Mises-Fisher distribution; `N = 1` logistic, `N = 2` Best-Fisher, `N = 3` exact inverse
CDF, `N >= 4` Wood's rejection algorithm).

# Errors
Fails for `N = 0`.

operators.name: num_native_spin_on_swendsen_wang_step_d1_n1
operators.doc:
Checked native method over explicitly normalized values. Session/kind, shape and work/allocation bounds are enforced.

One Swendsen-Wang sweep with a random embedding direction; returns the number of clusters.

A non-zero field is included through the ghost spin `sign(h) e_0`: the cluster attached to
the ghost is never flipped.

A ferromagnetic `j2 > 0` joins the bond set and the clusters stay independent. An
antiferromagnetic `j2 < 0` is frustrated, so it stays out of the bond set; its Boltzmann
factor then couples the orientations of *pairs* of clusters and they are no longer
independent, so the sweep becomes a cluster-level Metropolis: every cluster is flipped
atomically, in a fixed order, and accepted with `min(1, exp(-beta dE))`, `dE` being the
change of `2 J2 sum p_i p_j` over the diagonal bonds that cross it, evaluated against the
configuration left by the clusters already flipped in the same sweep (`p_i = s_i . r` is
the projection on the embedding direction, see [`Self::wolff_step`]). Both branches are
exact; for `j2 < 0` only the independence of the clusters — and hence the reading of the
sweep as independent Fortuin-Kasteleyn clusters — is lost.

# Errors
Fails for `J <= 0`.

factor then couples the orientations of *pairs* of clusters and they are no longer

atomically, in a fixed order, and accepted with `min(1, exp(-beta dE))`, `dE` being the
change of `2 J2 sum p_i p_j` over the diagonal bonds that cross it, evaluated against the
configuration left by the clusters already flipped in the same sweep (`p_i = s_i . r` is

exact; for `j2 < 0` only the independence of the clusters — and hence the reading of the
sweep as independent Fortuin-Kasteleyn clusters — is lost.

operators.name: num_native_spin_on_wolff_step_d1_n1
operators.doc:
Checked native method over explicitly normalized values. Session/kind, shape and work/allocation bounds are enforced.

Grows and flips one Wolff cluster; returns its size (`0` when the correction of a
frustrated `J2` boundary rejects the flip).

A non-zero field `h` is handled by the **ghost-spin** construction: the field couples every
site to an extra ghost spin `sign(h) e_0` with strength `|h|`, the cluster may absorb the
ghost, and when it does the cluster's complement is flipped instead (the global symmetry of the
extended system), which keeps detailed balance.

A ferromagnetic `j2 > 0` joins the bond set like `j`. An antiferromagnetic `j2 < 0` is
frustrated with respect to the `j` bonds, so it stays out of the bond set: the cluster
grows on the `j` bonds only and the flip is then accepted with `min(1, exp(-beta dE))`,
where `dE = 2 J2 sum p_i p_j` runs over the diagonal bonds with exactly one endpoint in
the cluster and `p_i = s_i . r` is the projection on the embedding direction. Those
projections, not the scalar products `s_i . s_j`, are what the reflection
`s_i -> s_i - 2 p_i r` changes: it maps `s_i . s_j` to `s_i . s_j - 2 p_i p_j`, so the
perpendicular components drop out (`p_i p_j = s_i s_j` only for `N = 1`). Only the
frustrated bonds need the correction — the Fortuin-Kasteleyn weight of a ferromagnetic
bond is the same before and after a cluster flip, while the Boltzmann factor of a
frustrated bond is not. The proposal is symmetric (the bond construction uses only bonds
inside the cluster, whose products the flip leaves unchanged), so the correction keeps
detailed balance.

# Errors
Fails for `J <= 0`.

site to an extra ghost spin `sign(h) e_0` with strength `|h|`, the cluster may absorb the
ghost, and when it does the cluster's complement is flipped instead (the global symmetry of the
extended system), which keeps detailed balance.

A ferromagnetic `j2 > 0` joins the bond set like `j`. An antiferromagnetic `j2 < 0` is
frustrated with respect to the `j` bonds, so it stays out of the bond set: the cluster
grows on the `j` bonds only and the flip is then accepted with `min(1, exp(-beta dE))`,
where `dE = 2 J2 sum p_i p_j` runs over the diagonal bonds with exactly one endpoint in
the cluster and `p_i = s_i . r` is the projection on the embedding direction. Those
projections, not the scalar products `s_i . s_j`, are what the reflection
`s_i -> s_i - 2 p_i r` changes: it maps `s_i . s_j` to `s_i . s_j - 2 p_i p_j`, so the
perpendicular components drop out (`p_i p_j = s_i s_j` only for `N = 1`). Only the
frustrated bonds need the correction — the Fortuin-Kasteleyn weight of a ferromagnetic
bond is the same before and after a cluster flip, while the Boltzmann factor of a
frustrated bond is not. The proposal is symmetric (the bond construction uses only bonds
inside the cluster, whose products the flip leaves unchanged), so the correction keeps
detailed balance.

# Errors
Fails for `J <= 0`.

Return the dimensionless heat-bath conditional probabilities in Potts color order for one zero-based site. Read the current neighborhood without changing spins or the seed stream.

weights and include the infinite-coupling limits. The model and RNG
are read-only.

Returns an error for an invalid site, output length, local spin label
or undefined effective coupling.

operators.name: num_native_spin_replica_exchange_wang_landau_d1_n1
signatures: (rssn/native/sim/particle-frame/v1, Tensor<[1], Int>, Bool, Dyn<term>, Int) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Checked native method over explicitly normalized values. Session/kind, shape and work/allocation bounds are enforced.

Replica-exchange Wang-Landau with several walkers per energy window.

After Vogel, Li, Wuest and Landau (2013): the energy range is split into overlapping windows, each window runs its own
Wang-Landau iteration with `walkers` walkers sharing `ln g`, neighbouring windows exchange
configurations with probability `min(1, g_i(E_a) g_j(E_b) / (g_i(E_b) g_j(E_a)))`, and the
per-window densities of states are joined at the overlap bin where their logarithmic
derivatives agree best. Works for the Ising model (`N = 1`) and continuous O(N) spins.

Returns `(bin centre, ln g)` for the visited bins, normalised to `sum g = 1`.

# Errors
Fails for invalid options, lattice errors, or if a walker cannot be placed in its window.

configurations with probability `min(1, g_i(E_a) g_j(E_b) / (g_i(E_b) g_j(E_a)))`, and the
per-window densities of states are joined at the overlap bin where their logarithmic
derivatives agree best. Works for the Ising model (`N = 1`) and continuous O(N) spins.

Returns `(bin centre, ln g)` for the visited bins, normalised to `sum g = 1`.

# Errors
Fails for invalid options, lattice errors, or if a walker cannot be placed in its window.

operators.name: num_native_spin_wang_landau_ising_d1
signatures: (rssn/native/sim/particle-frame/v1, Tensor<[1], Int>, Bool, Float, Float, Int, Int) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Checked native method over explicitly normalized values. Session/kind, shape and work/allocation bounds are enforced.

Wang-Landau estimate of the Ising density of states, normalised to `sum g = 2^N`.

The move set is single spin flips; the flatness criterion is `min H > flatness * mean H`
over the energies visited so far; `ln f` starts at 1 and is halved until `ln_f_final`.
Nearest-neighbour only (`J2 = 0`); the energy levels are those of [`Lattice::bonds`].

# Errors
Propagates lattice errors.

operators.name: num_native_spin_wang_landau_on_d1_n1
signatures: (rssn/native/sim/particle-frame/v1, Tensor<[1], Int>, Bool, Dyn<term>, Int, Float, Float, Float, Int, Int) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Checked native method over explicitly normalized values. Session/kind, shape and work/allocation bounds are enforced.

Wang-Landau density of states of an O(N) model with **continuous** spins on a binned
energy axis `[e_min, e_max)` with `nbins` bins (moves leaving the window are rejected).

Single-spin moves of width `delta`; `ln f` starts at 1 and is halved whenever the histogram
of visited bins satisfies `min H > flatness * mean H` (checked every `check` attempted
moves) until `ln_f_final`. Returns `(bin centre, ln g)` for the visited bins, normalised
to `sum g = 1`. The model is the nearest-neighbour one (`J2 = 0`); the signature carries no
coupling, so a next-nearest-neighbour run has to use [`ParallelTempering`].

operators.name: num_native_sqp_scaled
signatures: (Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Float[_], Float[_], Float[_], Float[_], Float, Int, Int, (Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> Float[_], (Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> Tensor<1, Float[_]>, (Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> { x: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, value: Float[_], iterations: Int, evaluations: Int, converged: Bool, lambda: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, mu: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, status: String, second_order: String, normalized_violation: None | Some(Float), normalized_kkt_residual: None | Some(Float) }
operators.doc:
Native scaled global/constrained optimization with shared actual host evaluation limit. Nelder: x,xscale,yscale,step,tol,iterations,budget,f. Differential evolution: lo,hi,xscale,yscale,population,generations,budget,seed,f. Annealing: x,xscale,yscale,step,temperature,cooling,iterations,budget,seed,f. Constrained: x,xscale,yscale,equality_scale,inequality_scale,tol,iterations,budget,f,eq,ineq. Constraints independently carry C/H units; SQP returns physical multipliers E/C and E/H, native status and second-order verdict. Second-order: x,lambda,mu,xscale,yscale,eqscale,ineqscale,budget,f,eq,ineq. No global-optimality claim; native iteration/status semantics retained.

Sequential quadratic programming for `min f(x)` subject to
`h(x) = 0` and `g(x) <= 0`.

Each iteration linearises the constraints, solves the quadratic program
of [`qp_active_set`] for a step `d`, and takes a backtracking step on the
`l1` merit function `f + rho (|h|_1 + max(0, g)_1)`. A least-squares
restoration phase is run whenever the iterate is infeasible, so the
constraints are satisfied to `tol` rather than merely penalised. The
multipliers returned in [`ConstrainedResult::lambda`] and
[`ConstrainedResult::mu`] are the ones of the final quadratic program,
i.e. the exact multipliers of the Lagrangian `L = f + lambda . h + mu . g`;
in particular `-mu_i` is the derivative of the optimal value with respect
to relaxing `g_i(x) <= 0` to `g_i(x) <= eps`.

`grad` may be `None`, in which case central differences are used for the
objective; constraint Jacobians are always central differences.

Convergence is declared when the violation is at most `tol` and the KKT
residual is at most `max(tol, 1e-8)`.

operators.name: num_native_sum_indefinite_sum
signatures: ((Float[_]) -> Float[_], Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Evaluates the discrete sum from config.h to x with steps of config.step. Fractional offsets use analytic continuation in normalized coordinates. The sum has the callback's output dimension. An integral interval that exceeds the callback budget is rejected before the callback runs.

Evaluate the indefinite sum with an explicit callback budget.

The exact lattice path takes one callback per step. For a fractional
offset, both Euler–Maclaurin shifts are reserved together and Taylor
fallback may use the remaining budget. If the shifts exceed the budget,
Taylor can use it in full. A finite normalization point itself needs no
calls. The callback receives only finite coordinates.

# Errors

Returns an error for non-finite endpoints, zero or non-finite step, or an
offset outside the exact floating-point lattice range. It also errors if
no strategy fits the budget or can produce a finite sum. A Taylor fallback
that is needed requires at most 64 terms.

operators.name: num_native_sum_numeric_taylor_coefficients
signatures: ((Float[_]) -> Float[_], Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, Int) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Actual Taylor coefficients in the explicitly normalized coordinate u=x/coordinate_reference. Every coefficient retains output units; divide coefficient k by coordinate_reference^k for derivatives in physical coordinates.

Taylor coefficients `c_m` of `f` about `center`.

They satisfy `f(t) ≈ Σ c_m (t -
center)^m` and come from the interpolating polynomial of degree `terms - 1`
through Chebyshev nodes on `[center - radius, center + radius]`. This is
accurate for moderate `terms` (up to about 16), unlike repeated finite
differences, and converges to the Taylor series for analytic `f`.

operators.name: num_native_sum_series
signatures: (Int, Int, Float[_], Float[_], Int, (Float) -> Float[_]) -> { value: Float[_], evaluations: Int }
operators.doc:
Physical native series/sequence convergence. sum_series: start,max_terms,tolerance,value_scale,max_evaluations,term(Float)->E. sequence_limit omits start. Levin: max_terms,value_scale,max_evaluations,term(Int)->E; result includes native error estimate. References/tolerances are positive physical E; callback failures propagate and budgets bound actual host calls.

Sums `term(n)` for `n = start, start + 1, ...` (at most `max_terms` terms)
and stops, before adding it, at the first term whose magnitude is below
`tolerance`.

operators.name: num_native_sum_series_antidiff
operators.doc:
Native antidifference of coefficients in normalized coordinate u=x/coordinate_reference. Coefficients and result share physical output dimension; this is a discrete sum with unit step in u.

Antidifference of the power series `Σ coefficients[m] (t - center)^m`,
normalised to zero at `t = center`. For repeated evaluation or differences
between nearby points, use [`PolynomialAntidifference`].

operators.name: num_native_tape_column_gather
operators.doc:
Prepare a tape that selects one of 1 to 62 measured source columns for each row. Input zero holds dimensionless offsets, truncated toward zero. Offsets select the subsequent source columns starting at zero. The sources and result use the same positive physical reference. An out-of-range offset is a measured evaluation error.

Builds a tape that selects one of `sources` input columns.

Input zero supplies a zero-based offset and the remaining inputs hold
the sources. [`Inst::Gather`] defines the offset and missing-value rules.
Returns `None` if there are no sources or the input count cannot be represented.

operators.name: num_native_tape_enclose
operators.doc:
Native outward interval enclosure; measured bounds and coordinate references are checked. Infinite endpoints retain their sound interval meaning.

Rigorous enclosures of every output over the input boxes `inputs`
(interval arithmetic with outward rounding; calls of operator
semantics without interval rules give the whole line).

operators.name: num_native_tape_eval
operators.doc:
Evaluate native tape using measured heterogeneous coordinates/parameters; returns checked measured Value cells.

Plain evaluation of every output.

operators.name: num_native_tape_eval_columns
operators.doc:
Native column tape evaluation; each coordinate/output column has independent retained physical references.

Evaluates the program at every row of a batch, column-wise.

`columns[i][row]` is input `i` (a missing element reads NaN, like a
missing input of [`Tape::eval`]); `out[k][row]` receives output `k`
for `row < min(out lengths)`. Rows are processed in blocks of
[`COLUMN_BLOCK`]: each instruction runs over a whole block before
the next one, which turns the per-instruction dispatch of the scalar
interpreter into one dispatch per block and lets the arithmetic
vectorise. Large pure batches split independent row chunks across the
active CPU pool while respecting cancellation and producing the exact
same bits as [`Tape::eval`].

operators.name: num_native_tape_function_from_tape
operators.doc:
Wrap a real native tape in the multiple-output executor.

Wraps a lowered program (the host fallback of [`device::DeviceBackend`]).

operators.name: num_native_tape_function_object
operators.doc:
Retain the exact native TapeFunction type, including its physical frame.

Wraps a lowered program (the host fallback of [`device::DeviceBackend`]).

operators.name: num_native_tape_function_tape
operators.doc:
Recover the defining native tape from a retained TapeFunction without serializing internal pointers.

The underlying program.

operators.name: num_native_tape_gradient
operators.doc:
Native forward tape gradient; each returned Value cell has its own output/input unit.

The gradient of output `k` with respect to every input at `inputs`
(forward mode, one pass per input).

This reference path retains its floating-point evaluation order; use [`Self::gradient_reverse`] for
one forward pass and one reverse sweep on large input spaces.

operators.name: num_native_tape_gradient_reverse
operators.doc:
Native reverse tape gradient with heterogeneous coordinate units.

Gradient of output `k`, in one value pass and one reverse sweep.

operators.name: num_native_tape_hash
operators.doc:
Native deterministic structural tape hash.

A structural hash, independent of node ids (for compilation caches).

operators.name: num_native_tape_hessian
operators.doc:
Native hyperdual tape Hessian; output(i,j) has units E/(D_i D_j).

The Hessian of output `k` with respect to every input at `inputs`,
row-major (`n` rows of `n` entries), by hyper-dual arithmetic.

Entry `(i, j)` is the `ε₁ε₂` component of a run whose two directions
are seeded by `e_i` and `e_j`. Every entry is computed by its own
pass, so symmetry is a property of the rules rather than of the
assembly. The cost is `n²` forward passes for `n` inputs.

Entries are NaN when the tape reaches an opaque operator
(`Call`, `Extern1`, `Extern2`) or a domain error; see the module
limitations. Large tapes with independent built-in instructions can
evaluate rows concurrently in the active CPU pool.

operators.name: num_native_tape_hessian_vector_product
operators.doc:
Native Hessian-vector product with a measured coordinate displacement direction; result units E/D_i.

`H_k(inputs) direction` without assembling a Hessian.

Forward-over-reverse AD uses one directional value pass and one reverse
sweep of dual adjoints. Cost and storage are linear in tape size for
bounded-arity analytic instructions, independent of input count.
Opaque calls have no second-order rule: affected entries are NaN.
Non-smooth functions use the documented hyper-dual conventions.
An invalid output or direction length returns a vector of NaNs.

operators.name: num_native_tape_int_pow
operators.doc:
Native normalized IEEE scalar operation. NaN/interval-entire sentinels retain their native meaning; no physical quantity units are erased.

`x^n` by square-and-multiply (the same sequence the JIT emits).

operators.name: num_native_tape_lower
signatures: (Tensor<1, String>, Tensor<1, String>, Tensor<1, String>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> rssn/native/backend/tape/v1
operators.doc:
Lower elementary expressions in declared symbol/parameter order. Every coordinate, parameter and output has an explicit positive physical reference; mixed units stay in checked Value cells.

Lowers the concrete terms `roots` to one tape with an output per root,
as functions of `inputs` and `params` (in that order).

# Errors
An unbound symbol, a non-numeric literal or an operator without scalar
semantics.

operators.name: num_native_tape_optimise
operators.doc:
Return the native optimized tape retaining its physical frame.

Constant folding, then dead-code elimination (registers renumbered).

operators.name: num_native_tape_run_float
operators.doc:
Explicit Float specialization of generic native tape execution, preserving physical coordinate/output references.

Evaluates every output over an arbitrary number type.

operators.name: num_native_tape_validate
operators.doc:
Validate native tape register and output invariants.

Validate SSA dependencies, input/parameter indices, calls and outputs.

Every operand must refer to an earlier instruction; each input and
parameter must lie within the declared arity. Call argument ranges
must exist and all outputs must name instructions. Gather offsets are
checked at runtime, since their values are data dependent.

# Errors
Returns [`BackendError::Codegen`] describing the invalid instruction or
output. Native backends call this before generating any memory loads.

operators.name: num_native_tape_vjp
operators.doc:
Native VJP; weights have functional/output units and each answer has functional/input units. Positive functional reference specifies the normalized objective measure.

Vector-Jacobian product `weightsᵀ J`, with respect to inputs.

One value pass and one reverse sweep, with storage linear in tape size.
Parameters are held constant. Repeated outputs and gathered inputs add
their adjoints. Only selected branches receive adjoints; comparison and
gather-index derivatives are zero. Opaque calls use the same central
differences as forward-mode AD. A wrong weight count, invalid selected
output, or NaN active output returns a vector of NaNs.

operators.name: num_native_uniform_dist_cdf
operators.doc:
Checked native method over explicitly normalized values. Session/kind, shape and work/allocation bounds are enforced.

Returns the cumulative distribution function (CDF) value at `x`.

operators.name: num_native_uniform_dist_inverse_cdf
operators.doc:
Checked native method over explicitly normalized values. Session/kind, shape and work/allocation bounds are enforced.

Returns the quantile (inverse CDF) at probability `p`.

Returns `NaN` when `p` is outside `[0, 1]`.

operators.name: num_native_uniform_dist_new
operators.doc:
Checked native legacy distribution. Continuous parameters and queries retain coherent physical units; inverse CDF restores sample units and PDF has inverse sample units.

Creates a new `UniformDist` instance.

# Arguments
* `min` - The minimum value of the distribution.
* `max` - The maximum value of the distribution.

# Returns
A `Result` containing the `UniformDist` instance, or an error string if parameters are invalid.

# Errors
Returns an error if `min >= max`.

operators.name: num_native_uniform_dist_pdf
operators.doc:
Checked native method over explicitly normalized values. Session/kind, shape and work/allocation bounds are enforced.

Returns the probability density function (PDF) value at `x`.

operators.name: num_native_usage
operators.doc: Session-local reverse AD object. Tape constructor reserves 1..65536 nodes. Linear quantity values use coherent units; addition requires matching dimensions, products/quotients and gradients propagate physical powers; transcendental arguments must be dimensionless. Opaque handles are kind checked, invalid across sessions and after release. Release dependent variables/gradients before their tape. Callbacks scope temporary handles. No native pointer/state is serialized.

operators.name: num_nonlinear_cg
signatures: (Tensor<1, Float>, Float, Int, Int, (Tensor<1, Float>) -> Float, (Tensor<1, Float>) -> Tensor<1, Float>) -> { x: Tensor<1, Float>, value: Float, iterations: Int, evaluations: Int, converged: Bool }
operators.doc:
Dimensionless serial optimization: initial vector,[lower bounds,upper bounds for lbfgs_b],positive tolerance,max_iterations,max_evaluations,objective callback,gradient callback. Both callbacks share a strict evaluation budget. Gradient length matches initial vector; L-BFGS methods retain ten correction pairs. Returns x,value,iterations,evaluations,converged; callback failures propagate unchanged.

Nonlinear Conjugate Gradient (Polak-Ribiere+ with automatic steepest-descent
restarts) for smooth unconstrained minimization.

operators.name: num_nonlinear_cg_scaled
signatures: (Tensor<1, Float[_]>, { coordinate_scale: Float[_], value_scale: Float[_], tolerance: Float, max_iterations: Int, max_evaluations: Int }, (Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> Float[_], (Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> { x: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, iterations: Int, evaluations: Int, converged: Bool, value: Float[_] }
operators.doc:
Measured nonlinear problem with explicit coordinate_scale and value_scale, dimensionless tolerance, max_iterations and max_evaluations controls. Solves in normalized coordinates/residuals. Arguments: initial, controls, optional lower/upper, objective/residual, optional gradient. Gradient units are objective/coordinate. Homogeneous coordinate and residual vectors; callback failures propagate and budgets are shared.

Nonlinear Conjugate Gradient (Polak-Ribiere+ with automatic steepest-descent
restarts) for smooth unconstrained minimization.

operators.name: num_norm
operators.doc:
Euclidean vector norm.

Computes the Euclidean norm ($`L_2`$ norm) of a vector.

Formula: $||\mathbf{v}||_2 = \sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n `v_i^2`}$

operators.name: num_normalize
operators.doc:
Normalize a nonzero vector.

Normalizes a vector to have a magnitude of 1.

# Errors
Returns an error if the vector is a zero vector.

operators.name: num_npy_decode
signatures: (String) -> { shape: Tensor<1, Int>, data: Tensor<1, Float> }
operators.doc: Decode hexadecimal NumPy float32 or float64 bytes into shape and row-major Float storage. Accepts either byte order and C/Fortran layouts, up to 262144 values.

operators.name: num_npy_encode
operators.doc: Encode shape and dimensionless row-major Float storage as little-endian NumPy float64 bytes represented in lowercase hexadecimal. Accepts scalars and empty arrays, up to 262144 values.

operators.name: num_ns_cell_index
operators.doc:
Native staggered flow in explicit Length/Time/Mass/Temperature references. Fields and coordinates are normalized in that frame; physical outputs retain their dimensions. Work, indices, callback domains, session and parent lifetime are checked.

Cell-centred pressure at flat cell index.

operators.name: num_ns_cell_size
operators.doc:
Native staggered flow in explicit Length/Time/Mass/Temperature references. Fields and coordinates are normalized in that frame; physical outputs retain their dimensions. Work, indices, callback domains, session and parent lifetime are checked.

Cell size.

operators.name: num_ns_config_new
signatures: (rssn/native/mechanical-references/v1, rssn/native/fluid-face-bcs/v1, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Float>, Float, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int) -> rssn/native/ns-config/v1
operators.doc:
Native staggered flow in explicit Length/Time/Mass/Temperature references. Fields and coordinates are normalized in that frame; physical outputs retain their dimensions. Work, indices, callback domains, session and parent lifetime are checked.

Creates a configuration with all walls no-slip.

# Errors
For bad dimensions or sizes.

operators.name: num_ns_data
operators.doc: Native staggered flow in explicit Length/Time/Mass/Temperature references. Fields and coordinates are normalized in that frame; physical outputs retain their dimensions. Work, indices, callback domains, session and parent lifetime are checked.

operators.name: num_ns_density
operators.doc:
Native staggered flow in explicit Length/Time/Mass/Temperature references. Fields and coordinates are normalized in that frame; physical outputs retain their dimensions. Work, indices, callback domains, session and parent lifetime are checked.

Cell-centred density (`None` for the uniform density of one).

operators.name: num_ns_divergence
operators.doc:
Native staggered flow in explicit Length/Time/Mass/Temperature references. Fields and coordinates are normalized in that frame; physical outputs retain their dimensions. Work, indices, callback domains, session and parent lifetime are checked.

Returns the net face flux per full cell volume at every cell, x fastest.

The face flux uses the aperture of each face in an immersed-body grid.
A cut cell's divergence per unit of fluid volume is obtained by
dividing its flux residual by the fluid volume fraction.

operators.name: num_ns_divergence_summary
signatures: (rssn/native/navier-stokes/v1) -> { max_abs: Float[1/Time], rms: Float[1/Time], net_outflow: Dyn<term>, fluid_volume: Dyn<term> }
operators.doc:
Reports maximum absolute divergence and a fluid-volume-weighted RMS, both in inverse time. Net outward flux has length^rank/time units, and fluid volume has length^rank units for a 2D or 3D grid. Cut-cell norms use actual fluid fractions. Fully solid domains return zero diagnostics.

Measures fluid volume, net flux and norms of the cellwise divergence.

Uses active pressure cells with positive fluid volume. With immersed
geometry, the norms divide each aperture-weighted residual by that
cell's fluid fraction. The net flux integrates the represented open
grid faces. An all-solid grid returns zeros.

# Errors

The velocity buffers or cell spacings are invalid, or the
fluid-cell divergence or integrated diagnostics are unrepresentable.

operators.name: num_ns_eddy_viscosity
operators.doc:
Native staggered flow in explicit Length/Time/Mass/Temperature references. Fields and coordinates are normalized in that frame; physical outputs retain their dimensions. Work, indices, callback domains, session and parent lifetime are checked.

Eddy viscosity `ν_t` of the sub-grid-scale model at every cell centre.

operators.name: num_ns_face_aperture
operators.doc:
Native staggered flow in explicit Length/Time/Mass/Temperature references. Fields and coordinates are normalized in that frame; physical outputs retain their dimensions. Work, indices, callback domains, session and parent lifetime are checked.

Open fraction of the cell face normal to axis `axis` with face index `i`.

operators.name: num_ns_flux_through
operators.doc:
Native staggered flow in explicit Length/Time/Mass/Temperature references. Fields and coordinates are normalized in that frame; physical outputs retain their dimensions. Work, indices, callback domains, session and parent lifetime are checked.

Volumetric flux through the plane `x_axis = index` (face index).

operators.name: num_ns_force_on_region
operators.doc:
Native staggered flow in explicit Length/Time/Mass/Temperature references. Fields and coordinates are normalized in that frame; physical outputs retain their dimensions. Work, indices, callback domains, session and parent lifetime are checked.

Force exerted by the fluid on whatever lies inside the box `[lo, hi]`,
from the steady momentum balance on its surface:
`F = -∮ [u (u·n) + p n - ν ∂_n u] dS` (densities are one).

The box must lie in the fluid and the flow must be steady for the
result to be the drag of the enclosed body. In 2D the force is per unit
length.

operators.name: num_ns_kinetic_energy
operators.doc:
Native integral of speed squared divided by two, without density weighting; output has dimensions Length^(dimension+2)/Time^2. For 2D this is the native integral per omitted depth.

Kinetic energy `½ ∫ |u|²` using face values.

operators.name: num_ns_mass
operators.doc:
Native staggered flow in explicit Length/Time/Mass/Temperature references. Fields and coordinates are normalized in that frame; physical outputs retain their dimensions. Work, indices, callback domains, session and parent lifetime are checked.

Total mass `∫ ρ dV` over the domain (the volume when `ρ ≡ 1`).

operators.name: num_ns_max_speed
operators.doc:
Native staggered flow in explicit Length/Time/Mass/Temperature references. Fields and coordinates are normalized in that frame; physical outputs retain their dimensions. Work, indices, callback domains, session and parent lifetime are checked.

Maximum speed over the faces (for CFL estimates).

operators.name: num_ns_n
operators.doc:
Native staggered flow in explicit Length/Time/Mass/Temperature references. Fields and coordinates are normalized in that frame; physical outputs retain their dimensions. Work, indices, callback domains, session and parent lifetime are checked.

Cells per axis.

operators.name: num_ns_new
operators.doc:
Consumes one native NS configuration and constructs its actual staggered solver. Initial velocity is three compiled physical spatial programs. All callbacks retain parent handles; callback budgets and original failures are preserved.

Creates a solver with the given initial velocity (faces) and time step.

# Errors
For inconsistent periodic faces or singular systems.

operators.name: num_ns_run
operators.doc:
Native staggered flow in explicit Length/Time/Mass/Temperature references. Fields and coordinates are normalized in that frame; physical outputs retain their dimensions. Work, indices, callback domains, session and parent lifetime are checked.

Runs `steps` steps.

# Errors
See [`NsSolver::step`].

operators.name: num_ns_sample_pressure
operators.doc:
Native staggered flow in explicit Length/Time/Mass/Temperature references. Fields and coordinates are normalized in that frame; physical outputs retain their dimensions. Work, indices, callback domains, session and parent lifetime are checked.

Multilinear interpolation of the cell-centred pressure at `x`.

operators.name: num_ns_sample_velocity
operators.doc:
Native staggered flow in explicit Length/Time/Mass/Temperature references. Fields and coordinates are normalized in that frame; physical outputs retain their dimensions. Work, indices, callback domains, session and parent lifetime are checked.

Multilinear interpolation of velocity component `c` at `x`.

operators.name: num_ns_set_density
operators.doc:
Native staggered flow in explicit Length/Time/Mass/Temperature references. Fields and coordinates are normalized in that frame; physical outputs retain their dimensions. Work, indices, callback domains, session and parent lifetime are checked.

Overwrites the density field and rebuilds the projection operator.

The two updates take effect together after the new operator is valid.

# Errors
Without a density field, for a wrong length, for a non-positive or
non-finite value, or when the new pressure operator cannot be prepared.

operators.name: num_ns_set_temperature
operators.doc:
Native staggered flow in explicit Length/Time/Mass/Temperature references. Fields and coordinates are normalized in that frame; physical outputs retain their dimensions. Work, indices, callback domains, session and parent lifetime are checked.

Overwrites the temperature field.

# Errors
Without a thermal model or for a wrong length.

operators.name: num_ns_step
operators.doc:
Native staggered flow in explicit Length/Time/Mass/Temperature references. Fields and coordinates are normalized in that frame; physical outputs retain their dimensions. Work, indices, callback domains, session and parent lifetime are checked.

Advances one time step.

# Errors
If a linear solve fails.

operators.name: num_ns_steps
operators.doc:
Native staggered flow in explicit Length/Time/Mass/Temperature references. Fields and coordinates are normalized in that frame; physical outputs retain their dimensions. Work, indices, callback domains, session and parent lifetime are checked.

Number of steps taken.

operators.name: num_ns_temperature
operators.doc:
Native staggered flow in explicit Length/Time/Mass/Temperature references. Fields and coordinates are normalized in that frame; physical outputs retain their dimensions. Work, indices, callback domains, session and parent lifetime are checked.

Cell-centred temperature (`None` without a thermal model).

operators.name: num_ns_volume_fraction
operators.doc:
Native staggered flow in explicit Length/Time/Mass/Temperature references. Fields and coordinates are normalized in that frame; physical outputs retain their dimensions. Work, indices, callback domains, session and parent lifetime are checked.

Fluid volume fraction of pressure cell `i` (1 without an immersed body).

operators.name: num_number_exact_bigint_crt_garner
operators.doc: Solves `x ≡ remainders[i] (mod primes[i])` via Garner's mixed-radix algorithm, returning the unique canonical solution `x` in `[0, prod(primes))`.

operators.name: num_number_exact_bigint_gcd
operators.doc: Nonnegative greatest common divisor of two arbitrary-precision integers.

operators.name: num_number_exact_bigint_isqrt
operators.doc: Floor integer square root `floor(sqrt(n))` for nonnegative `n`, or `None` for `n < 0`.

operators.name: num_number_exact_bigint_mod_inverse
operators.doc:
Modular multiplicative inverse of `a` modulo `modulus` in `[0, modulus)`.

Returns `None` if `modulus <= 0` or `gcd(a, modulus) != 1` (except `modulus == 1`,
which returns `Some(0)`).

operators.name: num_number_exact_bigint_nth_root
operators.doc: Truncated integer `k`-th root of `n` (`Some(r)` with `r^k` closest to `n` toward zero without exceeding `|n|` in magnitude).

operators.name: num_number_exact_bigint_xgcd
signatures: (Int, Int) -> { item0: Int, item1: Int, item2: Int }
operators.doc: Extended greatest common divisor `(g, x, y)` of arbitrary-precision integers such that `g = gcd(a, b) >= 0` and `a * x + b * y == g`.

operators.name: num_number_exact_jacobi_bigint
operators.doc:
The Jacobi symbol `(a / n)` for odd positive arbitrary-precision `n`.

Returns `None` if `n <= 0` or `n` is even.

operators.name: num_number_exact_strong_lucas_bigint
operators.doc:
Applies the strong Lucas probable-prime test with Selfridge’s parameters.

Strong Lucas probable-prime test of an odd integer `n > 2` with Selfridge's
parameters (`D` the first of `5, -7, 9, -11, ...` with Jacobi symbol `-1`,
`P = 1`, `Q = (1 - D) / 4`): checks `U_d = 0` or `V_{d 2^r} = 0` for some
`r < s`, where `n + 1 = d 2^s` with `d` odd.

operators.name: num_number_ext_batch_mod_pow
signatures: (Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Int>
operators.doc:
Batched modular exponentiation computing `bases[i]^exponents[i] mod modulus` in `[0, modulus)`.

Uses division-free Montgomery multiplication (`MontU64`) when `modulus` is odd
and parallelizes across large batches via [`par::map_indexed`].

# Errors
Returns [`NumberExtError::ShapeMismatch`] if `bases` and `exponents` differ in
length, or [`NumberExtError::Domain`] if `modulus <= 0`.

operators.name: num_number_ext_catalan_exact
operators.doc: Exact `n`-th Catalan number `C_n = C(2n, n) / (n + 1)`. Returns zero for negative arguments.

operators.name: num_number_ext_crt
signatures: (Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>) -> { item0: Int, item1: Int }
operators.doc:
Chinese Remainder Theorem: solves `x ≡ remainders[i] (mod moduli[i])`.

Returns `(first, period)` with `0 <= first < period`. The period is the
least common multiple of the moduli. Non-coprime moduli are supported.

# Errors
The inputs must be nonempty, of the same length, and have positive moduli
and consistent congruences. The period must fit in `i64`.

operators.name: num_number_ext_crt_bigint
signatures: (Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>) -> { item0: Int, item1: Int }
operators.doc:
Arbitrary-precision Chinese Remainder Theorem solving `x ≡ remainders[i] (mod moduli[i])`.

Returns `(first, period)` with `0 <= first < period`, where `period` is the
least common multiple of `moduli`. Non-coprime moduli are supported.

# Errors
Returns [`NumberExtError::ShapeMismatch`] if slice lengths differ,
[`NumberExtError::Empty`] if the slices are empty, or [`NumberExtError::Domain`]
if any modulus is nonpositive or the congruences are inconsistent.

operators.name: num_number_ext_mobius
operators.doc: Möbius function `μ(n)`, extended to return zero for `n <= 0`.

operators.name: num_number_ext_mobius_sieve
operators.doc:
Computes `μ(0)` through `μ(limit)` with a linear sieve.

The value at index zero is zero. Each composite is visited once using
its smallest prime factor, so consecutive values need no separate
factorizations. The sieve uses `O(limit)` time and storage.

# Errors
The inclusive length must fit the address space and its storage must be
allocatable.

operators.name: num_number_ext_mod_inv
operators.doc:
Modular multiplicative inverse in `[0, modulus)`.

# Errors
The modulus must be positive and relatively prime to `a`.

operators.name: num_number_ext_mod_pow
operators.doc:
Modular exponentiation: `base^exponent mod modulus`, in `[0, modulus)`.

# Errors
The modulus must be positive.

operators.name: num_number_ext_partition_count
operators.doc:
Integer partition function `p(n)` via Euler's pentagonal number theorem.

Negative arguments produce zero. The recurrence retains values through `n`.

# Panics
Panics when the table does not fit the host's address space.

operators.name: num_number_ext_solve_linear_congruence
signatures: (Int, Int, Int) -> None | Some({ item0: Int, item1: Int })
operators.doc:
Solves `a * x ≡ b (mod modulus)` over the integers.

A solution `(first, period)` represents exactly the integers
`first + k * period` for any integer `k`, with `0 <= first < period`.
The period is `modulus / gcd(a, modulus)`. Returns `None` when the
congruence has no solution. Modulus one admits all integers.
For example, `6 * x ≡ 8 (mod 14)` gives `(6, 7)`.

# Errors
The modulus must be nonzero.

operators.name: num_number_ext_stirling_first
operators.doc:
Unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind `c(n, k)`.

Returns zero when `n < 0` or `k` lies outside `0..=n`.

# Panics
Panics when the recurrence's workspace length cannot fit the address space.

operators.name: num_number_ext_stirling_first_signed
operators.doc:
Signed Stirling numbers of the first kind `s(n, k) = (-1)^(n - k) c(n, k)`.

Uses the same domain and workspace as [`stirling_first`].

operators.name: num_number_ext_stirling_second_exact
operators.doc:
Exact Stirling numbers of the second kind `S(n, k)`.

Returns zero when `n < 0` or `k` lies outside `0..=n`.

# Panics
Panics when the recurrence's workspace length cannot fit the address space.

operators.name: num_number_ext_totient_sieve
operators.doc:
Computes Euler's totient `φ(0)` through `φ(limit)` with a linear sieve.

The value at index zero is zero and `φ(1) = 1`. Uses pooled prime scratch
storage from [`global_pool`] and runs in `O(limit)` time.

# Errors
Returns [`NumberExtError::Domain`] when the inclusive length overflows
`usize` or cannot be reserved in memory.

operators.name: num_number_ext_xgcd
signatures: (Int, Int) -> { item0: Int, item1: Int, item2: Int }
operators.doc: Extended greatest common divisor `(g, x, y)` such that `a * x + b * y == g` and `g >= 0`. Wide outputs represent `gcd(i64::MIN, 0)` without overflow.

operators.name: num_number_theory_carmichael_lambda
operators.doc:
Computes Carmichael's reduced totient function $\lambda(n)$ (`carmichael_lambda(0) = 0`).

$\lambda(n)$ is the exponent of the multiplicative group $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^\times$,
i.e. the smallest positive integer $m$ such that $a^m \equiv 1 \pmod n$ for all
$\gcd(a, n) = 1$.

operators.name: num_number_theory_checked_lcm
operators.doc: The least common multiple, or `None` when it overflows `u64`.

operators.name: num_number_theory_discrete_log
operators.doc:
The least `x >= 0` with `g^x ≡ h (mod p)`.

Accepts prime and composite moduli, including bases that share factors with
the modulus. Returns `None` if there is no solution or `p` is outside
`2..=2^48`. After removing common factors, baby-step giant-step takes
`O(sqrt p)` time and memory in the worst case.

operators.name: num_number_theory_divisor_count
operators.doc: Returns the number of positive divisors `\tau(n) = \sigma_0(n)` (`divisor_count(0) = 0`).

operators.name: num_number_theory_divisor_sigma
operators.doc: Returns the sum of the `k`-th powers of the positive divisors of `n`, `\sigma_k(n) = \sum_{d \mid n} d^k`, saturating at `u128::MAX` (`divisor_sigma(0, _) = 0`).

operators.name: num_number_theory_divisors
operators.doc: Returns all positive divisors of `n` in ascending order (`divisors(0)` is empty).

operators.name: num_number_theory_extended_gcd_u64
signatures: (Int, Int) -> { gcd: Int, x: Int, y: Int }
operators.doc:
Given unsigned 64-bit integers a and b, return the exact record {gcd, x, y} satisfying a*x + b*y = gcd(a,b). Coefficients x and y are signed.

The extended Euclidean algorithm on `u64` inputs.

Returns `(g, x, y)` with `g = gcd(a, b)` and `a * x + b * y = g`. The
Bézout coefficients of `u64` inputs stay within `i128`.

operators.name: num_number_theory_factorize
operators.doc:
Returns the prime factors of `n` with multiplicity, in ascending order.

`0` and `1` have no factors. Small primes are removed by trial division;
the cofactor is split with Miller–Rabin and Pollard–Brent rho, so every
`u64` factors in milliseconds.

operators.name: num_number_theory_gcd
operators.doc: Computes the greatest common divisor (GCD) of two numbers using Stein's binary GCD algorithm after one initial Euclidean reduction step.

operators.name: num_number_theory_gcd_u128
operators.doc: Computes the greatest common divisor (GCD) of two 128-bit unsigned integers using Stein's binary GCD algorithm.

operators.name: num_number_theory_is_prime_bpsw
operators.doc: Deterministic Baillie–PSW primality test over `u64` (strong base-2 Miller–Rabin test combined with a strong Lucas probable-prime test using Selfridge's parameters, executed in the Montgomery domain).

operators.name: num_number_theory_is_prime_miller_rabin
operators.doc: Performs a deterministic Miller-Rabin primality test over `u64` using division-free Montgomery multiplication (`MontU64`).

operators.name: num_number_theory_is_prime_u128
operators.doc: Primality test for 128-bit unsigned integers combining deterministic `u64` Miller–Rabin with 13-base strong Miller–Rabin and a strong Selfridge Lucas test (Baillie–PSW) for values above `u64::MAX`.

operators.name: num_number_theory_isqrt
operators.doc: Floor of the square root of `n`, exact for all `u64`.

operators.name: num_number_theory_jacobi_symbol
operators.doc:
Jacobi symbol of a signed 128-bit numerator and a positive odd unsigned 64-bit denominator. Returns -1, 0, or 1.

Computes the Jacobi symbol $\left(\frac{a}{n}\right)$ for an odd positive integer `n`.

Returns `0` when `n == 0`, `n` is even, or $\gcd(a, n) > 1$. For `n == 1`, returns `1`.

operators.name: num_number_theory_lcm
operators.doc:
Computes the least common multiple (LCM) of two numbers.

Returns `0` when either argument is `0`, and `u64::MAX` when the true
value does not fit (use [`checked_lcm`] to tell the two apart).

operators.name: num_number_theory_legendre_symbol
operators.doc:
Legendre symbol of an unsigned 64-bit numerator and an odd prime denominator. Returns zero when the prime divides the numerator.

Computes the Legendre symbol $\left(\frac{a}{p}\right)$ for an odd prime `p`.

Returns `0` if `p < 3`, `p` is composite, or `p` divides `a`; `1` if `a` is
a quadratic residue modulo `p`; and `-1` if `a` is a quadratic non-residue.

operators.name: num_number_theory_mod_inv_u64
operators.doc:
Canonical inverse of an unsigned 64-bit integer modulo m >= 2. Returns a domain error when a and m are not coprime.

`a^(-1) mod modulus`, or `None` when `gcd(a, modulus) != 1` or
`modulus < 2`.

The extended Euclidean algorithm terminates in `O(log modulus)` steps with
small quotients, which is faster than Fermat exponentiation and works for
composite moduli.

operators.name: num_number_theory_mod_inverse
operators.doc:
Finds the modular multiplicative inverse of a number.

Solves for `x` in `ax ≡ 1 (mod m)` using the extended Euclidean
algorithm in `i128`. The modulus may be negative (its absolute value is
used); `m == 0` has no inverse. The result lies in `0..|m|`, and
`|m| == 1` gives `Some(0)`.

# Returns
An `Option<i64>` containing the modular inverse if it exists, otherwise `None`.

operators.name: num_number_theory_mod_pow
operators.doc: Computes `(base^exp) % modulus` efficiently using modular exponentiation (binary exponentiation).

operators.name: num_number_theory_mod_pow_u128
operators.doc:
`num_number_theory_mod_pow_u128(base, exponent, modulus)` raises a u128 base to a u128 exponent modulo a positive u128 integer without overflow.

Computes `(base^exp) % modulus` for 128-bit unsigned integers without overflow.

Returns `0` when `modulus <= 1`.

operators.name: num_number_theory_mul_mod
operators.doc:
`num_number_theory_mul_mod(a, b, modulus)` multiplies two u64 values modulo a positive u64 integer without overflow.

`a * b mod m` without overflow. `m` must be non-zero.

operators.name: num_number_theory_mul_mod_u128
operators.doc:
`num_number_theory_mul_mod_u128(a, b, modulus)` multiplies two u128 values modulo a positive u128 integer without overflow.

Computes `(a * b) % m` for 128-bit unsigned integers without overflow.

Returns `0` when `m <= 1`.

operators.name: num_number_theory_phi
operators.doc:
Computes Euler's totient function φ(n) (`φ(0) = 0`).

Uses [`factorize`], so it is fast for every `u64`.

operators.name: num_number_theory_prime_sqrt_plan_modulus
operators.doc:
Returns the prime modulus retained by the prepared square-root plan.

The prime modulus used by this plan.

operators.name: num_number_theory_prime_sqrt_plan_new
operators.doc:
Checks a 64-bit modulus and prepares its square-root method. Returns None for a modulus other than a prime. Modulus two is supported.

Prepares an odd prime modulus or `2`. Returns `None` for other moduli.

operators.name: num_number_theory_prime_sqrt_plan_sqrt
operators.doc:
Reduces the unsigned input modulo the prepared prime. Returns the smaller square root, or None if the input is a quadratic nonresidue.

Returns the smaller root of `n` modulo the prepared prime.

The argument is reduced modulo the prime. Non-residues give `None`.

operators.name: num_number_theory_primes_sieve
operators.doc:
Generates primes up to `limit` using the Sieve of Eratosthenes.

For `limit <= 1_000_000`, reuses the cached prime table in
[`crate::kernels::reuse::global_pool`]. For larger limits, executes an
odd-only bit-packed L1-cache-resident segmented sieve leasing scratch
storage from [`crate::kernels::reuse::global_pool`].

Returns an empty vector when the sieve table cannot be allocated
(`limit` near `usize::MAX`) instead of aborting.

operators.name: num_number_theory_primitive_root
operators.doc:
Smallest positive primitive root modulo an unsigned 64-bit integer. Returns a domain error if the multiplicative group has no primitive root.

Returns the smallest positive primitive root modulo `n` if the multiplicative
group $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^\times$ is cyclic ($n \in \{2, 4, p^k, 2p^k\}$
for an odd prime $p$), or `None` otherwise.

operators.name: num_number_theory_sqrt_mod_prime
operators.doc:
A square root of `n` modulo the prime `p`, choosing the smaller root.

Accepts `p = 2`. Returns `None` for a composite or invalid modulus or
when `n` is a non-residue. Use [`PrimeSqrtPlan`] for repeated queries
with the same prime modulus.

operators.name: num_ode_bdf
signatures: (Float[_], Float[_], Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Float[_], Float, Float[_], Int, (Float[_], Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> { times: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, states: Tensor<2, Float[_]>, evaluations: Int, rejected: Int }
operators.doc:
Serial adaptive vector IVP: initial time, final time, initial state vector, absolute state tolerance, relative tolerance, positive finite maximal time step, positive attempt budget, RHS callback. RHS(time,state) returns a same-length vector with state/time dimensions. Returns accepted times/states/evaluations/rejected; the rank-two state tensor has one row per accepted time. Coefficients use coherent units. Callback failures propagate unchanged, rejected attempts consume the budget, and numerical error estimates are heuristic. Events, DAEs and dense-output handles use the native Rust API.

Variable-order BDF (orders 1 to 5, NDF coefficients) with a
finite-difference Jacobian; see [`bdf_jac`].

# Errors
[`OdeError::StepLimit`], [`OdeError::NonFinite`], [`OdeError::SolveFailed`]
or [`OdeError::Invalid`].

operators.name: num_ode_dopri5
signatures: (Float[_], Float[_], Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Float[_], Float, Float[_], Int, (Float[_], Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> { times: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, states: Tensor<2, Float[_]>, evaluations: Int, rejected: Int }
operators.doc:

RHS(time,state) returns a same-length vector with state/time dimensions. Returns accepted times/states/evaluations/rejected; the rank-two state tensor has one row per accepted time. Coefficients use coherent units. Callback failures propagate unchanged, rejected attempts consume the budget, and numerical error estimates are heuristic. Events, DAEs and dense-output handles use the native Rust API.

Dormand-Prince 5(4) integration of `y' = f(t, y)` from `t0` to `t1`
(either direction) with dense output and event detection.

`f(t, y, dy)` writes the derivative into `dy`. Events are located by
Brent iteration on the continuous extension; a terminal event ends the
integration at the event time.

# Errors
[`OdeError::StepLimit`] or [`OdeError::NonFinite`].

operators.name: num_ode_gauss4_adaptive
signatures: (Float[_], Float[_], Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Float[_], Float, Float[_], Float[_], Float[_], Int, Int, (Float[_], Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> { times: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, states: Tensor<2, Float[_]>, rates: Tensor<2, Float[_]>, evaluations: Int, rejected: Int }
operators.doc:
Dimension-aware adaptive requested-method integration: t0,t1,y0,atol,rtol,h0,h_min,h_max,max_steps,max_evaluations,rhs. Callback derivative has state/time dimensions. Returns accepted times/states/Hermite rates and actual work counters; no method substitution. Adaptive state-dependent stepping does not preserve fixed-step symplecticity.

Integrate the selected RK4 or geometric method forward using step doubling.
The finite interval uses `start <= end`.

The accepted state is two half steps of the requested method, without
extrapolation or method substitution. Both the endpoint estimate and the
midpoint defect of its cubic Hermite extension control acceptance. A trial
needs a representable time strictly between its endpoints. A bracketed event
between adjacent times is reported at the later timestamp. Adaptive
state-dependent step selection does not retain fixed-step symplecticity.
Gauss–Legendre trials reuse stage storage for the duration of the solve.

# Errors
Invalid inputs or callback outputs, exhausted attempts/evaluations, a
tolerance requiring a smaller step than `h_min`, an unsplittable time grid,
or failed implicit stages.

operators.name: num_par_dot_fixed
signatures: (Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Int, Int) -> Float[_]
operators.doc:
Deterministic dot product of `a` and `b` over their common prefix `a.len().min(b.len())`.

Each fixed block of `block` elements accumulates with a 4-way unrolled sum, and block sums
are folded sequentially in block order so serial execution (`grain = usize::MAX`) and
parallel execution produce bit-identical results.

operators.name: num_par_norm2_fixed
operators.doc:
Deterministic Euclidean (`L2`) norm of `a` using fixed blocks of `block` elements.

Uses [`dot_fixed`] on the ordinary path and falls back to scale-normalized block
accumulation when intermediate squares overflow or underflow, keeping serial
(`grain = usize::MAX`) and parallel results bit-identical.

operators.name: num_par_prefix_sum_f64_fixed
operators.doc:
Deterministic inclusive prefix sum of `data` using a two-pass fixed-block scan.

Pass 1 scans each contiguous block of `block` elements independently; a sequential scan
computes exclusive block offsets left-to-right; pass 2 adds each block's offset to its
elements. Serial (`grain = usize::MAX`) and parallel executions produce bit-identical
outputs.

operators.name: num_pde_advection_adaptive
signatures: (Tensor<1, Int>, Float[_], Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, { kind: Tensor<1, Int>, value: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, flux: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, alpha: Tensor<1, Float>, beta: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, gamma: Tensor<1, Float[_]> }, { t0: Float[_], t1: Float[_], rtol: Float, atol: Float[_], h0: Float[_], h_min: Float[_], h_max: Float[_], max_steps: Int, max_rejections: Int, max_step_calls: Int, max_evaluations: Int }) -> { times: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, states: Tensor<2, Float[_]>, velocities: Tensor<2, Float[_]>, coordinates: Tensor<2, Float[_]>, accepted: Int, rejected: Int, step_calls: Int, evaluations: Int, error_ratio: Float, event_time: None | Some(Float[_]) }
operators.doc:
Tolerance-controlled PDE evolution with explicit coordinate L, time T, and field U dimensions. Diffusivity is L^2/T; velocity L/T; reaction 1/T; Neumann U/L; Robin alpha dimensionless, beta L, gamma U. Grid/state lengths and boundary pairing/corner data are checked. Controls: t0,t1,rtol,atol,h0,h_min,h_max,max_steps,max_rejections,max_step_calls,max_evaluations. Boundary record: kind,value,flux,alpha,beta,gamma vectors (one broadcast face or two per active axis). Only accepted states are returned; step doubling controls temporal error, independently of spatial error. Optional trailing direction and dimensionless terminal-event callback; wave events receive displacement and velocity separately. FEM uses a fixed simplex mesh; source variants take a vectorized (time,coordinates)->nodal-rate callback with a consistent mass load. FVM preserves periodic/transmissive flux methods; classic LF's timestep-dependent viscosity may prevent strict temporal convergence. DG uses periodic SSPRK3 in one or two dimensions; Fourier uses ETDRK4 and a dimensioned nonlinear rate callback. Budgets and callback failures are explicit errors.

Adaptive first-order upwind advection with a multidimensional CFL bound.

# Errors
Invalid grid, face data, velocities, controls, or exhausted temporal budgets.

Tolerance-controlled PDE evolution with explicit coordinate L, time T, and field U dimensions.
