signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, Int, Int) -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: `ode_borel(eq, y(x), x0, n, x1, k)` uses Borel–Padé resummation to evaluate formal solution `k` of `eq` at `x1` with `n` terms around singular point `x0`. Returns the real part, imaginary part, error estimate and Stokes indicator. `k` starts at zero.
examples: ode_borel(diff(diff(y(x), x), x) - x*y(x), y(x), oo, 90, 5, 0)

operators.name: ode_classify
operators.doc: `ode_classify(ode, y)`: classifies an ordinary differential equation `ode` for dependent function `y`, returning a list of applicable solver classes.

operators.name: ode_darboux
signatures: (Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Int) -> Tensor<2, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: `ode_darboux(dx, dy, x, y, [max_deg])`: finds Darboux polynomials and cofactors `[P, k]` for planar autonomous system `x' = dx, y' = dy`.

operators.name: ode_etdrk4
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
(Tensor<2, Int>, Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Tensor<1, Symbol>, Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int, Int, Int) -> Tensor<1, Float>
operators.doc: `ode_etdrk4(L, f, vars, t, u0, t0, t1, steps)`: `u(t1)` for `u' = L u + f(t, u)` by fourth-order exponential time differencing.
examples: ode_etdrk4(list(list(0, 1), list(-1, 0)), list(-0.5*u1, -0.5*u2), list(u1, u2), t, list(1, 0), 0, 1, 50)

operators.name: ode_fourier
operators.doc: `ode_fourier(ode, y)`: solves linear constant-coefficient `ode` for `y` using Fourier transform.

operators.name: ode_frobenius
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, Int) -> { _0: Dyn<term>, _1: Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, _2: Dyn<term> }
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int) -> { _0: Dyn<term>, _1: Tensor<2, Dyn<term>>, _2: Dyn<term> }
operators.doc: `ode_frobenius(eq, y(x), x0, n)` expands a homogeneous linear second-order equation about rational `x0` or `oo`, with order `n` up to 60. Returns the solution, indicial roots or formal exponent pairs, and a recurrence equation when available. The recurrence entry is an empty list otherwise.
examples: ode_frobenius(x^4*diff(diff(y(x), x), x) + 2*x^3*diff(y(x), x) - y(x), y(x), 0, 5)
ode_frobenius(diff(diff(y(x), x), x) - x*y(x), y(x), oo, 24)
ode_frobenius(x^2*diff(diff(y(x), x), x) - (x^2 + 1/4)*y(x) + x*diff(y(x), x), y(x), oo, 4)

operators.name: ode_imex
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, Int, Int, Int, Dyn<term>) -> Tensor<1, Float>
operators.doc: `ode_imex(f_ex, f_im, vars, t, y0, t0, t1, steps, scheme)`: `y(t1)` for `y' = f_ex + f_im` with explicit `f_ex` and stiff implicit `f_im` using `euler`, `ars222`, or `ars343`.

operators.name: ode_jacobi_last_multiplier
operators.doc: `ode_jacobi_last_multiplier(dx, dy, x, y, [max_deg])`: computes a Jacobi last multiplier (integrating factor) for planar system `x' = dx, y' = dy`.

operators.name: ode_series
operators.doc: `ode_series(ode, y, x0, order)`: computes a power-series solution `y(x) = ...` of `ode` about `x0` up to `order`.

operators.name: ode_solve
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, Int, Int, Float, Dyn<term>) -> Tensor<1, Float>
(Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Tensor<1, Symbol>, Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int, Float, Float, Dyn<term>) -> Tensor<1, Float>
operators.doc: `ode_solve(rhs, vars, t, y0, t0, t1, tol, method)`: `y(t1)` for `y' = rhs(t, y)` with `y(t0) = y0` using `dopri5`, `rosenbrock23`, `radau5`, `bdf`, `sdirk3`, or `exprb32`.
examples: ode_solve(list(y2, -y1), list(y1, y2), t, list(1, 0), 0, 1.5, 0.0000000001, dopri5)

operators.name: ode_symmetries
operators.doc: `ode_symmetries(ode, y)`: finds Lie point symmetry generators `[xi, eta]` admitted by `ode` for dependent function `y`.

operators.name: ode_symplectic
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int, Float, Int, Dyn<term>) -> Tensor<2, Float>
(Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Tensor<1, Symbol>, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int, Int, Int, Dyn<term>) -> Tensor<2, Float>
operators.doc: `ode_symplectic(accel, vars, q0, p0, t0, t1, steps, method)`: `list(q, p)` at `t1` for `q' = p`, `p' = accel(q)` using `verlet`, `yoshida4`, `yoshida6`, or `yoshida8`.
examples: ode_symplectic(list(-q1, -4*q2), list(q1, q2), list(1, 0), list(0, 1), 0, 1, 400, yoshida6)

operators.name: odeint
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc: `odeint(f, y, x, x0, y0, x1)`: numerically integrates `dy/dx = f(x, y)` from `(x0, y0)` to `x1`.

operators.name: omega
operators.doc: `omega(n)`: number of distinct prime factors of `n`.

operators.name: one_parameter_subgroup
operators.doc: `one_parameter_subgroup(A, t)`: one-parameter subgroup `exp_map(t * A)` generated by matrix `A`.

operators.name: oo
operators.doc: `oo`: positive real infinity (`+infinity`).

operators.name: op_add
operators.doc: `op_add(A, B, ...)`: sum `A + B + ...` of linear operators.

operators.name: op_apply
operators.doc: `op_apply(A, f)`: apply linear operator `A` to function or vector `f`.

operators.name: op_commutator
operators.doc: `op_commutator(A, B)`: commutator `[A, B] = A B - B A` of operators `A` and `B`.

operators.name: op_compose
operators.doc: `op_compose(A, B, ...)`: composition `A o B o ...` of linear operators (rightmost acts first).

operators.name: op_d
operators.doc: `op_d(x)`: differential operator `f -> d/dx(f)`.

operators.name: op_identity
operators.doc: `op_identity()`: identity linear operator `f -> f`.

operators.name: op_int
operators.doc: `op_int(a, x)`: Volterra integration operator `f -> int_a^x f(t) dt`.

operators.name: op_laplacian
operators.doc: `op_laplacian(vars)`: Laplacian differential operator `sum_i d^2 / dx_i^2` over `vars`.

operators.name: op_mul
operators.doc: `op_mul(g)`: linear multiplication operator `f -> g * f`.

operators.name: op_power
operators.doc: `op_power(A, n)`: `n`-fold composition `A^n` of linear operator `A`.

operators.name: op_scale
operators.doc: `op_scale(c, A)`: linear operator `A` scaled by `c`.

operators.name: operator_adjoint
operators.doc: `operator_adjoint(A)`: formal `L^2` adjoint `A*` of differential/multiplication operator `A`.

operators.name: or
operators.doc: `or(p1, p2, ...)`: variadic logical disjunction, true when at least one operand is true.

operators.name: orbit_density
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
Computes an `nx` by `ny` 2D occupancy histogram of `points` over `[xmin, xmax] × [ymin, ymax]`.

Computes the density distribution of orbit points in a 2D histogram.

# Arguments
* `points` - The orbit trajectory.
* `x_bins` - Number of bins in x direction.
* `y_bins` - Number of bins in y direction.
* `x_range` - Range for x axis.
* `y_range` - Range for y axis.

# Returns
A 2D vector of counts for each bin.

operators.name: orbit_entropy
operators.doc:
Computes the Shannon entropy of a 2D occupancy histogram `density`.

Computes the entropy of an orbit from its density distribution.

Uses Shannon entropy: H = -`sum(p_i` * `log(p_i)`)

# Arguments
* `density` - A 2D density histogram from `orbit_density`.

# Returns
The Shannon entropy of the distribution.

operators.name: orbit_iterate
operators.doc: `orbit_iterate(f, z, z0, n)`: symbolic `n`-fold iterate `f^{o n}(z0)`.

operators.name: orthogonal_coefficients
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Dyn<term>, Int, Int) -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: `orthogonal_coefficients(f, basis, x, a, b)`: Fourier coefficients `<e_i, f> / <e_i, e_i>` of `f` in orthogonal `basis`.

operators.name: orthogonalize
operators.doc: `orthogonalize(vecs)`: Gram-Schmidt orthogonal basis from a list of vectors.

operators.name: orthographic
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
(Int, Int, Int, Int, Int, Int) -> Tensor<2, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: Constructs a 4x4 OpenGL-style orthographic projection matrix from `(left, right, bottom, top, near, far)`.

operators.name: orthonormalize
operators.doc: `orthonormalize(vecs)`: Gram-Schmidt orthonormal basis from a list of vectors.

operators.name: oscillatory_integral
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
(Int, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, Int, Int, Int) -> Tensor<1, Float>
operators.doc: `oscillatory_integral(f, g, x, a, b, w, n)`: `list(re, im)` of `int_a^b f(x) exp(i w g(x)) dx` by Levin collocation at `n` Chebyshev points.

operators.name: outer
operators.doc: `outer(u, v)`: outer product matrix `u v^T` of vectors `u` and `v`.

operators.name: pacf
operators.doc:
`pacf(x, max_lag)`: the partial autocorrelation of `x` for lags `1..=max_lag`, by the Durbin–Levinson recursion.

Partial autocorrelation function, from the Durbin–Levinson recursion.

Returns `max_lag + 1` values with `result[0] = 1`; entry `k` is the last
coefficient of the order-`k` autoregression fitted to the sample
autocorrelations.

operators.name: parabolic_cylinder_d_complex
operators.doc:
`parabolic_cylinder_d_complex(nur, nui, zr, zi)`: `list(re, im)` of `D_nu(z)`.

Parabolic cylinder function `D_nu(z)` via asymptotic expansion for large `|z|`
in `|arg(z)| < 3*pi/4` and `1F1` connection formula with `rgamma` elsewhere.

operators.name: pareto
operators.doc: `pareto(scale, shape)`: Pareto distribution with minimum scale `scale` and shape parameter `shape`.

operators.name: partition_function
operators.doc: `partition_function(energies, T)`: canonical partition function `sum_i exp(-E_i / (k_B T))` over energy levels `energies`.

operators.name: partition_list
operators.doc: `partition_list(n)`: list of all integer partitions of `n` in non-increasing part order.

operators.name: partitions
operators.doc: `partitions(n)`: integer partition function `p(n)`, counting ways to write `n` as a sum of positive integers.

operators.name: partitions_distinct
operators.doc: `partitions_distinct(n)`: number of integer partitions of `n` into distinct positive parts.

operators.name: partitions_k
operators.doc: `partitions_k(n, k)`: number of integer partitions of `n` into exactly `k` positive parts.

operators.name: partitions_max
operators.doc: `partitions_max(n, k)`: number of integer partitions of `n` whose parts are at most `k`.

operators.name: path
operators.doc: `path(g, t, t0, t1)`: parameterized contour `g(t)` as `t` runs from `t0` to `t1`.

operators.name: pauli_matrices
operators.doc: `pauli_matrices`: list of the three 2x2 Pauli matrices `list(pauli_x, pauli_y, pauli_z)`.

operators.name: pauli_x
operators.doc: `pauli_x`: 2x2 Pauli matrix `sigma_x = [[0, 1], [1, 0]]`.

operators.name: pauli_y
operators.doc: `pauli_y`: 2x2 Pauli matrix `sigma_y = [[0, -i], [i, 0]]`.

operators.name: pauli_z
operators.doc: `pauli_z`: 2x2 Pauli matrix `sigma_z = [[1, 0], [0, -1]]`.

operators.name: pde_classify
operators.doc: `pde_classify(pde, u)`: classifies `pde` for unknown `u` by type (elliptic, parabolic, hyperbolic), order, dimension, and linearity.
examples: pde_classify(diff(u(x, t), t) - k*diff(diff(u(x, t), x), x), u(x, t))

operators.name: pde_complete_integral
operators.doc: `pde_complete_integral(pde, u)`: complete integral `u(x, y) = ...` of a first-order PDE via Charpit's method.

operators.name: pde_crum_kdv
operators.doc: `pde_crum_kdv(u, psis)`: iterated Crum-Darboux transformation of KdV seed `u` using eigenfunctions `psis`.

operators.name: pde_darboux_kdv
operators.doc: `pde_darboux_kdv(u, psi)`: single Darboux-Bäcklund transformation `u - 2 d^2/dx^2 ln(psi)` for KdV.

operators.name: pde_greens_ball
operators.doc: `pde_greens_ball(radius, dimension)`: Dirichlet Green's function for the negative Laplacian on a disk (`dimension = 2`) or ball (`dimension = 3`).

operators.name: pde_greens_ball_neumann
operators.doc: `pde_greens_ball_neumann(radius, dimension)`: zero-mean Neumann Green's function for the negative Laplacian on a disk (`dimension = 2`) or ball (`dimension = 3`).

operators.name: pde_greens_ball_robin
operators.doc: `pde_greens_ball_robin(radius, h)`: Green's function for the negative Laplacian inside a three-dimensional ball with Robin coefficient `h`.

operators.name: pde_greens_exterior_robin
operators.doc: `pde_greens_exterior_robin(radius, h, dimension)`: Green's function for the negative Laplacian outside a disk (`dimension = 2`) or ball (`dimension = 3`) with Robin coefficient `h`.

operators.name: pde_greens_function
operators.doc: `pde_greens_function(equation, u(x, …)[, conditions])`: Green's function of a linear constant-coefficient PDE. Homogeneous conditions on a box use eigenfunction series. Supported free-space and orthant cases use fundamental solutions or heat and wave kernels, with reflected sources for homogeneous Dirichlet or Neumann walls. The source coordinate for `x` is `s_x`.

operators.name: pde_greens_robin
operators.doc: `pde_greens_robin(dimension, h)`: Green's function for the negative Laplacian on a half-space with Robin coefficient `h` (`dimension = 2` or `3`).

operators.name: pde_hodograph
operators.doc: `pde_hodograph(sys, vars)`: derives the linear hodograph PDE `(lambda - mu) t_rs + lambda_r t_s - mu_s t_r = 0` for a 2x2 hyperbolic system.

operators.name: pde_hodograph_riemann
operators.doc: `pde_hodograph_riemann(gamma)`: Riemann function for the Euler-Poisson-Darboux hodograph equation.

operators.name: pde_hodograph_solution
operators.doc: `pde_hodograph_solution(F, G, ...)`: hodograph-transformed parametric solution `list(x(r, s), t(r, s))` in Riemann invariants.

operators.name: pde_kdv_reflectionless
operators.doc: `pde_kdv_reflectionless(params, x_t)`: KdV time evolution of the reflectionless potential `-N(N+1) kappa^2 sech^2(kappa x)`.

operators.name: pde_kdv_scattering
operators.doc: `pde_kdv_scattering(data, x, t)`: numeric KdV inverse-scattering (Gelfand-Levitan-Marchenko) evaluation at `(x, t)`.

operators.name: pde_kdv_soliton
operators.doc: `pde_kdv_soliton(kappas, x_t)`: N-soliton Hirota tau-function solution `-2 d^2/dx^2 ln det(I + A)` of the KdV equation.

operators.name: pde_nls_soliton
operators.doc: `pde_nls_soliton(params)`: bright soliton solution of the focusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation.

operators.name: pde_order
operators.doc: `pde_order(pde, u)`: highest partial-derivative order of `u` appearing in `pde`.
examples: pde_order(diff(u(x, y), x) + diff(u(x, y), y), u(x, y))

operators.name: pde_poisson_integral
operators.doc: `pde_poisson_integral(g, radius, dimension)`: harmonic extension of `g(phi)` on a disk (`dimension = 2`) or `g(theta, phi)` on a ball (`dimension = 3`). The positive `radius` is measured in the same units as `r`.

operators.name: pde_riemann_shallow_water
signatures: (Int, Int, Float, Int, Float) -> { _0: Float, _1: Float, _2: Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, _3: Tensor<1, Dyn<term>> }
operators.doc: `pde_riemann_shallow_water(hL, uL, hR, uR, g)`: exact Riemann problem solution `list(h*, u*, left_wave, right_wave)` for 1D shallow-water equations.

operators.name: pde_riemann_shallow_water_at
signatures: (Real, Real, Real, Real, Real, Real) -> Real
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
(Int, Int, Int, Float, Int, Float) -> Float
operators.doc: `pde_riemann_shallow_water_at(hL, uL, hR, uR, g, xi)`: self-similar shallow-water depth `h(x/t = xi)` from the Riemann solver.

operators.name: pde_riemann_shallow_water_velocity
signatures: (Real, Real, Real, Real, Real, Real) -> Real
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
(Int, Int, Int, Float, Int, Float) -> Float
operators.doc: `pde_riemann_shallow_water_velocity(hL, uL, hR, uR, g, xi)`: self-similar shallow-water velocity `u(x/t = xi)` from the Riemann solver.

operators.name: pde_separate
operators.doc: `pde_separate(pde, u)`: separated-variables ansatz and decoupled ODEs for `pde` and unknown `u`.

operators.name: pde_similarity
operators.doc: `pde_similarity(pde, u, generator)`: similarity reduction `list(u = g F(z), ODE)` along a scaling/symmetry `generator`.

operators.name: pde_sine_gordon_soliton
operators.doc: `pde_sine_gordon_soliton(params, x_t)`: kink/antikink or breather soliton solution of the sine-Gordon equation.

operators.name: pde_symmetries
operators.doc: `pde_symmetries(pde, u)`: Lie point symmetry infinitesimal generators of `pde` for unknown `u`.
examples: pde_symmetries(diff(u(x, t), t) = diff(diff(u(x, t), x), x), u(x, t))

operators.name: pde_traveling_wave
operators.doc: `pde_traveling_wave(pde, u, c)`: traveling-wave ansatz `u = F(x - c t)` and reduced ODE for speed `c`.

operators.name: pdf
operators.doc: `pdf(d, x)`: probability density function (or probability mass function) of distribution `d` at point `x`.

operators.name: pdsolve
signatures: () -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>> with 0... x Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: `pdsolve(pde, u, ...)`: general symbolic/numeric PDE solver for unknown `u` with optional boundary/initial conditions. For homogeneous heat or undamped wave equations on disks and balls, the numerical modal fallback accepts general initial data with homogeneous Neumann boundaries.
examples: pdsolve(list(diff(u(x, t), t) + diff(v(x, t), x) = 0, diff(u(x, t), x) + diff(v(x, t), t) = 0), list(u(x, t), v(x, t)))
pdsolve(list(diff(u(x, t), t) + diff(u(x, t), x) + diff(v(x, t), x) = 0, diff(v(x, t), t) + diff(v(x, t), x) = cos(x)), list(u(x, t), v(x, t)), list(u(x, 0) = 0, v(x, 0) = 0))

operators.name: pell
operators.doc: `pell(D)`: fundamental solution `list(x, y)` to Pell's equation `x^2 - D*y^2 = 1` for non-square `D > 0`.

operators.name: percentile
operators.doc:
`percentile(xs, p)`: `p`-th percentile (`quantile(xs, p / 100)`) of list `xs`.

Computes the p-th percentile of a slice of data.

# Arguments
* `data` - A mutable slice of `f64` data points.
* `p` - The desired percentile (e.g., 50.0 for median).

# Returns
The p-th percentile of the data (fractional `p` allowed), or NaN for empty
data, data containing NaN, or `p` outside `0..=100`.

operators.name: perfect_power
operators.doc: `perfect_power(n)`: `list(b, e)` with maximal `e >= 1` such that `b^e = n` (for `n >= 2`).

operators.name: period
operators.doc: `period(sequence)`: minimal positive period of a repeating list `sequence`.

operators.name: perm_compose
operators.doc: Composes two permutations `p` and `q` (1-based image lists) as `(p * q)(i) = p(q(i))`.

operators.name: perm_cycles
operators.doc: Decomposes permutation `p` into its non-trivial disjoint cycles.

operators.name: perm_group_are_conjugate
signatures: (Tensor<2, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>) -> Bool
operators.doc: Returns `true` if permutations `x` and `y` are conjugate in `<gens>`.

operators.name: perm_group_base
operators.doc: Returns a Schreier-Sims base (points whose pointwise stabilizer is trivial) for the group generated by `gens`.

operators.name: perm_group_basic_orbits
operators.doc: Returns the lengths of the basic orbits along the stabilizer chain (whose product equals the group order).

operators.name: perm_group_blocks
operators.doc: Computes the finest block system of `<gens>` placing points `a` and `b` in the same block.

operators.name: perm_group_center
operators.doc: Returns generators of the center `Z(G)` of the permutation group generated by `gens`.

operators.name: perm_group_centralizer
operators.doc: Returns generators of the centralizer of permutation `x` in the permutation group generated by `gens`.

operators.name: perm_group_class_count
operators.doc: Returns the number of conjugacy classes of `<gens>`.

operators.name: perm_group_composition_factors
operators.doc: Returns the prime orders `p` of the cyclic composition factors `C_p` of a solvable permutation group `<gens>`.

operators.name: perm_group_conjugacy_classes
operators.doc: Returns the conjugacy classes of `<gens>` as `list(list(representative, size), ...)` ordered by element order.

operators.name: perm_group_conjugating_element
operators.doc: Finds a permutation `g` in `<gens>` such that `g * x * g^(-1) = y`, or returns `false` if none exists.

operators.name: perm_group_contains
operators.doc: Tests whether permutation `p` belongs to the permutation group generated by `gens` by sifting through the stabilizer chain.

operators.name: perm_group_derived_series
operators.doc: Computes the orders of the derived series `G = G_0 > G_1 > ...` of the group generated by `gens`, stopping at the perfect core.

operators.name: perm_group_derived_subgroup
operators.doc: Returns generators of the commutator (derived) subgroup `G'` of the group generated by `gens`.

operators.name: perm_group_elements
operators.doc: Enumerates all elements of the permutation group generated by `gens` (for group orders up to 5040).

operators.name: perm_group_exponent
operators.doc: Computes the group exponent (LCM of all element orders) of `<gens>`.

operators.name: perm_group_intersection
operators.doc: Returns generators of the intersection `<gens> ∩ <hgens>` of two permutation groups.

operators.name: perm_group_is_abelian
operators.doc: Returns `true` if the permutation group generated by `gens` is abelian.

operators.name: perm_group_is_nilpotent
operators.doc: Returns `true` if the permutation group generated by `gens` is nilpotent.

operators.name: perm_group_is_normal
operators.doc: Returns `true` if `<hgens>` is a normal subgroup of `<gens>`.

operators.name: perm_group_is_primitive
operators.doc: Returns `true` if `<gens>` acts primitively (transitively with no non-trivial block system).

operators.name: perm_group_is_solvable
operators.doc: Returns `true` if the permutation group generated by `gens` is solvable.

operators.name: perm_group_is_transitive
operators.doc: Returns `true` if the permutation group generated by `gens` acts transitively on `1..n`.

operators.name: perm_group_lower_central_series

operators.doc:
Computes persistent homology barcodes over `Z/2` for a filtered complex up to `max_dim`, returning `list(birth, death)` pairs per dimension.

Exact persistent homology over `Z/2` of a filtered simplicial complex.

`filtration` lists `(value, simplex)` pairs in any order; every proper
face of a simplex must be present with a value no larger than the
simplex's. A repeated simplex enters at its earliest value, and both
signs of zero share a filtration level. Simplices are ordered by value,
then dimension, then lexicographically. The boundary matrix is reduced
by the standard left-to-right column algorithm with *clearing* (the twist
optimisation): dimensions are processed from the top down, and a column
that is the pivot of a reduced column of the next dimension is known to
reduce to zero and is skipped.

Returns one [`PersistenceDiagram`] per dimension `0..=max_dim`; each
interval is an exact `(birth, death)` pair of filtration values and a
class that never dies has `death = f64::INFINITY`. Zero-length
intervals are omitted. Intervals are sorted by birth then death.

# Errors
[`PersistenceError::InvalidFiltration`] if the input is not a filtration.

The polylogarithm `Li_s(z)` for real `s` and real `z`.

Real on `z <= 1` (including the negative axis); for `z > 1` the principal
value is complex in general and `NaN` is returned, except for
non-positive integer `s`, where `Li_{-n}(z)` is the real rational
function `z A_n(z)/(1-z)^(n+1)`. At `z = 1` the analytic continuation
`ζ(s)` is returned (and `+∞` at the pole `s = 1`).

operators.name: polylog_complex
operators.doc:
`polylog_complex(s, re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `Li_s(z)`.

The polylogarithm `Li_s(z)` for complex `s` and `z`, on the principal
branch (cut along `[1, ∞)`).

* `|z| <= 1/2`: the defining power series;
* non-positive integer `s = -n`: the rational function
  `z A_n(z)/(1-z)^(n+1)` with Eulerian numbers `A_n`;
* positive integer `s`: the logarithmic (Bernoulli/Hurwitz) continuation
  for `|z| <= 3/2` and Kummer's inversion relation beyond, so every `z` is
  covered;
* real `s >= -15.5` and real `z < 1` outside the series' fast region:
  the same continuation as [`lerch`] with `a = 1`;
* other `s`: the logarithmic expansion about `z = 1` for `|ln z| < 4.5`
  (the expansion is valid for `|ln z| < 2π`, but `ζ(s-k)` overflows
  `f64` before it converges near that bound);
* `z = 1`: `ζ(s)` (the analytic continuation, as in `mpmath`).

Outside the stated domain the result is `NaN + NaN i`. Accuracy is about
`1e-13` for moderate parameters.

`polynomial_system_roots(system)`: finite roots of a square polynomial system by total-degree homotopy continuation as `list(list(re, im), ...)`.

Solves a square polynomial system by total-degree homotopy continuation.

Solves the square polynomial system `system[i] = 0` (terms of equation
`i`, exponent vectors with one entry per variable) by total-degree
homotopy continuation in projective coordinates with a Cauchy endgame
and path-jumping protection; see the module documentation.

One [`PathEnd`] is returned per start solution (the product of the
degrees). Regular finite endpoints are Newton-polished; singular finite
endpoints and endpoints at infinity are classified with their winding
number. [`HomotopyOptions::precision`] selects double, double-double or
adaptive extended-precision tracking.

# Errors
[`RootError::Invalid`] for an empty system, exponent vectors of the wrong
length, nonfinite coefficients, equations without a positive declared
degree, or a product of equation degrees above 100 000.

operators.name: qr_pivoted_diagonal
operators.doc:
`qr_pivoted_diagonal(a)`: non-increasing absolute diagonal `|R_ii|` from column-pivoted QR of `a`.

Column-pivoted Householder QR (Businger and Golub).

At each step the remaining column of largest norm is brought forward, so
the diagonal of `R` decreases in magnitude and its decay reveals the
numerical rank. Column norms are downdated and recomputed when
cancellation makes the downdate unreliable. Each reflector applies to
contiguous columns, with large independent column batches running in parallel.

# Errors
[`LowRankError::Shape`] for inconsistent storage or non-finite entries,
and [`LowRankError::NoConvergence`] if the resulting factor exceeds the
representable floating-point range.

operators.doc: `raise_index(W, g)`: contravariant vector `g^ij W_j` obtained by raising index of `W` with inverse of metric `g`.

operators.name: randomized_singular_values
operators.doc: `randomized_singular_values(a, k)`: top `k` singular values of dense matrix `a` via randomized SVD.

operators.name: range_of
operators.doc: `range_of(xs)`: range `max(xs) - min(xs)` of list `xs`.

operators.name: rank
operators.doc: `rank(A)`: rank of matrix `A`.

operators.name: rational_approx
operators.doc: `rational_approx(f, x, a, b)`: AAA barycentric rational approximant of `f(x)` on `[a, b]`, including evaluation at the selected interpolation sites.

operators.name: ray
operators.doc: `ray(p, theta)`: half-line `{p + r * exp(I * theta) : r >= 0}` representing a branch cut.

operators.name: ray_plane
operators.doc: Intersects ray `(origin, dir)` with plane `(point, normal)`, returning `list(t, hit_point, normal)` or `false`.

operators.name: ray_sphere
operators.doc: Intersects ray `(origin, dir)` with sphere `(center, radius)`, returning `list(t, hit_point, normal)` or `false`.

operators.name: ray_triangle
signatures: (Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>) -> Bool
operators.doc: Intersects ray `(origin, dir)` with triangle `(a, b, c)`, returning `list(t, hit_point, normal)` or `false`.

operators.name: rayleigh
operators.doc: `rayleigh(sigma)`: Rayleigh distribution with scale parameter `sigma`.

operators.name: re
operators.doc: `re(z)`: real part of complex number `z`.

operators.name: real_integral
operators.doc: `real_integral(f, x)`: real-valued antiderivative of `f` with respect to `x` using `ln(abs(...))` where appropriate.

operators.name: real_qe
operators.doc: `real_qe(formula, vars)`: eliminates quantifiers over `vars` from a first-order real polynomial `formula` via cylindrical algebraic decomposition.

operators.name: real_root_intervals
operators.doc: `real_root_intervals(poly, var)`: returns isolating rational intervals `[lo, hi]` for all real roots of `poly` in `var`.

operators.name: reciprocal_lattice_vectors
signatures: (Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>) -> Tensor<2, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: `reciprocal_lattice_vectors(a1, a2, a3)`: reciprocal lattice basis `list(b1, b2, b3)`.

operators.name: reconstruct_holomorphic
operators.doc: `reconstruct_holomorphic(u, x, y)`: constructs holomorphic `u + I*v` from harmonic real part `u(x, y)`.

operators.name: refine_quality
signatures: (Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>, Real, Real) -> { points: Tensor<2, Real>, triangles: Tensor<2, Real> }
operators.doc:
`refine_quality(points, triangles, min_angle, max_area)`: `list(points, triangles)` after Ruppert-style circumcentre insertion until no triangle is below `min_angle` degrees or above `max_area`.

Refines `triangles` until every triangle satisfies an angle and area bound.

`min_angle_deg` is the smallest angle a triangle may have, and `max_area`
the largest area it may have. New vertices are inserted at circumcentres
(or at convex-hull edge midpoints when the circumcentre leaves the mesh),
and the triangulation is rebuilt as a Delaunay mesh after every pass.

# Errors

Returns `Err` when fewer than three points are given, when a triangle index
is out of range, when `min_angle_deg` is not in `(0, 60)`, or when
`max_area` is not positive and finite.

operators.name: reflect
operators.doc: Computes the reflection vector `d - 2 * dot(d, n) * n` of incident vector `d` across unit normal `n`.

operators.name: reflection
operators.doc: Constructs a homogeneous reflection matrix across a line (2D angle or normal) or hyperplane (normal vector).

operators.name: reflection_2d
operators.doc: Constructs a 3x3 homogeneous 2D reflection matrix across the line through the origin at angle `theta`.

operators.name: reflection_3d
operators.doc: Constructs a 4x4 homogeneous 3D reflection matrix across the plane through the origin with normal `list(a, b, c)`.

operators.name: refract
signatures: (Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>, Float) -> Tensor<1, Float>
operators.doc:
Computes the numeric Snell-refracted direction for incident vector `d`, normal `n`, and index ratio `eta`, or `false` on total internal reflection.

Computes the refraction of a vector through a surface.

Uses Snell's law with `eta` = n1/n2 (ratio of refractive indices).
Returns `None` for total internal reflection.

operators.name: reg_beta_complex
signatures: (Real, Real, Real, Real, Real, Real) -> Tensor<1, Real>
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
`reg_beta_complex(ar, ai, br, bi, zr, zi)`: `list(re, im)` of `I_z(a, b)`.

Regularized incomplete beta `I_z(a, b) = B_z(a, b) / B(a, b)`.

operators.name: reg_lower_gamma_complex
operators.doc:
`reg_lower_gamma_complex(ar, ai, zr, zi)`: `list(re, im)` of `P(a, z)`.

Regularized lower incomplete gamma `P(a, z) = gamma(a, z) / Gamma(a)`.

operators.name: reg_upper_gamma_complex
operators.doc:
`reg_upper_gamma_complex(ar, ai, zr, zi)`: `list(re, im)` of `Q(a, z)`.

Regularized upper incomplete gamma `Q(a, z) = Gamma(a, z) / Gamma(a)`.

operators.name: relativistic_energy
operators.doc: `relativistic_energy(m, p)`: relativistic energy `sqrt((p c_0)^2 + (m c_0^2)^2)`.

operators.name: relativistic_momentum
operators.doc:
`relativistic_momentum(m, v)`: relativistic momentum `gamma m v`.

Relativistic momentum: p = γmv

# Arguments
* `mass` - Rest mass (kg)
* `velocity` - Velocity (m/s)

operators.name: rem
operators.doc: `rem(p, q, var)`: returns the polynomial remainder of `p` divided by `q` in `var`.

operators.name: rencontres
operators.doc: `rencontres(n, k)`: rencontres number `D_{n, k}`, counting permutations of `n` elements with exactly `k` fixed points.

operators.name: representation_decompose
operators.doc: Decomposes matrix representation `mats` of finite group `G` into multiplicities of irreducible representations.

operators.name: representation_is_valid
operators.doc: Verifies whether matrix list `mats` (aligned with `G`'s elements) satisfies `M(a*b) = M(a)*M(b)` for all pairs.
examples: representation_is_valid(symmetric_group(3), list(list(list(1)), list(list(-1)), list(list(-1)), list(list(1)), list(list(1)), list(list(-1))))

operators.name: residuals
operators.doc: `residuals(xs, ys)`: residuals `y_i - f(x_i)` from simple linear regression on pairs `(xs, ys)`.

operators.name: residue
operators.doc:
`residue(f, z, a)` returns the coefficient of `(z - a)^(-1)` in `f(z)` near `a`.

It returns zero at a regular point and for a removable singularity.

It uses a pole calculation or a Laurent expansion and leaves a request unevaluated if the coefficient cannot be determined.

operators.name: residue_at_infinity
operators.doc: `residue_at_infinity(f, z)`: residue of `f(z)` at `z = infinity`, defined as `residue(-f(1/w)/w^2, w, 0)`.

operators.name: residue_real_integral
operators.doc: `residue_real_integral(f, x)`: evaluates `int_{-oo}^{oo} f(x) dx` by summing upper half-plane residues.

operators.name: residue_trig_integral
operators.doc: `residue_trig_integral(f, theta)`: evaluates `int_0^{2*pi} f(theta) dtheta` by unit-circle residue substitution.

operators.name: restrict
operators.doc: `restrict(formula, var, val)`: cofactors `formula` by assigning Boolean constant `val` (`true`/`false`) to `var`.

operators.name: resultant
operators.doc:
`resultant(p, q, var)` computes the Sylvester resultant of the nonzero polynomials `p` and `q` in `var`.

Coefficients may be exact rationals or expressions independent of `var`.

A positive-degree common factor gives zero. The resultant of two nonzero constants is one.

operators.name: rewrite_with
operators.doc: `rewrite_with(term, rules, vars)`: normalizes `term` to a normal form by exhaustively applying the rewrite `rules` over `vars`.

operators.name: rgamma_complex
operators.doc:
`rgamma_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `1 / Gamma(z)`.

Reciprocal gamma function `1 / Gamma(z)`, which is entire on `C` with
zeros at the non-positive integers.

operators.name: rhat
operators.doc:
`rhat(chains)`: the split Gelman–Rubin potential scale reduction of a list of chains of the same parameter; values near 1 indicate the chains have mixed.

Split-Rhat potential scale reduction factor of several chains.

Every chain is cut in half, the two halves are treated as independent
chains, and the ratio of the pooled variance estimate to the mean
within-chain variance is returned. Values near one indicate that the chains
have mixed; values well above one indicate that they disagree.

# Errors
Returns an error for fewer than two chains, chains of different lengths,
chains shorter than four draws, or a zero within-chain variance.

operators.name: ricci
operators.doc: `ricci(g, vars)`: Ricci curvature tensor `R_sn = R^r_srn` for metric `g` in `vars`.

operators.name: ricci_scalar
operators.doc:
`ricci_scalar(g, vars)`: scalar curvature `R = g^sn R_sn` for metric `g` in `vars`.

Ricci scalar `R = g^{μν} R_{μν}` at `point`.

# Errors

Returns an error for an invalid or singular metric at a connection stencil
point, or an unrepresentable stencil or result.

operators.name: riemann
operators.doc: `riemann(g, vars)`: Riemann curvature tensor `R^r_smn` for metric `g` in coordinates `vars`.

operators.name: riemann_genus
operators.doc: `riemann_genus(n, d)`: topological genus of the superelliptic Riemann surface `w^n = prod_{k=1}^d (z - r_k)` with distinct roots by the Riemann-Hurwitz formula.

operators.name: riemann_zeta_complex
operators.doc:
`riemann_zeta_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `zeta(s)`.

Complex Riemann zeta function `zeta(s)` over the entire complex plane.


Uses `eta(s) / (1 - 2^(1 - s))` for `Re(s) >= 0.5`, and the functional
equation `zeta(s) = 2^s * pi^(s - 1) * sin(pi * s / 2) * Gamma(1 - s) * zeta(1 - s)`
for `Re(s) < 0.5`.

operators.name: rips_filtration
operators.doc:
Constructs the Vietoris-Rips filtration of `points` up to diameter `max_eps` and simplex dimension `max_dim + 1`.

The Vietoris-Rips filtration of a finite metric space.

The space is given by its
distance matrix: every clique of the graph of edges of length at most
`max_eps`, up to dimension `max_simplex_dim`, with value its diameter.
`None` when more than `limit` simplices would be needed.

operators.name: rips_persistence
operators.doc: Computes Vietoris-Rips persistence barcodes `H_0 .. H_max_dim` for `points` up to `max_eps`.

operators.name: rips_persistence_diagram
operators.doc: Computes the Vietoris-Rips persistence diagram for `points` up to `max_eps` and `max_dim` as a flat list of `list(dim, birth, death)`.

operators.name: rising
operators.doc: `rising(x, k)`: rising factorial (Pochhammer symbol) `x * (x + 1) * ... * (x + k - 1)`.

operators.name: root_branch
operators.doc: `root_branch(z, n, k)` gives `|z|^(1/n) * exp(I * (arg(z) + 2*pi*k) / n)`. For a positive integer degree `n`, integer indices that differ by a multiple of `n` select the same root.

operators.name: root_of
operators.doc: `root_of(k, c0, c1, ..., cn)` represents the root with zero-based index `k` of `c0 + c1*x + ... + cn*x^n`. For exact rational coefficients, distinct real roots appear in ascending order, followed by the non-real roots ordered numerically by real and imaginary parts.

operators.name: rossler_orbit
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
(Tensor<1, Int>, Float, Int, Float, Float, Float) -> Tensor<2, Float>
operators.doc: Integrates the Rossler system `(p0, dt, n, a, b, c)` for `n` steps of size `dt` from `p0`.

operators.name: rotation
operators.doc: Constructs a 3x3 homogeneous 2D rotation matrix by angle `theta`.

operators.name: rotation_2d
operators.doc: Constructs a 3x3 homogeneous 2D rotation matrix by angle `theta`.

operators.name: rotation_3d_x
operators.doc: Constructs a 4x4 homogeneous 3D rotation matrix about the x-axis by angle `theta`.

operators.name: rotation_3d_y
operators.doc: Constructs a 4x4 homogeneous 3D rotation matrix about the y-axis by angle `theta`.

operators.name: rotation_3d_z
operators.doc: Constructs a 4x4 homogeneous 3D rotation matrix about the z-axis by angle `theta`.

operators.name: rotation_axis_angle
operators.doc: Constructs a 4x4 homogeneous 3D Rodrigues rotation matrix about normalized axis `list(ax, ay, az)` by angle `theta`.

operators.name: rotational_kinetic_energy
operators.doc: `rotational_kinetic_energy(inertia, w)`: rotational kinetic energy `(1/2) I w^2`.

operators.name: rouche_compare
operators.doc: `rouche_compare(f, g, z, center, radius)`: returns `1` if `|f(z)| > |g(z)|` on `|z - center| = radius`, `0` if `|f(z)| < |g(z)|`.

operators.name: round
operators.doc: `round(x)`: nearest integer to `x`, rounding half away from zero.

operators.name: rowspace
operators.doc: `rowspace(A)`: basis of the row space of matrix `A`.

operators.name: rref
operators.doc: `rref(A)`: reduced row echelon form of matrix `A`.

operators.name: rs_check
operators.doc: Verifies whether a Reed-Solomon codeword `c` with `n` parity symbols has zero syndromes.

operators.name: rs_decode
operators.doc: Decodes a Reed-Solomon codeword `c` with `n` parity symbols, correcting up to `n/2` symbol errors and returning the data part.

operators.name: rs_encode
operators.doc: Encodes `data` using systematic Reed-Solomon over GF(2^8) with `n` parity symbols.

operators.name: rs_error_count
operators.doc: Estimates the number of errors in a Reed-Solomon codeword `c` with `n` parity symbols as the degree of the Berlekamp-Massey error locator polynomial.

operators.name: rsa_decrypt
operators.doc: Computes RSA decryption `c^d mod n` for ciphertext `c`, private exponent `d`, and modulus `n`.

operators.name: rsa_encrypt
operators.doc: Computes RSA encryption `m^e mod n` for message `m`, public exponent `e`, and modulus `n`.

operators.name: rsa_keygen
operators.doc: Generates an RSA key tuple `list(n, e, d)` from distinct primes `p`, `q` and public exponent `e` with `d*e = 1 (mod (p-1)*(q-1))`.

operators.name: rsolve
operators.doc: `rsolve(equation, target, initial)`: solve a linear recurrence `equation` for `target` given `initial` conditions.

operators.name: rsolve_z
operators.doc: `rsolve_z(rec, seq, [ics...])`: solves a linear constant-coefficient recurrence relation `rec` for sequence `seq` via Z-transform.

operators.name: saddle_point_asymptotic
operators.doc: `saddle_point_asymptotic(g, phi, z, z0, lambda)`: leading saddle-point asymptotic approximation of `int g(z) exp(lambda * phi(z)) dz` near `z0`.

operators.name: sample_std
operators.doc: `sample_std(xs)`: sample standard deviation of list `xs`.

operators.name: sample_variance
operators.doc: `sample_variance(xs)`: sample variance `(1/(n-1)) sum (x_i - mean)^2` of list `xs`.

operators.name: sat_model
operators.doc: `sat_model(formula)`: returns one satisfying assignment for `formula` (or `false` if unsatisfiable).

operators.name: satisfiable
operators.doc: `satisfiable(formula)`: decides whether propositional `formula` has at least one satisfying assignment (`true` or `false`).

operators.name: sc
operators.doc: Inert simplicial complex wrapper `sc(list(simplex, ...))` where each simplex is a sorted list of integer vertices.

operators.name: sc_betti
operators.doc: Computes the `k`-th Betti number of simplicial complex `K` over the rationals.

operators.name: sc_boundary
operators.doc: Computes the oriented boundary chain `list(list((-1)^i, face_i), ...)` of simplex `s`.

operators.name: sc_boundary_matrix
operators.doc: Returns the integer boundary matrix `d_k` of simplicial complex `K` with `(k-1)`-simplices as rows and `k`-simplices as columns.

operators.name: sc_chain_boundary
operators.doc: Computes the boundary of a `k`-chain in simplicial complex `K`, simplifying coefficients and dropping zero terms.

operators.name: sc_coboundary_matrix
operators.doc: Returns the integer coboundary matrix `d^k` (transpose of `d_{k+1}`) of simplicial complex `K`.

operators.name: sc_cohomology
operators.doc: Computes the exact integral cohomology group `H^k(K; Z)` via the universal coefficient theorem.

operators.name: sc_cohomology_betti
operators.doc: Computes the `k`-th cohomology Betti number of simplicial complex `K`.

operators.name: sc_complex
operators.doc: Constructs a normalized simplicial complex `sc(...)` closed under faces from a list of simplices.

operators.name: sc_components
operators.doc: Returns the connected components of the 1-skeleton of simplicial complex `K` as sorted vertex lists.

operators.name: sc_cone
operators.doc: Constructs the cone `CK` over simplicial complex `K`.

operators.name: sc_dimension
operators.doc: Returns the dimension of simplicial complex `K`, or `-1` for the empty complex.

operators.name: sc_dunce_cap
operators.doc: Constructs a triangulation of the dunce cap with `k >= 3` edges per boundary arc (contractible but not collapsible).

operators.name: sc_euler_characteristic
operators.doc: Computes the Euler characteristic `sum (-1)^k * |K_k|` of simplicial complex `K`.

operators.name: sc_euler_from_betti
operators.doc: Computes the Euler characteristic `sum (-1)^k * b_k` from the Betti numbers of simplicial complex `K`.

operators.name: sc_fundamental_group
operators.doc: Computes a simplified edge-path presentation `list(n, relators)` of the fundamental group `pi_1(K)` for the component of the smallest vertex.

operators.name: sc_fundamental_group_raw
signatures: (sc) -> { _0: Int, _1: Tensor<1, Tensor<1, Int>>, _2: Tensor<2, Int> }
operators.doc: Computes the unsimplified edge-path presentation `list(n, relators, edges)` of `pi_1(K)` before Tietze simplification.

operators.name: sc_grid
operators.doc: Constructs a triangulated `w` by `h` rectangular grid simplicial complex.

operators.name: sc_homology
operators.doc: Computes the exact integral homology group `H_k(K; Z)` via Smith normal form as `list(rank, list(torsion...))`.

operators.name: sc_homology_all
operators.doc: Computes exact integral homology groups `H_k(K; Z)` for all dimensions `k = 0..dim(K)`.

operators.name: sc_homology_mod
operators.doc: Computes `dim H_k(K; Z/p)` of simplicial complex `K` over prime field `Z/p`.

operators.name: sc_induced_homology
operators.doc: Computes the rational matrix of the induced homomorphism `f_* : H_k(K; Q) -> H_k(L; Q)` for simplicial map `f`.

operators.name: sc_induced_homology_rank
operators.doc: Computes the rank of the induced homomorphism `f_* : H_k(K; Q) -> H_k(L; Q)` for simplicial map `f`.

operators.name: sc_intersection
operators.doc: Returns the intersection `K ∩ L` of two simplicial complexes.

operators.name: sc_is_simplicial_map
operators.doc: Returns `true` if vertex map `f` sends every simplex of `K` to a simplex of `L`.

operators.name: sc_is_subcomplex
operators.doc: Returns `true` if simplicial complex `L` is a subcomplex of `K`.

operators.name: sc_join
operators.doc: Constructs the simplicial join `K * L` of complexes `K` and `L`.

operators.name: sc_klein_bottle
operators.doc: Constructs a triangulated `m` by `n` Klein bottle simplicial complex (`m, n >= 3`).

operators.name: sc_mayer_vietoris_check
operators.doc: Verifies rank-level exactness and Euler characteristic additivity of the Mayer-Vietoris sequence for `A` and `B`.

operators.name: sc_mayer_vietoris_ranks
operators.doc: Computes the ranks of the connecting maps in the Mayer-Vietoris exact sequence for `A` and `B`.

operators.name: sc_pi1_abelianization
operators.doc: Computes the abelianization of `pi_1(K)` via Smith normal form as `list(rank, list(torsion...))`.

operators.name: sc_product
operators.doc: Constructs the triangulated Cartesian product `K × L` of two simplicial complexes.

operators.name: sc_projective_plane
operators.doc: Constructs a triangulation of the real projective plane `RP^2` (`k = 0` gives the minimal 6-vertex triangulation; `k >= 3` refines the boundary to `2k` edges).

operators.name: sc_reduced_homology
operators.doc: Computes the reduced integral homology group `H~_k(K; Z)` as `list(rank, list(torsion...))`.

operators.name: sc_relative_homology
operators.doc: Computes the exact relative integral homology group `H_k(K, L; Z)` for subcomplex `L` of `K`.

operators.name: sc_simplex
operators.doc: Constructs the standard `n`-simplex simplicial complex on `n + 1` vertices.

operators.name: sc_simplex_dimension
operators.doc: Returns the dimension `len(s) - 1` of simplex `s`.

operators.name: sc_simplices
operators.doc: Returns the list of `k`-simplices in simplicial complex `K`.

operators.name: sc_skeleton
operators.doc: Returns the `d`-skeleton of simplicial complex `K` (all simplices of dimension `<= d`).

operators.name: sc_sphere
operators.doc: Constructs the `n`-sphere `S^n` as the boundary of the `(n+1)`-simplex.

operators.name: sc_suspension
operators.doc: Constructs the suspension `SK` of simplicial complex `K`.

operators.name: sc_torus
operators.doc: Constructs a triangulated `m` by `n` torus simplicial complex (`m, n >= 3`).

operators.name: sc_union
operators.doc: Returns the union `K ∪ L` of two simplicial complexes.

operators.name: sc_verify_boundary
operators.doc: Verifies that the boundary operator satisfies `d_k * d_{k+1} = 0` for all dimensions in complex `K`.

operators.name: sc_verify_coboundary
operators.doc: Verifies that the coboundary operator satisfies `d^{k+1} * d^k = 0` for all dimensions in complex `K`.

operators.name: sc_verify_euler
operators.doc: Verifies that the alternating sum of Betti numbers equals the alternating simplex count of complex `K`.

operators.name: sc_wedge
operators.doc: Constructs the wedge sum `sc_wedge(K, L[, u, v])` by identifying vertex `u` of `K` with `v` of `L` (defaulting to smallest vertices).

operators.name: scalar_field_lagrangian
operators.doc: `scalar_field_lagrangian(phi, m, x)`: free real scalar field Lagrangian density `(1/2)(partial_mu phi)^2 - (1/2) m^2 phi^2`.

operators.name: scale_dist
operators.doc: `scale_dist(c, d)`: distribution of scaled random variable `c * X` where `X ~ d`.

operators.name: scale_factors
operators.doc: `scale_factors(sys, vars)`: Lamé scale factors `h_i = sqrt(g_ii)` of orthogonal coordinate system `sys` in `vars`.

operators.name: scaling
operators.doc: Constructs an `(n+1)x(n+1)` homogeneous scaling matrix from `n` scale factors.

operators.name: scaling_2d
operators.doc: Constructs a 3x3 homogeneous 2D scaling matrix for `(sx, sy)`.

operators.name: scaling_3d
operators.doc: Constructs a 4x4 homogeneous 3D scaling matrix for `(sx, sy, sz)`.

operators.name: scattering_amplitude
operators.doc: `scattering_amplitude(psi_i, psi_f, V, x)`: Born-approximation transition matrix element `<psi_f|V|psi_i>`.

operators.name: scattering_cross_section
operators.doc: `scattering_cross_section(M, flux, dphi)`: differential cross section `|M|^2 / flux * dphi`.

operators.name: schroeder
operators.doc: `schroeder(n)`: `n`-th large Schroeder number, counting lattice paths from `(0, 0)` to `(n, n)` with steps `(1, 0)`, `(0, 1)`, `(1, 1)` not crossing `y = x`.

operators.name: schwarzian_derivative
operators.doc: `schwarzian_derivative(f, z)`: Schwarzian derivative `(f'''/f') - (3/2)*(f''/f')^2`.

operators.name: schwarzschild_metric
operators.doc: `schwarzschild_metric(M, coords)`: Schwarzschild metric tensor in `(-, +, +, +)` signature for mass `M` and `coords = list(t, r, theta, phi)`.

operators.name: schwarzschild_radius
operators.doc: `schwarzschild_radius(M)`: Schwarzschild event-horizon radius `2 G_N M / c_0^2`.

operators.name: sde_levy_areas
signatures: (Int, Real[_], Tensor<1, Real>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Real[_]>
operators.doc: `sde_levy_areas(seed, h, dw, terms)`: the `m*m` row-major iterated Ito integrals over one step, conditioned on the `m` increments `dw`, with a seeded Fourier bridge truncated at `terms` modes. Requires finite inputs and results, at most 4,194,304 output entries and 67,108,864 pair-mode terms.

operators.name: sde_scheme_info
operators.doc: `sde_scheme_info(name)`: the metadata of one stochastic scheme as `list(strong_order, ito, commutative_only, adaptive, levy_areas)` — the strong order for commutative noise and four flags (1 or 0). Unknown names stay a request.

operators.name: sde_wiener
operators.doc: `sde_wiener(seed, m, steps, h)`: the `steps x m` matrix of seeded Brownian increments `dW[k][j] ~ N(0, h)`, reproducible bit for bit from `seed`.

operators.name: sdp_solve
signatures: (Tensor<1, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<1, Symbol>, Tensor<1, Real>, Int) -> { x: Tensor<1, Real>, objective: Real, iterations: Real, primal_residual: Real, dual_residual: Real, min_eigenvalue: Real }
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
`sdp_solve(c, f0, fs, a, rel, b, max_iter)`: `list(x, objective, iterations, primal_residual, dual_residual, min_eigenvalue)` minimising `c . x` subject to `F_0 + sum x_i F_i >= 0` and the equality rows `a x = b`.

Solves a semidefinite program by SDPAD.

# Errors
Returns an error string when the dimensions disagree, when an entry is not
finite, when `max_iter` is zero, or when the `x`-update system is singular.

operators.name: sec
operators.doc: `sec(x)`: secant `1 / cos(x)` of angle `x` in radians.

operators.name: sech
operators.doc: `sech(x)`: hyperbolic secant `1 / cosh(x)`.

operators.name: second_order_energy_correction
operators.doc: `second_order_energy_correction(V, states, energies, n, x)`: second-order Rayleigh-Schrodinger energy shift `sum_{m != n} |<m|V|n>|^2 / (E_n - E_m)` over basis `states` in variable `x` (1-based index `n`).

operators.name: shear
operators.doc: Constructs a homogeneous shear matrix from 2 (`2D`) or 6 (`3D`) shear parameters, or a general off-diagonal list.

operators.name: shear_2d
operators.doc: Constructs a 3x3 homogeneous 2D shear matrix from `(shx, shy)`.

operators.name: shear_3d
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc: Constructs a 4x4 homogeneous 3D shear matrix from 6 off-diagonal shear factors.

operators.name: shi
operators.doc: `shi(x)`: hyperbolic sine integral `Shi(x) = int_0^x sinh(t)/t dt`.

operators.name: shift_dist
operators.doc: `shift_dist(c, d)`: distribution of shifted random variable `X + c` where `X ~ d`.

operators.name: si
operators.doc: `si(x)`: sine integral `Si(x) = int_0^x sin(t)/t dt`.

operators.name: sigma
operators.doc: `sigma(n, k)`: sum of `k`-th powers of positive divisors `sigma_k(n)` of `n`.

operators.name: sigma_SB
operators.doc: `sigma_SB`: Stefan-Boltzmann constant in W/(m^2*K^4).

operators.name: sign
operators.doc: `sign(x)`: signum function (`-1` for `x < 0`, `0` at `0`, `1` for `x > 0`).

operators.name: sign_complex
operators.doc:
`sign_complex(z)`: complex signum `z / abs(z)` on the unit circle.

Complex signum `z / |z|`, or `0` if `z == 0`.

operators.name: similarity_dimension
operators.doc: Computes the similarity dimension `-ln(N)/ln(r)` for equal contraction ratios, or builds the Moran equation `sum r_i^D = 1`.

operators.name: simplify_logic
operators.doc: `simplify_logic(formula)`: simplifies propositional `formula` using Quine-McCluskey minimization.

operators.name: simplify_radicals
operators.doc: `simplify_radicals(expr)`: simplifies radical expressions in `expr` by denesting nested roots and combining or rationalizing surds.

operators.name: simplify_units
operators.doc: `simplify_units(expr)`: reduces a dimensional expression `expr` to coherent SI base units.

operators.name: simplify_with_relations
operators.doc: `simplify_with_relations(expr, relations, vars)`: simplifies `expr` modulo polynomial side `relations` over `vars`.

operators.name: sin
operators.doc: `sin(x)`: sine of angle `x` in radians.

operators.name: sin_integral_complex
operators.doc:
`sin_integral_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `Si(z)`.

Complex sine and cosine integrals `(Si(z), Ci(z))`.

operators.name: sinc
operators.doc:
`sinc(x)`: normalized cardinal sine `sin(pi * x) / (pi * x)` with `sinc(0) = 1`.

Computes the sinc function sinc(x) = sin(πx) / (πx).

operators.name: singularity
operators.doc: `singularity(f, z, a)`: classification of `f(z)` at `a` (`regular`, `removable`, `list(pole, m)`, or `essential`).

operators.name: sinh
operators.doc:
`sinh(x)`: hyperbolic sine `(e^x - e^-x) / 2`.

`sinh(x)` as a ball.

# Errors
Fails when an exponent leaves the representable range.

operators.name: sinh_integral_complex
operators.doc:
`sinh_integral_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `Shi(z)`.

Complex hyperbolic sine and cosine integrals `(Shi(z), Chi(z))`.

operators.name: skewness
operators.doc:
`skewness(xs)`: Pearson skewness `m3 / m2^(3/2)` of list `xs`.

Computes the adjusted Fisher-Pearson sample skewness coefficient `G1`
(the estimator used by Excel's `SKEW` and by `scipy.stats.skew(bias=False)`).

With `g1 = m3 / m2^(3/2)` (central moments divided by `n`),
`G1 = sqrt(n (n - 1)) / (n - 2) * g1`.

Returns `NaN` for fewer than three points and `0.0` for constant data.

operators.name: skewness_of
operators.doc: `skewness_of(d)`: skewness (standardized 3rd central moment) of distribution `d`.

operators.name: sl2_basis
operators.doc: `sl2_basis()`: Chevalley basis `(h, e, f)` of `sl(2)` with `[h, e] = 2e`, `[h, f] = -2f`, `[e, f] = h`.

operators.name: sl_basis
operators.doc: `sl_basis(n)`: standard traceless matrix basis of the special linear Lie algebra `sl(n)`.

operators.name: sl_density
operators.doc: `sl_density(lambda, epsilon, coeffs...)`: spectral density `Im(m(lambda + i * epsilon)) / pi` of a Sturm-Liouville operator.

operators.name: sl_eigen
operators.doc: `sl_eigen(n, coeffs...)`: `n`-th eigenvalue of a regular Sturm-Liouville problem `-(p y')' + q y = mu w y` via Chebyshev collocation.

operators.name: sl_mfun_im
operators.doc: `sl_mfun_im(lambda, epsilon, coeffs...)`: imaginary part of the Weyl-Titchmarsh `m`-function at `lambda + i * epsilon`.

operators.name: sl_mfun_re
operators.doc: `sl_mfun_re(lambda, epsilon, coeffs...)`: real part of the Weyl-Titchmarsh `m`-function at `lambda + i * epsilon`.

operators.name: sl_mode
operators.doc: `sl_mode(n, x, coeffs...)`: `n`-th normalized Sturm-Liouville eigenfunction evaluated at `x`.

operators.name: sl_neg_root
operators.doc: `sl_neg_root(alpha1, beta1, alpha2, beta2, L)`: unique negative Sturm-Liouville eigenvalue root (if any) for Robin boundary conditions on `[0, L]`.

operators.name: sl_neg_root_n
signatures: (Real, Real, Real, Real, Real, Real) -> Real
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc: `sl_neg_root_n(alpha1, beta1, alpha2, beta2, L, k)`: `k`-th negative Sturm-Liouville eigenvalue root on `[0, L]`.

operators.name: sl_root
signatures: (Real, Real, Real, Real, Real, Real) -> Real
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc: `sl_root(alpha1, beta1, alpha2, beta2, L, k)`: `k`-th positive Sturm-Liouville eigenvalue root on `[0, L]` with general linear boundary conditions.

operators.name: sl_weight
operators.doc: `sl_weight(x, coeffs...)`: Sturm-Liouville weight function `w(x)` evaluated at `x`.

operators.name: smith
operators.doc: `smith(A)`: Smith normal form `list(S, U, V)` of integer matrix `A` with `U A V = S`.

operators.name: smul
operators.doc: `smul(c, A)`: scalar multiplication `c * A` of scalar `c` and matrix or vector `A`.
examples: smul(-1, matmul(list(list(1, 0, 0), list(0, 1, 0), list(0, 0, 1)), list(list(4, 1, 0), list(0, 4, 1), list(0, 0, 4))))

operators.name: so3_basis
operators.doc: `so3_basis()`: standard basis `(Lx, Ly, Lz)` of `so(3)` with `[Li, Lj] = eps_ijk Lk`.

operators.name: so_basis
operators.doc: `so_basis(n)`: standard skew-symmetric matrix basis `E_ij - E_ji` of `so(n)`.

operators.name: sobolev_h1
operators.doc: `sobolev_h1(f, x, a, b)`: Sobolev `H^1` norm `sqrt(||f||_2^2 + ||f'||_2^2)` on `[a, b]`.

operators.name: socp_solve
signatures: (Tensor<1, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<1, Symbol>, Tensor<1, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>, Int) -> { x: Tensor<1, Real>, objective: Real, iterations: Real, primal_residual: Real, dual_residual: Real, gap: Real }
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc:
`socp_solve(c, a, rel, b, cones, bounds, max_iter)`: `list(x, objective, iterations, primal_residual, dual_residual, gap)` of a second-order cone program; each cone is `list(a, b, c, d)` standing for `||A x + b|| <= c . x + d`.

Solves a second-order cone program.

# Errors
Returns an error string when the dimensions disagree, when an entry is not
finite, when `max_iter` is zero, or when the KKT system is singular.

operators.name: solve
operators.doc: `solve(eq_or_system, var_or_vars)`: symbolically solves an equation, inequality, or system for `var_or_vars`.

operators.name: solve_box
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Int>) -> Tensor<1, Tensor<2, Float>>
(Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Tensor<1, Symbol>, Tensor<2, Int>) -> Tensor<1, Tensor<3, Float>>
operators.doc: `solve_box(system, vars, box_bounds)`: isolates all roots of `system` in `vars` within `box_bounds`.
examples: solve_box(list(x^2 + y^2 - 1, y - x), list(x, y), list(list(-2, 2), list(-2, 2)))

operators.name: solve_burgers_equation
operators.doc: `solve_burgers_equation(pde, u, ...)`: solves Burgers' inviscid or viscous nonlinear PDE.

operators.name: solve_complex
operators.doc: `solve_complex(poly, var)`: finds all complex roots of polynomial `poly` in `var`.

operators.name: solve_euler_lagrange
operators.doc: `solve_euler_lagrange(L, y, x)`: solves the Euler-Lagrange differential equation `euler_lagrange(L, y, x) = 0` for `y`.

operators.name: solve_general
operators.doc: `solve_general(eq_or_system, var_or_vars)`: solves an equation or system symbolically, including parameterized/underdetermined solution sets.

operators.name: solve_heat_equation
operators.doc: `solve_heat_equation(pde, u, ...)`: solves the heat/diffusion equation `u_t = alpha laplacian(u) + f`.

operators.name: solve_heat_equation_1d
operators.doc: `solve_heat_equation_1d(pde, u, ...)`: solves the 1D heat equation.

operators.name: solve_heat_equation_2d
operators.doc:
`solve_heat_equation_2d(pde, u, ...)`: solves the 2D heat equation.

Solves a 2D heat equation `u_t = alpha * ∇²u` using the finite difference method.

operators.name: solve_heat_equation_3d
operators.doc: `solve_heat_equation_3d(pde, u, ...)`: solves the 3D heat equation.

operators.name: solve_helmholtz_equation
operators.doc: `solve_helmholtz_equation(pde, u, ...)`: solves the Helmholtz equation `laplacian(u) + k^2 u = f`.

operators.name: solve_klein_gordon_equation
operators.doc: `solve_klein_gordon_equation(pde, u, ...)`: solves the Klein-Gordon wave equation.

operators.name: solve_laplace_equation
operators.doc: `solve_laplace_equation(pde, u, ...)`: solves Laplace's equation `laplacian(u) = 0`.

operators.name: solve_laplace_equation_1d
operators.doc: `solve_laplace_equation_1d(pde, u, ...)`: solves the 1D Laplace equation.

operators.name: solve_laplace_equation_2d
operators.doc: `solve_laplace_equation_2d(pde, u, ...)`: solves the 2D Laplace equation.

operators.name: solve_laplace_equation_3d
operators.doc: `solve_laplace_equation_3d(pde, u, ...)`: solves the 3D Laplace equation.

operators.name: solve_pde
operators.doc:
`solve_pde(pde, u, ...)`: alias for `pdsolve`; solves `pde` for unknown `u`.

Unified time-dependent PDE evolution driver supporting both fixed and
adaptive step sizes via [`OdeStepMode`](crate::kernels::ode::OdeStepMode).

`step_fn(t, state, dt)` advances `state` by a single step `dt` from time
`t`. In [`OdeStepMode::Fixed`](crate::kernels::ode::OdeStepMode::Fixed),
it takes uniform steps of size `dt` (with the final step landing on
`t_span.1`). In
[`OdeStepMode::Adaptive`](crate::kernels::ode::OdeStepMode::Adaptive), it
delegates to [`adaptive_evolve`] with Richardson step-doubling of `order`.

# Errors
Returns [`FdmError::Domain`] for invalid time spans, step sizes,
tolerances, non-finite states, or step-budget exhaustion.

operators.name: solve_pde_by_characteristics
operators.doc: `solve_pde_by_characteristics(pde, u, ...)`: solves first-order or quasilinear PDEs via the method of characteristics.

operators.name: solve_pde_by_greens_function
operators.doc: `solve_pde_by_greens_function(pde, u, ...)`: solves linear inhomogeneous PDEs via Green's function integration.

operators.name: solve_pde_by_separation_of_variables
operators.doc: `solve_pde_by_separation_of_variables(pde, u, ...)`: solves linear boundary-value PDEs by separation of variables.

operators.name: solve_poisson_equation
operators.doc: `solve_poisson_equation(pde, u, ...)`: solves Poisson's equation `laplacian(u) = f`.

operators.name: solve_poisson_equation_1d
operators.doc: `solve_poisson_equation_1d(pde, u, ...)`: solves the 1D Poisson equation.

operators.name: solve_poisson_equation_2d
operators.doc: `solve_poisson_equation_2d(pde, u, ...)`: solves the 2D Poisson equation.

operators.name: solve_poisson_equation_3d
operators.doc: `solve_poisson_equation_3d(pde, u, ...)`: solves the 3D Poisson equation.

operators.name: solve_schrodinger_equation
operators.doc: `solve_schrodinger_equation(pde, u, ...)`: solves the time-dependent or stationary Schrodinger PDE.

operators.name: solve_second_order_pde
operators.doc: `solve_second_order_pde(pde, u, ...)`: general solver for linear second-order PDEs.

operators.name: solve_time_independent_schrodinger
operators.doc: `solve_time_independent_schrodinger(H, psi, x)`: returns `list(E, psi)` for eigenstate `psi` of `H`.

operators.name: solve_wave_equation
operators.doc: `solve_wave_equation(pde, u, ...)`: solves the wave equation `u_tt = c^2 laplacian(u) + f`.

operators.name: solve_wave_equation_1d
operators.doc:
`solve_wave_equation_1d(pde, u, conditions)` solves a symbolic wave equation and returns an equation for the unknown function.

Supply the unknown as an application such as `u(x, t)`. The optional list of conditions gives initial values, initial velocity, or boundary data.

This spelling uses the same solver as `solve_wave_equation`. The arguments of the unknown function determine the spatial dimension.

operators.name: solve_wave_equation_1d_dalembert
operators.doc: `solve_wave_equation_1d_dalembert(pde, u, ...)`: solves the 1D wave equation via d'Alembert's traveling-wave formula.

operators.name: solve_wave_equation_2d
operators.doc: `solve_wave_equation_2d(pde, u, ...)`: solves the 2D wave equation.

operators.name: solve_wave_equation_3d
operators.doc: `solve_wave_equation_3d(pde, u, ...)`: solves the 3D wave equation.

operators.name: solve_with_fourier_transform
operators.doc: `solve_with_fourier_transform(pde, u, ...)`: solves linear constant-coefficient PDEs using the Fourier transform.

operators.name: sp_add
operators.doc: `sp_add(A, B)`: returns the sum `A + B` of two `sparse` matrices.
examples: sp_add(sparse(3, 3, list(list(1, 1, 2), list(2, 2, 3), list(3, 1, 1), list(3, 3, 4))), sp_scale(-1, sparse(3, 3, list(list(1, 1, 2), list(2, 2, 3), list(3, 1, 1), list(3, 3, 4)))))

operators.name: sp_basis
operators.doc: `sp_basis(n)`: standard symplectic matrix basis of `sp(2n)`.

operators.name: sp_det
operators.doc: `sp_det(A)`: computes the exact determinant of a square `sparse` matrix `A`.

operators.name: sp_det_mod
operators.doc: `sp_det_mod(A, p)`: computes the determinant of integer `sparse` matrix `A` modulo prime `p`.

operators.name: sp_diag
operators.doc: `sp_diag(entries)`: constructs a sparse diagonal matrix from a list of diagonal entries.

operators.name: sp_dims
operators.doc: `sp_dims(sp)`: returns `[rows, cols]` for a `sparse` matrix.

operators.name: sp_from_dense
operators.doc: `sp_from_dense(mat)`: converts a dense matrix (list of row lists) into a canonical `sparse` matrix.

operators.name: sp_identity
operators.doc: `sp_identity(n)`: constructs the `n x n` sparse identity matrix.

operators.name: sp_matmul
operators.doc: `sp_matmul(A, B)`: returns the matrix product `A * B` of two `sparse` matrices.
examples: sp_matmul(sparse(3, 3, list(list(1, 1, 2), list(2, 2, 3), list(3, 1, 1), list(3, 3, 4))), sp_identity(3))

operators.name: sp_matvec
operators.doc: `sp_matvec(A, v)`: multiplies a `sparse` matrix `A` by a dense vector `v`.
examples: sp_matvec(sparse(3, 3, list(list(1, 1, 2), list(2, 2, 3), list(3, 1, 1), list(3, 3, 4))), list(1, 1, 1))
sp_matvec(sparse(2, 2, list(list(1, 2, a), list(2, 1, b))), list(x, y))

operators.name: sp_minpoly_mod
operators.doc: `sp_minpoly_mod(A, p)`: computes the minimal polynomial coefficients of integer `sparse` matrix `A` modulo prime `p`.

operators.name: sp_nnz
operators.doc: `sp_nnz(sp)`: returns the number of nonzero entries in a `sparse` matrix.
examples: sp_nnz(sp_add(sparse(3, 3, list(list(1, 1, 2), list(2, 2, 3), list(3, 1, 1), list(3, 3, 4))), sp_scale(-1, sparse(3, 3, list(list(1, 1, 2), list(2, 2, 3), list(3, 1, 1), list(3, 3, 4))))))

operators.name: sp_nullspace
operators.doc: `sp_nullspace(A)`: computes a basis for the right nullspace `{x : A * x = 0}` of a `sparse` matrix `A`.

operators.name: sp_rank
operators.doc: `sp_rank(A)`: computes the exact rank of a `sparse` matrix `A`.

operators.name: sp_rank_mod
operators.doc: `sp_rank_mod(A, p)`: computes the rank of integer `sparse` matrix `A` modulo prime `p`.

operators.name: sp_scale
operators.doc: `sp_scale(scalar, A)`: scales a `sparse` matrix `A` by `scalar`.
examples: sp_scale(-1, sparse(3, 3, list(list(1, 1, 2), list(2, 2, 3), list(3, 1, 1), list(3, 3, 4))))

operators.name: sp_solve
operators.doc: `sp_solve(A, b)`: solves the square linear system `A * x = b` for a `sparse` matrix `A`.

operators.name: sp_solve_general
operators.doc: `sp_solve_general(A, b)`: solves a general (possibly rectangular or rank-deficient) sparse linear system `A * x = b`.

operators.name: sp_solve_mod
operators.doc: `sp_solve_mod(A, b, p)`: solves `A * x = b (mod p)` for integer `sparse` matrix `A` and prime `p`.
examples: sp_solve_mod(sparse(3, 3, list(list(1, 1, 2), list(2, 2, 3), list(3, 1, 1), list(3, 3, 4))), list(2, 3, 5), 101)

operators.name: sp_to_dense
operators.doc: `sp_to_dense(sp)`: converts a `sparse` matrix into a dense list of row lists.
examples: sp_to_dense(sp_matmul(sparse(3, 3, list(list(1, 1, 2), list(2, 2, 3), list(3, 1, 1), list(3, 3, 4))), sp_identity(3)))

operators.name: sp_transpose
operators.doc: `sp_transpose(sp)`: returns the transpose of a `sparse` matrix.

operators.name: sparse
operators.doc: `sparse(rows, cols, entries)`: canonical sparse matrix constructor with dimensions `rows x cols` and sorted nonzero `[row, col, value]` triples.

operators.name: sparse_solve
signatures: (Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<1, Real>, Real, Symbol) -> Tensor<1, Real>
operators.doc: `sparse_solve(entries, b, tol, method)`: solve sparse `A x = b` from `(i, j, v)` triplets using `minres`, `fgmres`, `bicgstab_l`, or `idr_s`.

operators.name: spectral
operators.doc: `spectral(A)`: spectral decomposition `list(eigenvalues, projectors)` of diagonalizable matrix `A`.

operators.name: spectral_analysis
signatures: (Tensor<2, Int>) -> { _0: Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, _1: Tensor<1, { _0: Dyn<term>, _1: Int, _2: Tensor<2, Dyn<term>> }> }
operators.doc: Returns `list(eigenvals(M), eigenvects(M))` for square matrix `M`.

operators.name: spence_complex
operators.doc:
`spence_complex(re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `Li_2(1 - z)`.

Spence's dilogarithm `spence(z) = Li_2(1 - z)`.

operators.name: spherical_harmonic
operators.doc: `spherical_harmonic(l, m, theta, phi)`: orthonormal spherical harmonic `Y_l^m(theta, phi)` with the Condon-Shortley phase as an explicit trigonometric expression.

operators.name: spherical_in_complex
operators.doc:
`spherical_in_complex(n, re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `i_n(z)`.

Modified spherical Bessel function `i_n(z) = sqrt(pi / (2z)) * I_{n + 1/2}(z)`.

operators.name: spherical_jn_complex
operators.doc:
`spherical_jn_complex(n, re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `j_n(z)`.

Spherical Bessel function `j_n(z) = sqrt(pi / (2z)) * J_{n + 1/2}(z)`.

operators.name: spherical_kn_complex
operators.doc:
`spherical_kn_complex(n, re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `k_n(z)`.

Modified spherical Bessel function `k_n(z) = sqrt(2 / (pi*z)) * K_{n + 1/2}(z)` (DLMF 10.47.9: `sqrt(pi/(2z)) * K_{n+1/2}(z)`).

operators.name: spherical_yn_complex
operators.doc:
`spherical_yn_complex(n, re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `y_n(z)`.

Spherical Bessel function `y_n(z) = sqrt(pi / (2z)) * Y_{n + 1/2}(z)`.

operators.name: spheroidal_eigen
operators.doc: `spheroidal_eigen(m, n, gamma)`: numeric angular spheroidal eigenvalue `lambda_{mn}(gamma)`.

operators.name: spheroidal_mode
operators.doc: `spheroidal_mode(m, n, gamma, x)`: normalized angular spheroidal wave function `S_{mn}(gamma, x)`.

operators.name: spheroidal_radial
operators.doc: `spheroidal_radial(kind, m, n, gamma, xi)`: prolate (`kind > 0`) or oblate radial spheroidal wave function at `xi`. The kind, coordinate and `gamma` must be finite, and the degree and order must be integers with `0 <= m <= n <= 10000`. The radial coordinate is at least one for prolate and at least zero for oblate.

operators.name: spin_operator
operators.doc: `spin_operator(sigma)`: spin-1/2 operator `(hbar / 2) * sigma`.

operators.name: sqrt
operators.doc: `sqrt(x)`: principal square root of `x`.

operators.name: sqrt_branch
operators.doc: `sqrt_branch(z, k)` selects the principal square root for an even integer `k` and its negative for an odd integer `k`.

operators.name: sqrt_cut
operators.doc:
`sqrt_cut(z, theta0)`: square root with branch cut along ray `theta0`.

Square root `sqrt(|z|) * cis(arg_branch(z, theta0) / 2)` with branch cut along ray `theta0`.

operators.name: sqrtmod
operators.doc: `sqrtmod(a, p)`: modular square root `r` satisfying `r^2 = a (mod p)` for prime `p`.

operators.name: square_free_factors
operators.doc:
`square_free_factors(poly, var)` decomposes a nonzero polynomial in the symbol `var` over the rationals.

Returns `list(unit, list(list(factor, multiplicity), ...))`. The unit is the leading coefficient. Each factor is monic and square-free, and the factors are pairwise coprime and ordered by increasing multiplicity.

A nonzero constant has an empty factor list. The zero polynomial and coefficients outside the rationals leave the request unevaluated.

operators.name: ss_transfer
signatures: (Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>, Tensor<2, Real>) -> { num: Tensor<1, Real>, den: Tensor<1, Real> }
operators.doc:
`ss_transfer(a, b, c, d)`: `list(num, den)`, the transfer function from the first input to the first output.

Converts a state-space model to one transfer function per input/output
pair, ordered output-major (output `0` against every input, then output
`1`, and so on).

The denominator is obtained by the Faddeev-LeVerrier algorithm and the
numerator from the Markov parameters `C A^k B` plus the feedthrough term.

# Errors
Returns an error when the model has inconsistent dimensions or the
polynomial construction fails.

operators.name: standard_error
operators.doc:
`standard_error(xs)`: standard error of the mean `sample_std / sqrt(n)` of list `xs`.

Computes the sample standard error of the mean (SEM = `std_dev` / sqrt(n)).

operators.name: std
operators.doc: `std(xs)`: population standard deviation of list `xs`.

operators.name: std_of
operators.doc: `std_of(d)`: standard deviation `sqrt(Var(X))` of distribution `d`.

operators.name: stefan_boltzmann_law
operators.doc: `stefan_boltzmann_law(T)`: blackbody total emissive power `sigma_SB T^4`.

operators.name: stirling1
operators.doc: `stirling1(n, k)`: unsigned Stirling number of the first kind `|s(n, k)|`, counting permutations of `n` elements with `k` cycles.

operators.name: stirling2
operators.doc: `stirling2(n, k)`: Stirling number of the second kind `S(n, k)`, counting partitions of an `n`-element set into `k` non-empty subsets.

operators.name: stokes_theorem
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc: `stokes_theorem(F, surface, u, v, u0, u1, v0, v1)`: circulation of `F` around the boundary of `surface(u, v)` via Stokes' theorem.

operators.name: structure_constants
signatures: () -> Tensor<3, Int> with 0... x Tensor<3, Int>
() -> Tensor<3, Dyn<term>> with 0... x Tensor<3, Dyn<term>>
operators.doc: `structure_constants(basis[, coords])`: structure constants tensor `c[i][j][k]` satisfying `[e_i, e_j] = sum_k c_ijk e_k`.

operators.name: struve_h
operators.doc: `struve_h(nu, z)`: Struve function `H_nu(z)`.

operators.name: struve_h_complex
operators.doc:
`struve_h_complex(nu, re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `H_nu(z)`.

Complex Struve function `H_nu(z)` via ascending power series (using `rgamma`
to handle negative half-integer `nu`) and large-`|z|` asymptotic expansion.

operators.name: struve_l
operators.doc: `struve_l(nu, z)`: modified Struve function `L_nu(z)`.

operators.name: struve_l_complex
operators.doc:
`struve_l_complex(nu, re, im)`: `list(re, im)` of `L_nu(z)`.

Complex modified Struve function `L_nu(z) = -i * exp(-i*nu*pi/2) * H_nu(i*z)`.

operators.name: student_t
operators.doc: `student_t(nu)`: Student's t-distribution with `nu` degrees of freedom.

operators.name: sturm_sequence
operators.doc:
`sturm_sequence(poly, var)` returns the Sturm chain of a univariate polynomial with exact rational coefficients.

The output is a `list(...)` of polynomials in `var`. For a nonconstant polynomial the chain starts with the polynomial and its derivative, followed by successive negated nonzero remainders.

A constant produces a singleton list, including `list(0)` for zero. For example, `sturm_sequence(x^2 - 2, x)` returns `list(x^2 - 2, 2*x, 2)`.

operators.name: su2_basis
operators.doc: `su2_basis()`: standard basis `-I * sigma_k / 2` of `su(2)` with `[e_i, e_j] = eps_ijk e_k`.

operators.name: su_basis
operators.doc: `su_basis(n)`: standard skew-Hermitian traceless matrix basis of `su(n)`.

operators.name: sub
operators.doc:
`sub(a, b)`: the difference `a - b`.

The engine's normal form has no subtraction node: this request is rewritten to `add(a, mul(-1, b))` and prints as `a - b`.

operators.name: sum
operators.doc: `sum(expr, k, lo, hi)` or `sum(tensor, [axis])`: symbolic/numeric summation over bound index `k` from `lo` to `hi`, or tensor reduction along `axis`.

operators.name: sum_dist
operators.doc: `sum_dist(d1, d2)`: distribution of the sum `X + Y` of independent random variables `X ~ d1` and `Y ~ d2`.

operators.name: surface_integral
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
operators.doc: `surface_integral(f, r, u, v, u0, u1, v0, v1)`: scalar surface integral `int_{v0}^{v1} int_{u0}^{u1} f(r(u, v)) ||r_u x r_v|| du dv`.

operators.name: svd
signatures: (Tensor<2, Int>) -> { _0: Tensor<2, Float>, _1: Tensor<1, Float>, _2: Tensor<2, Float> }
operators.doc:
`svd(A)`: singular value decomposition `list(U, S, V)` of matrix `A`.

Thin singular-value decomposition using the bidiagonal SVD backend.

Rank-deficient matrices retain orthonormal null-space columns. No Gram
matrix is formed, so small singular values do not lose accuracy through
squaring the condition number.

# Errors
Returns [`DenseError::Shape`] for inconsistent storage or non-finite input,
and [`DenseError::NoConvergence`] if the backend does not converge.

operators.name: sym
operators.doc: A symbol leaf.

operators.name: symmetric_group
operators.doc: Constructs the symmetric group `S_n` (`n <= 6`) of permutations in lexicographic order.

operators.name: syt_count
operators.doc: `syt_count(shape)`: number of standard Young tableaux of `shape` via the hook-length formula.

operators.name: t_test
operators.doc: `t_test(sample, mu)`: one-sample Student's t-test returning `list(statistic, p_value)` for `sample` against population mean `mu`.

operators.name: tan
operators.doc:
`tan(x)`: tangent `sin(x) / cos(x)` of angle `x` in radians.

`tan(x)` as a ball.

# Errors
Fails where the cosine interval contains zero, or for an argument beyond
`2^20` in magnitude.

operators.name: tanh
operators.doc:
`tanh(x)`: hyperbolic tangent `sinh(x) / cosh(x)`.

`tanh(x)` as a ball.

# Errors
Fails when an exponent leaves the representable range.

operators.name: tautology
operators.doc: `tautology(formula)`: decides whether propositional `formula` holds under all variable assignments (`true` or `false`).

operators.name: taylor
operators.doc: `taylor(f, x, a, n)`: Taylor polynomial of `f` about `x = a` up to degree `n`.

operators.name: tensor_add
operators.doc: `tensor_add(A, B)`: componentwise sum `A + B` of tensors of the same shape.

operators.name: tensor_contract
operators.doc: `tensor_contract(t, i, j)`: self-contraction (generalized trace) of tensor `t` over axes `i` and `j`.

operators.name: tensor_decomposition
signatures: (Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Int>) -> Tensor<1, { _0: Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, _1: Dyn<term> }>
operators.doc: `tensor_decomposition(T, hw1, hw2)`: irreducible decomposition `list(list(hw, m), ...)` of `V(hw1) (x) V(hw2)` for type `T`.

operators.name: tensor_inner
